name: 17-alpha-Estradiol
description: The non-feminising estradiol stereoisomer; extended lifespan in male mice only.

name: 5-Amino-1MQ
description: A small-molecule NNMT inhibitor studied for raising cellular NAD and reducing adipocyte lipid storage. Rodent data only; sold as a supplement well ahead of any human evidence.

name: 7-Keto-DHEA
description: DHEA metabolite that does not convert to testosterone or oestrogen -- which is the entire point of it.

name: 8-Mercapto-Octanoic Acid Phenylamide
description: 8-Mercapto-Octanoic Acid Phenylamide is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC3. ChEMBL records IC50 110.0 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: 9-Me-BC (9-Methyl-β-carboline)
description: Research beta-carboline with dopaminergic-neuron claims from laboratory models and no established human safety dataset.

name: A-485
description: The first potent selective catalytic inhibitor of p300/CBP acetyltransferase activity, and the tool that established acetylation writers as druggable rather than only their readers and erasers.

name: Abacavir
description: Inhibits HIV reverse transcriptase and is used only as part of a resistance-aware antiretroviral regimen.

name: Abaloparatide
description: PTHrP-analog bone-building drug used for severe osteoporosis.

name: Abarelix
description: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1252).

name: Abatacept
description: CTLA-4-Ig fusion protein that blocks T-cell costimulation, used in rheumatoid arthritis and psoriatic arthritis.

name: Abciximab
description: The first GPIIb/IIIa blocker, a chimeric antibody fragment with an extremely long receptor residence time; now withdrawn from most markets.

name: Abexinostat
description: An oral hydroxamate pan-HDAC inhibitor studied in follicular lymphoma and renal cell carcinoma, dosed on an intermittent schedule specifically to manage the thrombocytopenia that limits the class.

name: Abiraterone (Zytiga)
description: CYP17 inhibitor that blocks androgen biosynthesis at its source (testes, adrenals, and prostate tumor tissue itself), used for advanced prostate cancer.

name: Abp-700
description: Abp-700 is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is gABA-A receptor; anion channel agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Abrocitinib (Cibinqo)
description: Oral JAK1 inhibitor for refractory atopic dermatitis carrying JAK-class boxed warnings.

name: AC-262536
description: Preclinical nonsteroidal androgen-receptor modulator with no approved use or human efficacy/safety dataset.

name: Acalabrutinib
description: Inhibits BTK to interrupt B-cell receptor signalling; covalent and reversible agents differ in kinase selectivity, bleeding and atrial-fibrillation risk; second-generation covalent.

name: Acamprosate
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201293).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive modulator

name: Acarbose
description: Alpha-glucosidase inhibitor that slows carbohydrate digestion in the gut, blunting post-meal blood sugar spikes; older and less potent than newer glucose-lowering drug classes but still real and well-studied.

name: ACE-031
description: Soluble activin type IIB receptor decoy developed to increase muscle mass; development stopped after vascular adverse events.

name: ACE-083
description: Locally injected follistatin-based ligand trap that increased muscle volume but failed to deliver sufficient functional improvement.

name: ACE-031 (Ramatercept)
description: Soluble ActRIIB-Fc decoy receptor that soaks up myostatin and related ligands. Clinical development was halted over vascular adverse effects — epistaxis and telangiectasia — not for lack of efficacy. Circulates on the black market.

name: Aceclofenac
description: Diclofenac analogue with better gastric tolerability.

name: Acemetacin
description: Cyclooxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL189171).

name: Acenocoumarol
description: Inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase so clotting factors are undercarboxylated; effect is delayed, diet-sensitive and needs INR monitoring; shorter half-life than warfarin.

name: Acetaminophen
description: Cyclooxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL112).

name: Acetazolamide
description: Inhibits carbonic anhydrase, lowering bicarbonate-dependent fluid secretion; metabolic acidosis and paraesthesia are the usual class effects.

name: Acetohexamide
description: Closes pancreatic beta-cell KATP channels to stimulate insulin release, with hypoglycemia as the central class risk.

name: Acipimox
description: Nicotinic-acid analogue and anti-lipolytic drug used for hypertriglyceridaemia in some countries. Controlled human studies show lower free fatty acids and triglycerides; flushing and metabolic tradeoffs still matter.

name: Acitretin (oral, Soriatane)
description: Oral monoaromatic retinoid for severe psoriasis; the active metabolite of etretinate, with the same teratogenic ceiling.

name: Acolbifene
description: Acolbifene is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is estrogen receptor modulator; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Acotiamide
description: Acotiamide is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is acetylcholinesterase inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: ACP-105
description: Non-steroidal SARM from a discontinued CNS/bone programme; never past early-stage research.

name: Acrivastine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1224).

name: Aciclovir
description: The drug that made herpes treatable, and the classic example of selective activation: it is only phosphorylated in virus-infected cells.

name: Acyline
description: Acyline is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Adalimumab
description: Neutralizes TNF or its receptor signaling to suppress systemic inflammation, increasing susceptibility to selected infections.

name: Adapalene (Differin)
description: Third-generation topical retinoid, receptor-selective for RAR, a first-line OTC acne treatment.

name: Adefovir
description: Nucleotide analogue for hepatitis B, dose-limited by nephrotoxicity and now largely superseded by tenofovir.

name: Adenosine (IV)
description: Endogenous nucleoside given as a rapid intravenous bolus to terminate AV-nodal reentrant tachycardia, with a half-life of under ten seconds.

name: Adipiplon
description: Adipiplon is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is gABA-A receptor; anion channel partial agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Adipotide (FTPP)
description: Experimental peptide that targets the blood supply of fat tissue to induce localized fat loss.

name: ADMA (Asymmetric Dimethylarginine)
description: Endogenous competitive NOS inhibitor produced by protein methylation and cleared by DDAH. Not a drug — it is a cardiovascular risk biomarker, and it is in the catalog so the graph can express endogenous NOS inhibition.

name: Adomeglivant
description: Adomeglivant is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is glucagon receptor antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: ADS-100380
description: ADS-100380 is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC1. ChEMBL records IC50 750.0 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: ADS-102550
description: ADS-102550 is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC1. ChEMBL records IC50 29.0 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: Aducanumab (Aduhelm)
description: The first anti-amyloid antibody approved, on a surrogate endpoint after two trials that disagreed. Withdrawn in 2024. Its history is the reason plaque clearance alone is no longer accepted as sufficient evidence.

name: Aescin
description: Horse-chestnut triterpene mixture studied for edema and venous tone; renal and bleeding cautions apply.

name: Afamelanotide (Melanotan I)
description: Approved alpha-MSH analog that stimulates melanin production, distinct from the unapproved Melanotan II.

name: Afatinib
description: Inhibits oncogenic EGFR-family signaling; activity depends on tumor genotype and acquired resistance.

name: Afelimomab
description: Neutralizes TNF or its receptor signaling to suppress systemic inflammation, increasing susceptibility to selected infections.

name: Aficamten
description: A next-generation cardiac myosin inhibitor for obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, with a shorter half-life than mavacamten and no CYP2C19 genotype dependence.

name: Afoxolaner
description: Afoxolaner is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is ectoparasiticide for systemic use; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Aged Garlic Extract
description: Standardized aged garlic preparation studied for modest vascular effects; may add to antiplatelet therapy.

name: Agmatine
description: Decarboxylated arginine acting as an NMDA channel blocker and imidazoline ligand. Mostly preclinical, with essentially no controlled human cognitive data.

name: Agomelatine (Valdoxan)
description: Melatonin-receptor agonist and 5-HT2C antagonist antidepressant used outside the US; liver monitoring is required.

name: AICAR
description: AMPK activator that produced 'exercise in a pill' headlines in mice; injectable only and poorly absorbed.

name: Ajmaline
description: Modulates fast cardiac sodium channels to alter impulse conduction; proarrhythmia makes clinical supervision essential.

name: Alaproclate
description: Inhibits serotonin reuptake through SERT; benefits, activation, sexual effects, and withdrawal profiles differ by agent.

name: Albendazole
description: Benzimidazole with the broadest anthelmintic spectrum, and the drug of choice for neurocysticercosis and hydatid disease.

name: Albiglutide (Tanzeum)
description: Once-weekly GLP-1 approved and then withdrawn for commercial reasons, not safety.

name: Albuterol
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL714).

name: Alcaftadine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201747).

name: Alclofenac
description: Cyclooxygenase-1 inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL94081).

name: Alclometasone Dipropionate
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200989).

name: Aldesleukin
description: Recombinant IL-2; high-dose for melanoma and renal cancer, low-dose to expand regulatory T cells.

name: Aleglitazar
description: Aleglitazar is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Alemtuzumab
description: Anti-CD52 antibody producing profound, prolonged lymphocyte depletion, highly effective in multiple sclerosis and followed by a high rate of secondary autoimmunity.

name: Alendronate (Fosamax)
description: First-generation nitrogen-containing bisphosphonate that inhibits osteoclast-mediated bone resorption, the original standard-of-care osteoporosis drug.

name: Alfacalcidol (1-alpha-hydroxyvitamin D3)
description: Vitamin D analogue needing only hepatic hydroxylation to become calcitriol; standard in Japan and Europe.

name: Alfatradiol (17α-Estradiol)
description: Topical stereoisomer of estradiol used for androgenetic alopecia in some countries, with much weaker estrogen-receptor activity than 17β-estradiol.

name: Alfentanil
description: Short-acting fentanyl analogue with a low pKa, so a large fraction is unionised and it reaches the brain faster than fentanyl despite lower lipophilicity.

name: Alfuzosin
description: Blocks alpha-1 adrenoceptors to relax vascular or prostatic smooth muscle; first-dose hypotension and floppy-iris syndrome are class effects.

name: Algal DHA
description: Algae-derived docosahexaenoic acid providing a non-fish omega-3 source; DHA can raise LDL in some settings.

name: Alirocumab (Praluent)
description: PCSK9 monoclonal antibody, the other half of the class alongside evolocumab.

name: Aliskiren (Tekturna)
description: The only direct renin inhibitor ever marketed; blocks the renin-angiotensin cascade at its first step.

name: Alitretinoin
description: Retinoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL705).

name: Alitretinoin (oral, Toctino)
description: Oral 9-cis retinoic acid licensed for severe chronic hand eczema; the systemic drug, not the Kaposi sarcoma gel.

name: Allopurinol
description: Xanthine oxidase inhibitor for gout; also a major interaction hazard with azathioprine.

name: Almorexant
description: Almorexant is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is orexin receptor antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Almotriptan
description: Triptan with a tolerability profile close to placebo in trials, licensed for adolescents in several countries.

name: Alogliptin
description: Inhibits DPP-4 to prolong endogenous incretin signaling and glucose-dependent insulin release.

name: Alosetron
description: Antagonises 5-HT3 receptors on vagal afferents and in the area postrema; QT effects vary by agent; restricted prescribing for IBS-D.

name: Aloxiprin
description: Aloxiprin is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is cyclooxygenase inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Alpha-GPC (Choline Alfoscerate)
description: A choline-donating phospholipid that crosses the blood-brain barrier and feeds acetylcholine synthesis. The clinical evidence sits in adult-onset cognitive impairment, not in healthy enhancement.

name: Alpha-Ketoglutarate
description: Metabolic intermediate supplement studied for extending healthy lifespan in animal models.

name: Alpha-Linolenic Acid (ALA)
description: Essential plant omega-3 fatty acid with limited conversion to longer-chain EPA and DHA.

name: Alpha-Lipoic Acid (ALA)
description: Antioxidant compound studied for improving insulin sensitivity in type 2 diabetes; also marketed as a general metabolic-health supplement.

name: Alpha-Yohimbine (Rauwolscine)
description: Alpha-2 adrenergic antagonist related to yohimbine, sold as a stimulant fat-loss ingredient with sparse human evidence and meaningful cardiovascular/anxiety risk.

name: Alprazolam
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL661).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Alprostadil
description: PGE1 used intracavernosally for erectile dysfunction and to maintain ductal patency in neonates.

name: Alteplase
description: Recombinant tPA for stroke, pulmonary embolism and myocardial infarction, within tight time windows.

name: Amantadine
description: Aminoadamantane with weak NMDA antagonist and dopamine-releasing activity; originally an influenza A antiviral, now an antiparkinsonian.

name: Ambenonium
description: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1652).

name: Ambrisentan
description: Endothelin receptor, ET-A/ET-B antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1111).

name: Amcinonide
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200732).

name: Amflutizole
description: Inhibits xanthine oxidoreductase to reduce urate production at its terminal synthetic step; investigational, development discontinued.

name: Amifampridine (3,4-Diaminopyridine)
description: Presynaptic voltage-gated potassium channel blocker; the approved symptomatic treatment for Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome.

name: Amikacin
description: Aminoglycoside resistant to most aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes, which makes it the reserve agent of the class and part of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis regimens.

name: Amiloride
description: Potassium-sparing epithelial sodium channel blocker; the non-hormonal alternative to spironolactone.

name: Amineptine
description: Inhibits norepinephrine reuptake, often alongside serotonin effects; blood pressure and discontinuation effects require attention.

name: 5-Amino-1MQ
description: NNMT inhibitor with promising mouse adipose data and nothing at all in humans.

name: Aminocaproic Acid
description: Lysine analogue antifibrinolytic blocking plasminogen binding to fibrin.

name: Aminoglutethimide
description: The original aromatase inhibitor -- and a demonstration of why non-selectivity was a problem.

name: Aminophylline
description: Inhibits PDE5 so nitric-oxide/cGMP vasodilation persists in corporal and pulmonary vascular smooth muscle; non-selective PDE inhibitor and adenosine antagonist.

name: Aminosalicylic Acid
description: Dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1169).

name: Amiodarone
description: Alters cardiac repolarization through potassium-channel effects; QT prolongation and torsades risk vary by agent.

name: Amisulpride
description: Dopamine receptors; D2 & D3 antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL243712).

name: Amitriptyline
description: Serotonin transporter inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL629).

name: Amlitelimab
description: Amlitelimab is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 4 inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.
mechanism: tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 4 inhibitor

name: Amlodipine
description: Dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker and ALLHAT first-line arm; ankle oedema is the dose-limiting complaint.

name: Amorolfine
description: Disrupts fungal ergosterol synthesis or membrane function; interaction and organ-toxicity profiles differ substantially.

name: Amoxapine
description: Serotonin transporter inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1113).

name: Amoxicillin
description: Aminopenicillin with useful oral bioavailability and gram-positive plus limited gram-negative cover. First-line for otitis, sinusitis and community pneumonia, and the backbone of Helicobacter eradication regimens.

name: Amphetamine
description: Reverses the dopamine transporter into efflux rather than merely blocking reuptake, which is why it releases transmitter instead of only preserving it. Meta-analysis in healthy non-sleep-deprived adults found no cognitive enhancement.

name: Amphotericin B
description: Disrupts fungal ergosterol synthesis or membrane function; interaction and organ-toxicity profiles differ substantially.

name: Ampicillin
description: The parenteral aminopenicillin, retaining unique activity against Listeria and Enterococcus faecalis. Poor oral absorption is why amoxicillin displaced it outside hospital.

name: Ampreloxetine
description: Ampreloxetine is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is norepinephrine transporter inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Amycretin
description: Single molecule acting at both the GLP-1 and amylin receptors; early-phase.

name: Anacardic acid
description: A salicylic acid derivative from cashew nut shell liquid and the first reported HAT inhibitor. Its non-specificity is a standing caution about natural-product epigenetic claims.

name: Anacetrapib
description: CETP inhibitor that won its outcomes trial and was still never filed, partly because it accumulates in adipose tissue.

name: Anagliptin
description: Inhibits DPP-4 to prolong endogenous incretin signaling and glucose-dependent insulin release.

name: Anagrelide
description: PDE3 inhibitor used to lower platelet counts in essential thrombocythemia. Its platelet-lowering action is a megakaryocyte effect, separate from the cAMP-mediated antiplatelet one.

name: Anakinra
description: Recombinant IL-1 receptor antagonist with a very short half-life, requiring daily injection.

name: Anamorelin
description: Oral ghrelin agonist approved in Japan for cancer cachexia; rejected in Europe.

name: Arimidex (Anastrozole)
description: Non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor used to control estrogen-related side effects during anabolic steroid use.

name: Andarine (S4)
description: SARM studied for lean mass, known for a dose-dependent yellow-tinted vision side effect.

name: Andexanet Alfa
description: Recombinant decoy factor Xa that reverses apixaban and rivaroxaban by binding them, with a rebound once the infusion ends.

name: 4-Androstenediol
description: Testosterone precursor one enzymatic step further out than androstenedione.

name: Androstenedione
description: Direct testosterone precursor once sold as a bodybuilding supplement ('andro'), banned in most sports after evidence it does raise testosterone.

name: Anfibatide
description: Anfibatide is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is platelet glycoprotein Ib alpha chain antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.
mechanism: platelet glycoprotein Ib alpha chain antagonist

name: Angiotensin Ii
description: Type-1 angiotensin II receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL408403).

name: Anidulafungin
description: Echinocandin cleared by spontaneous chemical degradation rather than by any enzyme, so no dose adjustment is needed in hepatic or renal failure.

name: Anifrolumab
description: Anti-type-I-interferon-receptor antibody for systemic lupus, targeting the interferon signature that dominates lupus transcriptomics.

name: Aniracetam
description: Fat-soluble racetam and a genuine positive allosteric modulator of the AMPA receptor in vitro. Human evidence is thin and mostly predates modern trial standards.

name: Antazoline
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1305).

name: Antithrombin Alfa
description: Coagulation factor X inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201554).

name: Anti-thymocyte Globulin
description: Polyclonal antibody preparation raised in rabbits or horses, used for induction immunosuppression and for aplastic anaemia.

name: AOD-9604
description: Modified fragment of the C-terminus of human growth hormone, engineered to retain GH's fat-mobilizing effect without its growth-promoting activity.

name: Apalutamide (Erleada)
description: Second-generation androgen receptor antagonist; blocks nuclear translocation as well as binding.

name: Apararenone
description: Blocks mineralocorticoid-receptor signalling to reduce sodium retention and fibrotic remodelling; hyperkalaemia is the defining class risk; investigational.

name: Apc-100
description: Apc-100 is a phase 1 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is androgen Receptor antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Apicidin
description: A cyclic tetrapeptide HDAC inhibitor discovered as an antiprotozoal against Apicomplexa, and one of the first demonstrations that parasite HDACs are a drug target in their own right.

name: Apigenin
description: Chamomile flavonoid taken as a CD38 inhibitor to spare NAD+; human evidence is thin.

name: Apitegromab
description: Investigational antibody that selectively blocks activation of latent myostatin for spinal muscular atrophy.

name: Apixaban (Eliquis)
description: Direct factor Xa inhibitor used for atrial fibrillation and venous thromboembolism; interactions and additive bleeding make casual stack use hazardous.

name: Apomorphine
description: D2-like dopamine receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL53).

name: Apremilast
description: Inhibits PDE4 to raise intracellular cAMP and dampen inflammatory cytokine production; emesis and weight loss are class-limiting.

name: Aprepitant
description: Neurokinin-1 antagonist that controls delayed chemotherapy-induced nausea, which the 5-HT3 antagonists do not reach.

name: Aprocitentan
description: Endothelin receptor, ET-A/ET-B antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2165326).

name: ARA-290 (Cibinetide)
description: Eleven-amino-acid peptide from the EPO helix B domain. Engineered specifically to hit the innate repair receptor WITHOUT the erythropoietic effect — it does not raise haematocrit, which is the entire point of the molecule.

name: Arbutin
description: Natural hydroquinone glycoside found in bearberry and other plants; competitively inhibits tyrosinase, giving hydroquinone-like skin-lightening effects with a gentler safety profile.

name: Arformoterol
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1363).

name: Argatroban
description: Intravenous direct thrombin inhibitor used especially in heparin-induced thrombocytopenia.

name: L-Arginine
description: Amino acid marketed as a post-workout growth hormone booster; a controlled trial found the opposite -- combined with resistance exercise, oral arginine actually blunted the natural exercise-induced GH pulse rather than enhancing it.

name: Argireline (Acetyl Hexapeptide-8)
description: Topical peptide marketed as a needle-free alternative to Botox, studied for reducing facial expression wrinkles by inhibiting neurotransmitter release at the neuromuscular junction.

name: Arimistane (Androstatrienedione)
description: DHEA metabolite sold as an over-the-counter aromatase inhibitor; no human trial data at all.

name: Aripiprazole
description: Dopamine D2 partial agonist, the first of the third-generation antipsychotics, acting as a functional stabiliser rather than a blocker.

name: Armodafinil (Nuvigil)
description: The longer-lived R-enantiomer of modafinil, with the same dopamine transporter mechanism and a flatter plasma curve. Differences from modafinil are pharmacokinetic rather than pharmacodynamic.

name: Artemether
description: Artemisinin derivative and, with lumefantrine, the backbone of first-line malaria treatment across most of the world.

name: Articaine
description: Dental local anaesthetic with a thiophene ring for tissue penetration and an ester side chain giving rapid plasma clearance.

name: Artichoke Leaf Extract
description: Botanical extract studied for modest lipid and digestive effects; formulation and cynarin content vary.

name: Asciminib
description: Inhibits BCR–ABL-family kinase signaling; mutation coverage and off-target cardiovascular risks differ by agent.

name: Asenapine
description: Sublingual atypical antipsychotic with an exceptionally broad receptor profile, given sublingually because oral bioavailability is under two percent.

name: Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera)
description: Ayurvedic adaptogen herb; an RCT in resistance-trained men found it raised serum testosterone alongside strength and muscle mass gains versus placebo.

name: Asoprisnil
description: Asoprisnil is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is progesterone receptor modulator; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Aspirin
description: Irreversible platelet COX-1 inhibitor used for secondary cardiovascular prevention; bleeding risk usually outweighs benefit for unsupervised primary prevention.

name: Astaxanthin
description: Potent carotenoid antioxidant studied for protecting skin against UV-driven photoaging.

name: Astemizole
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL296419).

name: Asunercept
description: Asunercept is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 6 binding agent; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.
mechanism: tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 6 binding agent

name: Atacicept
description: Atacicept is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 13B inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.
mechanism: tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 13B inhibitor

name: Ataciguat (HMR1766)
description: sGC activator targeting oxidised enzyme. Notable for a 2025 randomized trial testing whether reactivating oxidised sGC slows calcific aortic valve disease — an unusual indication for this class.

name: Atazanavir
description: HIV protease inhibitor with a relatively lipid-friendly profile, distinguished by the benign unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia it causes.

name: Atenolol (Tenormin)
description: Water-soluble beta blocker that barely enters the brain; the standard comparator in older trials.

name: Atezolizumab
description: Anti-PD-L1 antibody, blocking the ligand rather than the receptor and leaving PD-L2 signalling intact.

name: Atogepant
description: Blocks CGRP ligand or receptor signalling in the trigeminovascular system for migraine prevention or acute treatment; oral small-molecule gepant.

name: Atomoxetine (Strattera)
description: Selective noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor for ADHD. Non-stimulant and non-scheduled, with a slow onset over weeks rather than hours -- a genuinely different clinical shape from the stimulants.

name: Atorvastatin (Lipitor)
description: Widely used statin (HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor) for LDL cholesterol reduction -- relevant to steroid users given AAS-associated dyslipidemia risk.

name: Atosiban
description: Acts at the oxytocin receptor to drive uterine contraction and milk ejection, or blocks it to suppress preterm labour; receptor antagonist, tocolytic.

name: Atovaquone
description: Hydroxynaphthoquinone targeting the parasite mitochondrial electron transport chain, used for malaria, Pneumocystis and toxoplasmosis.

name: Atracurium
description: Benzylisoquinolinium relaxant eliminated by spontaneous Hofmann degradation, so it is independent of liver and kidney entirely.

name: Atrasentan
description: A selective endothelin A receptor antagonist developed for proteinuric kidney disease. Sparing the ETB receptor is what limits the fluid retention that ended earlier non-selective attempts.

name: Atropine
description: The reference antimuscarinic, used for bradycardia, as an antisialagogue and as the antidote to organophosphate poisoning.

name: Avacincaptad Pegol
description: Inhibits a step of the complement cascade; blocking terminal complement raises encapsulated-organism risk and requires meningococcal vaccination; C5 aptamer, intravitreal.

name: Avacopan
description: Oral C5a receptor antagonist that allows glucocorticoid sparing in ANCA-associated vasculitis, a rare example of replacing steroids rather than adding to them.

name: Avanafil (Stendra)
description: Fastest-onset PDE5 inhibitor, designed for higher selectivity against the off-target enzymes.

name: Avelumab
description: Anti-PD-L1 antibody retaining a wild-type Fc, so it can also mediate antibody-dependent killing of PD-L1-positive tumour cells.

name: Avibactam
description: Non-beta-lactam diazabicyclooctane inhibitor with a reversible covalent mechanism, extending ceftazidime to KPC and OXA-48 producers.

name: Avobenzone
description: The main organic UVA filter in sunscreens, and photounstable unless formulated with a stabiliser.

name: Axitinib
description: Inhibits VEGF-receptor angiogenic signaling; hypertension, bleeding, thrombosis, and wound-healing effects require monitoring.

name: Azacitidine
description: Hypomethylating agent incorporated into RNA and DNA, depleting DNMT1; standard in myelodysplastic syndrome.

name: Azasetron
description: Antagonises 5-HT3 receptors on vagal afferents and in the area postrema; QT effects vary by agent; approved in Japan.

name: Azatadine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL946).

name: Azathioprine
description: Thiopurine prodrug used in inflammatory bowel disease, autoimmune hepatitis and transplantation, and the reason TPMT genotyping exists.

name: Azd-5423

name: Azelaic Acid
description: Naturally occurring dicarboxylic acid that reversibly inhibits tyrosinase, used topically for melasma/hyperpigmentation and acne; a large head-to-head trial found it comparably effective to hydroquinone.

name: Azelastine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL639).

name: Azilsartan medoxomil (Edarbi)
description: The most recently approved angiotensin receptor blocker, with unusually slow dissociation from the AT1 receptor.

name: Azilsartan Medoxomil
description: Type-1 angiotensin II receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2028661).

name: Azimilide
description: Alters cardiac repolarization through potassium-channel effects; QT prolongation and torsades risk vary by agent.

name: Azithromycin
description: Inhibits bacterial protein synthesis at the ribosome; spectrum, resistance, and toxicity are agent-specific.

name: Aztreonam
description: Monobactam active only against aerobic gram-negative organisms, with essentially no cross-reactivity to penicillin allergy, which is its main clinical niche.

name: Azumamide C
description: Azumamide C is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC11. ChEMBL records Ki 35.0 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: Azumamide E
description: Azumamide E is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC2. ChEMBL records Ki 50.0 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: Bacitracin
description: Topical polypeptide antibiotic, systemically nephrotoxic and therefore never given by injection.

name: Baclofen
description: GABA-B agonist for spasticity; abrupt withdrawal from intrathecal delivery is life-threatening.

name: Bacopa Monnieri
description: Ayurvedic herb with the largest trial base of any herbal nootropic, and results that are far less consistent than its reputation. Effects take weeks and are strongest on delayed recall.

name: Bafetinib
description: Inhibits BCR–ABL-family kinase signaling; mutation coverage and off-target cardiovascular risks differ by agent.

name: Bakuchiol
description: Plant-derived retinol alternative studied for anti-aging effects with less irritation.

name: Balaglitazone

name: Balcinrenone

name: Baloxavir Marboxil
description: Single-dose influenza antiviral with a mechanism upstream of neuraminidase, blocking transcription rather than release.

name: Balsalazide
description: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201346).

name: BAM15
description: Mitochondrial protonophore ('uncoupler') studied in animals for reversing diet-induced obesity without the hyperthermia risk of older uncouplers like DNP.

name: Bambuterol
description: Bambuterol is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

mechanism: beta-2 adrenergic receptor mRNA RNAi inhibitor

name: Bardoxolone Methyl
description: Bardoxolone Methyl is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Baricitinib (oral, Olumiant)
description: Oral JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor, the first systemic drug approved anywhere for severe alopecia areata.

name: Barusiban
description: Acts at the oxytocin receptor to drive uterine contraction and milk ejection, or blocks it to suppress preterm labour; investigational antagonist.

name: Basiliximab
description: Anti-CD25 antibody for transplant induction, blocking the high-affinity IL-2 receptor on recently activated T cells only.

name: BAY 60-7550
description: Selective PDE2 inhibitor. A research tool, never developed clinically — treat any consumer-facing claim about it as unsupported.

name: Bazedoxifene
description: Third-generation SERM, sold paired with conjugated oestrogens to block their endometrial effect.

name: Beclomethasone Dipropionate
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200500).

name: Bedaquiline
description: Diarylquinoline that opened a genuinely new target in tuberculosis after forty years, inhibiting the mycobacterial ATP synthase.

name: Beetroot Extract
description: Dietary nitrate source that can increase nitric-oxide signaling and lower blood pressure modestly.

name: Belantamab Mafodotin
description: Tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 17 binding agent; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL4298209).
mechanism: Tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 17 binding agent

name: Belatacept
description: Higher-affinity CTLA-4-Ig developed for kidney transplantation as a calcineurin-free maintenance regimen preserving renal function.

name: Belimumab
description: Tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 13B inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1789843).
mechanism: Tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 13B inhibitor

name: Belinostat
description: Intravenous pan-HDAC inhibitor for peripheral T-cell lymphoma.

name: Bempedoic acid
description: ATP citrate lyase inhibitor that lowers LDL without acting in muscle -- the reason it exists is statin intolerance.

name: Benazepril (Lotensin)
description: Long-acting ACE inhibitor prodrug, best known as the backbone of the ACCOMPLISH combination trial.

name: Benperidol
description: Dopamine D2 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL297302).

name: Benralizumab
description: Anti-IL-5-receptor antibody that depletes eosinophils outright rather than starving them, through enhanced antibody-dependent killing.

name: Benserazide
description: The peripheral decarboxylase inhibitor used with levodopa outside North America, pharmacologically interchangeable with carbidopa at the doses used in co-formulation.

name: Benzbromarone
description: Blocks proximal-tubule urate reabsorption to raise fractional urate excretion; urine volume and stone risk need attention; restricted in some countries over hepatotoxicity.

name: Benzgalantamine
description: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL5095056).

name: Benznidazole
description: First-line nitroimidazole for Chagas disease, effective in acute infection and of limited benefit once cardiomyopathy is established.

name: Benzocaine
description: Over-the-counter topical ester anaesthetic, and the commonest drug cause of acquired methaemoglobinaemia.

name: Benzolamide
description: Inhibits carbonic anhydrase, lowering bicarbonate-dependent fluid secretion; metabolic acidosis and paraesthesia are the usual class effects; research tool compound.

name: Benzoyl Peroxide (topical)
description: Oxidising topical antimicrobial for acne that generates free radicals in the follicle and selects no resistance.

name: Benzphetamine
description: Norepinephrine transporter releasing agent; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL3545985).

name: Benzydamine
description: Cyclooxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL12610).

name: Bepotastine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201758).

name: Bepridil
description: Withdrawn calcium channel blocker with additional sodium and potassium channel activity, remembered for torsades de pointes.

name: Beraprost
description: Orally active prostacyclin analogue used in Japan and South Korea.

name: Berberine
description: Plant alkaloid studied as an AMPK activator ('nature's Ozempic' in popular framing), most robustly evidenced for improving glucose/lipid metabolism in fatty liver disease models.

name: Berdazimer
description: Topical nitric oxide releasing gel for molluscum contagiosum, the first drug approved for that infection.

name: Bergamot Extract
description: Citrus bergamot polyphenol extract studied for lipid lowering; supplement assays and trial quality vary.

name: Besifloxacin
description: Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase or topoisomerase IV; tendon, neurologic, cardiac, and resistance risks limit indiscriminate use.

name: Beta-Alanine
description: Buffers muscle acidity during high-intensity exercise, extending time to fatigue in resistance and sprint training.

name: Betahistine
description: Histamine H3 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL24441).

name: Betaine Anhydrous (TMG)
description: Methyl donor that can lower homocysteine and modestly affect performance, while sometimes raising LDL.

name: Betaine (TMG)
description: Methyl donor approved as a drug for homocystinuria and sold everywhere as a supplement.

name: Betamethasone Acetate
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200538).

name: Betamethasone Benzoate
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200376).

name: Betamethasone
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL632).

name: Betamethasone Dipropionate
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200384).

name: Betamethasone Phosphoric Acid
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201207).

name: Betamethasone Valerate
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1497).

name: Betaxolol

name: Bethanidine
description: Norepinephrine transporter substrate; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201260).

name: Betrixaban

name: Bexagliflozin

name: Bicalutamide (Casodex)
description: Nonsteroidal antiandrogen that competitively blocks testosterone and DHT at the androgen receptor, used in prostate cancer and sometimes for anti-androgen effect.

name: Bicifadine
description: Inhibits norepinephrine reuptake, often alongside serotonin effects; blood pressure and discontinuation effects require attention.

name: Bictegravir
description: Inhibits HIV integrase strand transfer as a component of combination antiretroviral therapy.

name: Bifonazole
description: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL277535).

name: Biib-023

mechanism: tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 12 inhibitor

name: Bilastine
description: Histamine H1 receptor inverse agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1742423).

description: Antibody that blocks activin type II receptors to increase muscle mass while reducing fat mass.

name: Bimatoprost (Latisse)
description: The prostaglandin analogue actually approved for growing eyelashes.

name: Bimatoprost (topical, Latisse)
description: Prostamide analogue applied to the lash line for eyelash hypotrichosis, a glaucoma drug repurposed on its side effect.

name: Bimekizumab
description: Blocks IL-17 ligand or receptor signaling to reduce neutrophil-dominant inflammation.

name: Biotin
description: B-vitamin widely marketed for hair and nail growth despite thin evidence outside of documented deficiency.

name: Birabresib (OTX-015)
description: BET bromodomain inhibitor investigated in haematological malignancy.

name: Bisegliptin

description: Cyclooxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1120).

name: Bisthianostat

name: Bitolterol
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201295).

name: Bivalirudin
description: Short-acting intravenous direct thrombin inhibitor used during coronary intervention.

name: Blarcamesine

name: Bleselumab

name: BMS-564929
description: SARM designed for high tissue selectivity; reached Phase I and stopped.

name: Boceprevir
description: First-generation hepatitis C protease inhibitor, added to interferon and ribavirin in 2011 and obsolete within three years.

name: Bococizumab
description: Discontinued anti-PCSK9 antibody whose efficacy waned because antidrug antibodies developed.

name: Bolandiol (19-Nortestosterone-3β,17β-diol)
description: Nandrolone precursor, converted to 19-nortestosterone in vivo. Sold as a prohormone; behaves as a nandrolone-class androgen once converted.

name: Bolasterone
description: Potent oral anabolic steroid historically used in doping and later reformulated as a designer compound.

name: Equipoise (Boldenone)
description: Veterinary-derived injectable steroid with slow-acting, moderate anabolic effects and high hematocrit impact.

name: Boldione (Androstadienedione)
description: Prohormone that converts to boldenone; inherits Equipoise's problems without its pharmaceutical history.

name: Boron
description: Trace mineral supplement studied for lowering SHBG, which in turn raises the free (unbound, biologically active) fraction of circulating testosterone.

name: Bosentan
description: Endothelin receptor, ET-A/ET-B antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL957).

name: Bosutinib
description: Inhibits BCR–ABL-family kinase signaling; mutation coverage and off-target cardiovascular risks differ by agent.

name: Boswellia serrata
description: Boswellic-acid botanical extract studied for osteoarthritis symptoms and inflammation; extract standardization matters.

name: Botulinum toxin
description: Injectable neurotoxin used to relax the masseter for jawline slimming and to treat facial wrinkles.

name: BPC-157

name: BPC-157
description: Synthetic peptide fragment studied for tendon, ligament, and gut healing acceleration.

name: Brazikumab
description: Neutralizes IL-23 signaling to suppress pathogenic Th17 maintenance in immune-mediated disease.

name: Bremelanotide
description: Melanocortin receptor 4 agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2070241).

name: Brentuximab Vedotin
description: Tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 8 binding agent; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1742994).

name: Brepocitinib
description: Investigational TYK2/JAK1 inhibitor studied in inflammatory skin and autoimmune disorders; systemic immunosuppression and class safety issues remain relevant.

description: Alters cardiac repolarization through potassium-channel effects; QT prolongation and torsades risk vary by agent.

name: Brexanolone
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL207538).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Briakinumab
description: Neutralizes IL-23 signaling to suppress pathogenic Th17 maintenance in immune-mediated disease.

name: Brimonidine
description: Alpha-2 agonist used as a glaucoma drop and as a topical gel for rosacea erythema.

name: Brinzolamide
description: Inhibits carbonic anhydrase, lowering bicarbonate-dependent fluid secretion; metabolic acidosis and paraesthesia are the usual class effects; topical ophthalmic.

name: Brodalumab
description: Blocks IL-17 ligand or receptor signaling to reduce neutrophil-dominant inflammation.

name: Brofaromine

name: Bromantane
description: Russian actoprotector claimed to raise dopamine synthesis rather than release it. Human evidence is almost entirely from Russian-language trials that have not been replicated elsewhere.

name: Bromazepam
description: GABA receptor alpha-2 subunit positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL277062).
mechanism: GABA receptor alpha-2 subunit positive allosteric modulator

name: Bromelain
description: Pineapple-derived protease mixture marketed for swelling and recovery; evidence and enzyme potency vary by product.

name: Bromfenac
description: Cyclooxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1077).

name: Bromocriptine (Parlodel)
description: Older dopamine agonist used to suppress prolactin, shorter-acting and less well-tolerated than cabergoline for the same purpose.

name: Bromodiphenhydramine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201245).

name: Brompheniramine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL811).

name: Bucindolol
description: Bucindolol is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is beta-2 adrenergic receptor antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Bucladesine (Dibutyryl-cAMP)
description: Cell-permeable cAMP analogue that acts as cAMP itself rather than changing its production or breakdown. Approved in Japan as a topical agent; otherwise a laboratory tool.

name: Buclizine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201271).

name: Budesonide
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1370).

name: Bulevirtide (Hepcludex)
description: A myristoylated peptide that blocks the NTCP bile acid transporter hepatitis B and D use as their entry receptor. The first approved therapy specifically for hepatitis D.

name: Bumetanide
description: Potent loop diuretic used for fluid overload; can cause dehydration, hypokalemia, and renal stress.

name: Bupivacaine
description: Long-acting amide local anaesthetic and the classic cardiotoxin of the class, which is why the levo-enantiomer was developed.

name: Buprenorphine
description: High-affinity partial mu agonist with a ceiling on respiratory depression, the safety property that makes it a first-line maintenance treatment.

name: Bupropion (Wellbutrin)
description: Norepinephrine/dopamine reuptake inhibitor used for depression and smoking cessation and combined with naltrexone for obesity; can raise blood pressure and seizure risk.

name: Buserelin
description: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2110824).

name: Buspirone (Buspar)
description: Azapirone 5-HT1A partial agonist for generalised anxiety; non-sedating, non-addictive, and slow to take effect.

name: Buspirone
description: Azapirone anxiolytic acting through 5-HT1A partial agonism, with no sedation, no dependence and a two-week onset.

name: Butabarbital

name: Butalbital
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL454).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Butenafine
description: Disrupts fungal ergosterol synthesis or membrane function; interaction and organ-toxicity profiles differ substantially.

name: Butorphanol
description: Kappa agonist / partial mu agonist available as a nasal spray.

name: C646
description: A pyrazolone p300 HAT inhibitor found by virtual screening, widely used before A-485 despite modest potency and off-target activity.

name: Cabergoline (Dostinex)
description: Long-acting dopamine agonist that suppresses prolactin, commonly used off-label by AAS users to manage prolactin-related side effects from 19-nor compounds like nandrolone/trenbolone.

name: Cabotegravir
description: Inhibits HIV integrase strand transfer as a component of combination antiretroviral therapy.

name: Cabozantinib
description: Inhibits VEGF-receptor angiogenic signaling; hypertension, bleeding, thrombosis, and wound-healing effects require monitoring.

name: Caffeine
description: The most widely used psychoactive compound in the world. Blocks adenosine receptors rather than adding stimulation, so it masks accumulated sleep pressure without repaying it. Also studied topically on the scalp against androgen-driven follicle suppression.

name: Cagrilintide
description: Long-acting amylin receptor agonist studied for weight management, often paired with semaglutide.

name: Calcifediol Anhydrous
description: Vitamin D receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1040).

name: Calcifediol (25-hydroxyvitamin D3)
description: The circulating vitamin D prohormone itself, marketed as a repletion therapy that skips the liver step.

name: Calcipotriene
description: Vitamin D receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200666).

name: Calcipotriol (topical, Dovonex)
description: Topical vitamin D3 analogue for plaque psoriasis, with far less effect on calcium than calcitriol.

name: Calcitonin (salmon)
description: Peptide hormone that directly switches off osteoclasts; largely displaced by better antiresorptives.

name: Calcitriol (1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3)
description: The fully active vitamin D hormone; needs no renal activation, and has the narrowest safety margin.

name: Calusterone
description: 17-alkylated oral anabolic androgenic steroid, historically used in breast cancer treatment; largely obsolete today.

name: Canagliflozin Anhydrous
description: Sodium/glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2048484).

name: Canagliflozin (Invokana)
description: SGLT2 inhibitor studied in the large CANVAS Program, which found real cardiovascular and renal benefit beyond blood sugar control -- alongside empagliflozin and dapagliflozin, one of the three major drugs in this class.

name: Canakinumab (Ilaris)
description: Anti-interleukin-1-beta monoclonal antibody; the drug that first proved the inflammatory hypothesis of atherosclerosis.

name: Candesartan Cilexetil
description: Type-1 angiotensin II receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1014).

name: Candesartan (Atacand)
description: ARB with unusually tight receptor binding and a large heart failure trial programme.

name: Cangrelor
description: Inhibits platelet P2Y12 ADP signalling to reduce aggregation, at the cost of bleeding risk; intravenous, reversible.

name: Cannabidiol (Epidiolex)

name: Canrenoate

name: Canrenone
description: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1463345).

name: Capecitabine (Xeloda)
description: An oral prodrug converted to 5-fluorouracil in three enzymatic steps, the last by thymidine phosphorylase which is enriched in tumour tissue. That last step is the basis for its relative tumour selectivity.

name: Capreomycin
description: Injectable cyclic peptide for resistant tuberculosis, sharing the aminoglycoside toxicity profile without being an aminoglycoside.

name: Capromorelin
description: Oral ghrelin-receptor agonist approved in veterinary medicine for appetite stimulation; not approved for human use.

name: Capsaicin
description: TRPV1 agonist used topically for neuropathic pain and studied for thermogenesis; initial burning reflects target activation.

name: Capsazepine
description: Activates TRPV1 on nociceptive afferents, where sustained exposure defunctionalises the nerve terminal and produces lasting analgesia; antagonist, research tool.

name: Captopril (Capoten)
description: The first orally active ACE inhibitor, a sulfhydryl-containing short-acting agent that opened the whole drug class.

name: Carbamazepine
description: Reduces high-frequency neuronal firing through voltage-gated sodium-channel modulation.

name: Carbetocin
description: Acts at the oxytocin receptor to drive uterine contraction and milk ejection, or blocks it to suppress preterm labour; long-acting analogue.

name: Carbidopa
description: A peripheral AADC inhibitor that does not cross the blood-brain barrier. It has no therapeutic effect alone; it exists to stop levodopa being decarboxylated in the gut and bloodstream, roughly quadrupling the fraction reaching the brain.

name: Carbinoxamine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL864).

name: Carboprost
description: 15-methyl PGF2alpha used for postpartum haemorrhage refractory to oxytocin.

name: Cardarine (GW501516)
description: PPAR-delta agonist studied for endurance and fat oxidation; not a SARM despite common grouping.

name: Carglumic Acid
description: N-acetylglutamate analogue that activates carbamoyl-phosphate synthetase I in specific hyperammonemia disorders.

name: Cariprazine
description: Antagonizes or partially agonizes dopamine D2 receptors; movement, metabolic, and prolactin effects depend on receptor profile.

name: Carperitide
description: Recombinant human ANP, approved and used in Japan for acute heart failure. Same receptor as nesiritide, different peptide.

name: Carprofen
description: Cyclooxygenase-2 inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1316).

name: Cartalax (Ala-Glu-Asp)
description: Short peptide bioregulator marketed for cartilage support. Published evidence is limited to cell and tissue-culture work on the AED peptide; no established human efficacy or regulatory approval.

name: Carvedilol
description: Non-selective alpha/beta blocker with antioxidant activity and the strongest heart-failure evidence of the class.

name: Caspofungin
description: First echinocandin, fungicidal against Candida and fungistatic against Aspergillus, targeting a wall component humans do not have.

name: CB-03-01 (Clascoterone research formulation)
description: Research/development naming for clascoterone formulations; route and concentration matter, and evidence should not be transferred blindly from approved acne cream.
