name: Cefazolin
description: First-generation cephalosporin and the standard agent for surgical prophylaxis and for methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia, where it outperforms vancomycin.

name: Cefepime
description: Fourth-generation cephalosporin combining antipseudomonal and gram-positive activity, and a poor inducer of AmpC beta-lactamases.

name: Cefiderocol
description: Siderophore cephalosporin that hijacks bacterial iron transport to cross the outer membrane, reserved for carbapenem-resistant gram-negative infection.

name: Ceftaroline
description: The cephalosporin with meaningful MRSA activity, achieved by binding the altered PBP2a that confers methicillin resistance.

name: Ceftazidime
description: Third-generation cephalosporin with strong antipseudomonal activity but weak staphylococcal cover, a trade-off written into its side chain.

name: Ceftriaxone
description: Third-generation cephalosporin with a long half-life allowing once-daily dosing and good cerebrospinal fluid penetration, making it the empirical choice in bacterial meningitis.

name: Cefuroxime
description: Second-generation cephalosporin with improved stability to staphylococcal and some gram-negative beta-lactamases. Available orally as the axetil ester.

name: Celecoxib
description: Cyclooxygenase-2 inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL118).

name: Celiprolol
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor partial agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL27810).

name: Cemiplimab
description: Anti-PD-1 antibody first approved for advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, a tumour with a very high mutational burden.

name: Cenobamate
description: Reduces high-frequency neuronal firing through voltage-gated sodium-channel modulation.

name: Cephalexin
description: Oral first-generation cephalosporin used for skin and soft tissue infection and for uncomplicated urinary infection in pregnancy.

name: Ceramides
description: Lipid molecules naturally present in the skin barrier, used topically to restore barrier function.

name: Cerdulatinib
description: Cerdulatinib is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is tyrosine-protein kinase SYK inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Cerebrolysin
description: Peptide preparation derived from porcine brain tissue, studied as a neuroprotective/cognitive agent.

name: Cerivastatin
description: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1477).

name: Certolizumab Pegol
description: PEGylated anti-TNF Fab fragment with no Fc region, which is why it does not cross the placenta by active transport.

name: Certolizumab Pegol
description: Neutralizes TNF or its receptor signaling to suppress systemic inflammation, increasing susceptibility to selected infections.

name: Cetilistat
description: Cetilistat is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is pancreatic lipase inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Cetirizine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1000).

name: Cetrorelix (Cetrotide)
description: GnRH antagonist used in IVF to stop a premature LH surge; immediate suppression, no flare.

name: Chiglitazar
description: Chiglitazar is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Chloramphenicol
description: Inhibits bacterial protein synthesis at the ribosome; spectrum, resistance, and toxicity are agent-specific.

name: Chlordiazepoxide
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL451).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Chlormadinone Acetate
description: Progesterone receptor modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL110691).

name: Chloroprocaine
description: Ester local anaesthetic with the shortest duration in the class, cleared by plasma cholinesterase within minutes.

name: Chloroquine
description: The archetypal 4-aminoquinoline antimalarial, largely defeated by resistance but still central to malaria pharmacology and to lysosomal biology.

name: Chlorotrianisene
description: Estrogen receptor beta modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200761).

name: Chlorpheniramine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL505).

name: Chlorphenoxamine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2110774).

name: Chlorphentermine
description: Serotonin transporter substrate; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201269).

name: Chlorpromazine
description: Antagonizes or partially agonizes dopamine D2 receptors; movement, metabolic, and prolactin effects depend on receptor profile.

name: Chlorpropamide
description: Closes pancreatic beta-cell KATP channels to stimulate insulin release, with hypoglycemia as the central class risk.

name: Chlorthalidone
description: Thiazide-like diuretic; ALLHAT's reference arm and the best of the three at systolic control.

name: Cholecalciferol
description: Vitamin D receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1042).

name: Cholestyramine
description: Bile acid sequestrant; the oldest lipid drug class with hard outcome data behind it.

name: Choline
description: The dietary precursor of acetylcholine and of membrane phosphatidylcholine. An essential nutrient most people under-consume, which is different from being a cognitive enhancer in the replete.

name: Chondroitin (Sulfate)
description: Glycosaminoglycan component of cartilage studied for osteoarthritis pain relief, usually paired with glucosamine.

name: Choriogonadotropin Alfa
description: Luteinizing hormone/Choriogonadotropin receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201464).

name: Cianidanol
description: Unknown; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL311498).

name: Cibenzoline
description: Modulates fast cardiac sodium channels to alter impulse conduction; proarrhythmia makes clinical supervision essential.

name: Cibinetide (ARA-290)
description: Erythropoietin-derived peptide studied for tissue-protective and anti-inflammatory effects without erythropoietin's blood-thickening risk.

name: Ciclesonide
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2040682).

name: Cidofovir
description: Acyclic nucleoside phosphonate already carrying one phosphate, active against CMV, adenovirus and polyomavirus, and severely nephrotoxic.

name: Cilazapril
description: Blocks the renin–angiotensin system to reduce angiotensin-driven vasoconstriction or aldosterone signaling.

name: Cilofexor
description: Non-steroidal FXR agonist investigated for MASH and primary sclerosing cholangitis.

name: Cilomilast
description: Inhibits PDE4 to raise intracellular cAMP and dampen inflammatory cytokine production; emesis and weight loss are class-limiting; investigational, not approved.

name: Cilostazol
description: PDE3 inhibitor and antiplatelet vasodilator approved for intermittent claudication. It can cause headache, palpitations and tachycardia and is contraindicated in heart failure.

name: Ciltacabtagene Autoleucel
description: Tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 17 binding agent; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL4802263).
mechanism: Tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 17 binding agent

name: Cimetidine
description: Blocks parietal-cell H2 receptors to reduce stimulated gastric acid secretion; notable CYP inhibition and antiandrogenic effect.

name: Cimicoxib
description: Cimicoxib is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is cyclooxygenase-2 inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Cinacalcet
description: Acts on the PTH axis: intermittent PTH1R agonism is anabolic for bone, while calcimimetics suppress PTH secretion through the calcium-sensing receptor; calcimimetic, suppresses PTH.

name: Cinaciguat
description: Soluble guanylate cyclase ACTIVATOR — it works on the oxidised, haem-free enzyme that no longer responds to NO. Intravenous development was halted over excessive hypotension.

name: Cinnarizine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL43064).

name: Cipepofol
description: Cipepofol is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is gABA-A receptor; anion channel agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Ciprofibrate
description: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL557555).

name: Ciprofloxacin
description: Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase or topoisomerase IV; tendon, neurologic, cardiac, and resistance risks limit indiscriminate use.

name: Cisapride
description: Withdrawn 5-HT4 agonist prokinetic, the drug whose torsades deaths established hERG screening as a regulatory requirement.

name: Cisatracurium
description: The single potent isomer of atracurium, retaining organ-independent elimination without the histamine release.

name: Citalopram
description: Inhibits serotonin reuptake through SERT; benefits, activation, sexual effects, and withdrawal profiles differ by agent.

name: Citarinostat (ACY-241)
description: A more selective and more orally available successor to ricolinostat, studied in myeloma and in solid tumours combined with checkpoint blockade.

name: Citicoline (CDP-Choline)
description: Supplies both choline for acetylcholine and cytidine for membrane phospholipid synthesis, which is the claimed advantage over plain choline donors.

name: L-Citrulline
description: Urea-cycle amino acid that raises arginine and nitric-oxide availability more reliably than oral arginine; studied for blood flow and exercise performance.

name: Citrulline Malate
description: Nitric-oxide precursor supplement studied for exercise performance and the muscle 'pump'.

name: Citrus Bergamot (BPF)
description: Best-studied non-prescription lipid option -- lowers LDL and raises HDL in human trials.

name: Civamide
description: Activates TRPV1 on nociceptive afferents, where sustained exposure defunctionalises the nerve terminal and produces lasting analgesia; cis-isomer of capsaicin.

name: CJC-1295
description: Long-acting GHRH analog peptide that raises pulsatile growth hormone release, often paired with ipamorelin.

name: Clarithromycin
description: Inhibits bacterial protein synthesis at the ribosome; spectrum, resistance, and toxicity are agent-specific.

name: Clascoterone (Winlevi)
description: The first topical androgen receptor blocker approved for acne; broken down before it reaches circulation.

name: Clavulanic Acid
description: Suicide beta-lactamase inhibitor with negligible antibacterial activity of its own, paired with amoxicillin to restore activity against beta-lactamase producers.

name: Clazosentan
description: ETA-selective antagonist approved in Japan for cerebral vasospasm after subarachnoid haemorrhage.

name: Clemastine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1626).

name: Clenbuterol
description: Beta2-adrenergic agonist marketed as a veterinary asthma drug, widely misused by athletes/bodybuilders for its fat-oxidizing and muscle-sparing effects despite real cardiac risk.

name: Clevidipine
description: Ultra-short intravenous calcium-channel blocker for closely titrated acute hypertension; not an at-home intervention.

name: Clindamycin
description: Inhibits bacterial protein synthesis at the ribosome; spectrum, resistance, and toxicity are agent-specific.

name: Clindamycin (topical, 1% solution/gel)
description: Topical lincosamide antibiotic for acne; the workhorse of fixed combinations and the classic driver of C. acnes resistance.

name: Clobazam
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL70418).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Clobetasol Propionate
description: Super-potent topical corticosteroid for inflammatory dermatoses and some alopecia protocols; skin atrophy and systemic absorption limit duration.

name: Clobetasol propionate 0.05% (topical)
description: Class I superpotent topical corticosteroid, the reference point for topical steroid potency scales.

name: Clocortolone Pivalate
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200975).

name: Clodronate
description: Suppresses osteoclast-mediated bone resorption; jaw osteonecrosis and atypical femoral fracture are rare long-term class risks; non-nitrogen-containing.

name: Clofazimine
description: Riminophenazine used in leprosy and resistant tuberculosis, notorious for the reversible red-brown skin discoloration it causes in everyone.

name: Clofibrate
description: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL565).

name: Clometacin
description: Cyclooxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL13376).

name: Clomethiazole
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL315795).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Clomid (Clomiphene)
description: Selective estrogen receptor modulator used post-cycle to restart endogenous LH/FSH and testosterone production.

name: Clomipramine
description: Serotonin transporter inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL415).

name: Clonazepam
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL452).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Clonidine
description: Central alpha-2 agonist; effective, sedating, and dangerous to stop abruptly.

name: Clopidogrel (Plavix)
description: P2Y12 platelet inhibitor used after acute coronary syndromes and stenting; response varies with CYP2C19 activation and bleeding risk compounds with other antithrombotics.

name: Clorazepic Acid
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1213252).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Clorindione
description: Inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase so clotting factors are undercarboxylated; effect is delayed, diet-sensitive and needs INR monitoring.

name: Clostebol (4-Chlorotestosterone)
description: Chlorinated testosterone that cannot aromatise; notorious as an accidental doping positive from topical wound creams.

name: Clotiazepam
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1697737).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Clozapine
description: The only antipsychotic with proven superiority in treatment-resistant schizophrenia, requiring mandatory blood monitoring for agranulocytosis.

name: Cocoa Flavanols
description: Cocoa flavanols can improve endothelial function, while ordinary chocolate adds variable sugar and calories.

name: Codeine
description: Prodrug opioid whose entire analgesic effect depends on CYP2D6 conversion to morphine, making it the textbook pharmacogenetic drug.

name: Colchicine
description: Low-dose anti-inflammatory with a hard cardiovascular outcome trial behind it -- the only compound here targeting inflammation directly.

name: Colesevelam (Welchol)
description: Modern bile acid sequestrant with far fewer interactions than cholestyramine, plus a glucose indication.

name: Colestipol
description: Bile-acid sequestrant that lowers LDL but can raise triglycerides and impair absorption of drugs and vitamins.

name: Colforsin Daropate
description: Water-soluble forskolin derivative that activates adenylyl cyclase directly, bypassing receptors entirely. Used intravenously in Japan for acute heart failure.

name: Colistin (Polymyxin E)
description: Last-line polypeptide for carbapenem-resistant gram-negative infection, revived from the 1960s despite nephrotoxicity because nothing else works.

name: Oral collagen peptides
description: Hydrolyzed collagen supplement taken for skin hydration, elasticity, and wrinkle reduction.

name: Coluracetam
description: Racetam claimed to act as a high-affinity choline uptake enhancer, a mechanism distinct from the rest of the family. Abandoned in clinical development.

name: Conivaptan
description: Acts on vasopressin receptors to alter free-water handling or vascular tone; sodium shifts require monitoring; V1a/V2 antagonist.

name: Copper
description: Trace mineral required by lysyl oxidase, the enzyme that cross-links collagen and elastin fibers into strong connective tissue; deficiency measurably weakens tendon and bone.

name: Coenzyme Q10
description: Mitochondrial electron carrier; a real systolic blood pressure effect in cardiometabolic disease, much weaker evidence in plain hypertension.

name: Corifollitropin Alfa
description: Follicle stimulating hormone receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2108185).

name: Cortagen
description: Khavinson tetrapeptide bioregulator (Ala-Glu-Asp-Pro) derived from cortical peptide fractions. Short-peptide gerontology literature out of St Petersburg; not developed or approved in the West.

name: Cortexin
description: Polypeptide extract of bovine cerebral cortex, prescribed widely in Russia and the CIS and essentially unknown to Western regulators. Evidence base is almost entirely Russian-language and rarely blinded.

name: Corticotropin
description: Melanocortin receptor 2 agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201610).

name: Corticotropin Zinc Hydroxide
description: Melanocortin receptor 2 agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201609).

name: Cortisone Acetate
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1650).

name: Cortivazol
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2105842).

name: Cosyntropin
description: Melanocortin receptor 2 agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2103784).

name: Cotadutide
description: Investigational GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist studied for weight loss and liver-fat reduction.

name: Creatine Monohydrate
description: Best known for muscle, but the brain also runs a phosphocreatine buffer. Cognitive effects appear under sleep deprivation or metabolic stress and are absent in rested young adults.

name: Creatine Nitrate
description: Creatine salt marketed to combine phosphocreatine support with nitrate-mediated blood flow; far less studied than creatine monohydrate.

name: Crinecerfont
description: CRF1 receptor antagonist used to reduce excess adrenal androgen production in congenital adrenal hyperplasia.

name: Crisaborole (topical 2% ointment, Eucrisa)
description: Boron-based topical PDE4 inhibitor for mild to moderate atopic dermatitis; steroid-free and unrestricted by body site.

name: Crizanlizumab (Adakveo)
description: A monoclonal antibody against P-selectin that reduces the multicellular adhesion driving vaso-occlusive crises, targeting the adhesion step rather than the polymerisation step of sickle cell disease.

name: Sodium Cromoglicate
description: The original mast cell stabiliser, prophylactic only and safe enough to be sold over the counter as an eye drop and nasal spray.

name: Crotedumab
description: Crotedumab is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is glucagon receptor inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Crovalimab
description: Inhibits a step of the complement cascade; blocking terminal complement raises encapsulated-organism risk and requires meningococcal vaccination; C5 inhibitor.

name: Cudc-101
description: Cudc-101 is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC6. ChEMBL records IC50 5.1 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: Curcumin
description: Anti-inflammatory compound from turmeric that inhibits NF-kB signaling; poor natural bioavailability limits how much of its preclinical promise translates to oral supplementation without a specialized delivery formulation.

name: Curcumin Phytosome
description: Enhanced-absorption curcumin formulation; improved exposure also increases the relevance of drug interactions.

name: Cutamesine
description: Engages the sigma-1 chaperone at the ER-mitochondrial interface, modulating calcium handling and ER stress responses; investigational.

name: Cyclizine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL648).

name: Cyclofenil
description: Estrogen receptor modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL141305).

name: Cyclopentolate
description: Short-acting antimuscarinic mydriatic and cycloplegic used for refraction, particularly in children.

name: Cycloserine
description: Second-line antituberculous drug whose central nervous system toxicity reflects a second pharmacology entirely separate from its antibacterial action.

name: Cyclosporine
description: Calcineurin inhibitor binding cyclophilin, the original transplant immunosuppressant; also a potent P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 inhibitor.

name: Cyproheptadine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL516).

name: Cyproterone Acetate
description: Steroidal antiandrogen and progestin that blocks the androgen receptor and suppresses LH/testosterone production, used for antiandrogen therapy and as a contraceptive component.

name: Cysteamine 5% cream (topical)
description: Aminothiol depigmenting cream positioned as a hydroquinone alternative for melasma.

name: Dabigatran (Pradaxa)
description: Direct thrombin inhibitor used for atrial fibrillation and venous thromboembolism; renal clearance and bleeding interactions are central.

name: Dabigatran Etexilate
description: Thrombin inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL539697).

name: Dacinostat
description: Dacinostat is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC3. ChEMBL records IC50 0.4 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: Daclatasvir
description: Blocks an HCV replication target and is combined with complementary direct-acting antivirals to prevent resistance.

name: Dacomitinib
description: Inhibits oncogenic EGFR-family signaling; activity depends on tumor genotype and acquired resistance.

name: Dalbavancin
description: Long-acting lipoglycopeptide dosed once or twice per course, which turns a skin infection admission into an outpatient visit.

name: Dalcetrapib
description: CETP modulator that raises HDL but failed an unselected cardiovascular outcomes trial; genotype-guided research continues.

name: Dalteparin
description: Low molecular weight heparin, the standard agent for cancer-associated thrombosis in the era before direct oral anticoagulants.

name: Danazol
description: Synthetic attenuated androgen used for endometriosis and hereditary angioedema; binds the androgen receptor and displaces hormones from SHBG.

name: Danicopan
description: Inhibits a step of the complement cascade; blocking terminal complement raises encapsulated-organism risk and requires meningococcal vaccination; oral factor D inhibitor.

name: Dantrolene
description: Ryanodine receptor antagonist and the only effective treatment for malignant hyperthermia.

name: Danuglipron
description: Oral small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist in development for obesity and type 2 diabetes.

name: Dapagliflozin (Farxiga)
description: Another major SGLT2 inhibitor with real cardiovascular and kidney-protective outcome trial data, alongside empagliflozin one of the most-studied drugs in this class.

name: Dapansutrile
description: Oral NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitor investigated in gout and heart failure.

name: Dapoxetine
description: Inhibits serotonin reuptake through SERT; benefits, activation, sexual effects, and withdrawal profiles differ by agent.

name: Daprodustat
description: Oral HIF-PHI for anaemia of chronic kidney disease.

name: Dapsone
description: Sulfone used in leprosy, dermatitis herpetiformis and Pneumocystis prophylaxis, with a distinctive haematological toxicity profile.

name: Dapsone (topical gel 5% / 7.5%, Aczone)
description: Topical sulfone for acne; the gel, not the oral tablet that causes haemolysis and methaemoglobinaemia.

name: Daptomycin
description: Cyclic lipopeptide that is rapidly bactericidal against gram-positive organisms but inactivated by pulmonary surfactant, so it can never be used for pneumonia.

name: Daratumumab
description: Anti-CD38 antibody that transformed myeloma treatment, and which interferes with blood transfusion cross-matching because red cells also carry CD38.

name: Darbepoetin Alfa
description: Erythropoietin receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201566).

name: Darexaban
description: Directly inhibits factor Xa to reduce thrombin generation; renal clearance and reversal-agent availability differ by agent; investigational, discontinued.

name: Daridorexant (Quviviq)
description: Dual orexin receptor antagonist for insomnia, engineered for a short half-life to limit next-morning residual effect.

name: Darifenacin
description: Antagonises muscarinic receptors; peripheral selectivity determines how much dry mouth, constipation and central anticholinergic burden an agent carries; M3-selective.

name: Darigabat
description: Darigabat is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is gABA-A receptor; anion channel agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Darolutamide (Nubeqa)
description: Androgen receptor antagonist built with a polar structure that limits how much crosses into the brain.

name: Darunavir
description: The most robust HIV protease inhibitor, retaining activity against multiply resistant virus because of the number of backbone hydrogen bonds it forms.

name: Darusentan
description: Darusentan is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is endothelin receptor ET-A antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Dasantafil
description: Inhibits PDE5 so nitric-oxide/cGMP vasodilation persists in corporal and pulmonary vascular smooth muscle; investigational, development discontinued.

name: Dasatinib (Sprycel)
description: Leukaemia kinase inhibitor repurposed as half of the original senolytic combination.

name: Dasiglucagon Hydrochloride
description: Glucagon receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL4650274).

name: Davalintide
description: Amylin analogue studied for appetite suppression and weight loss; development did not establish routine clinical use.

name: Db959
description: Db959 is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor delta agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Debrisoquin
description: Norepinephrine transporter inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL169901).

name: Decitabine
description: Deoxy analogue of azacitidine incorporating only into DNA.

name: Deferasirox
description: Oral iron chelator for transfusional overload; renal and hepatic toxicity require monitoring.

name: Deferiprone
description: Oral iron chelator that penetrates cells well enough to remove cardiac iron, at the cost of agranulocytosis risk.

name: Deferoxamine
description: Parenteral iron chelator requiring prolonged subcutaneous infusion.

name: Deflazacort
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201891).

name: Degarelix (Firmagon)
description: GnRH antagonist that drops testosterone in days without the testosterone surge agonists cause.

name: Delafloxacin
description: Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase or topoisomerase IV; tendon, neurologic, cardiac, and resistance risks limit indiscriminate use.

name: Delamanid
description: Nitro-dihydro-imidazooxazole for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis, sharing pretomanid's activation route.

name: Delapril
description: Blocks the renin–angiotensin system to reduce angiotensin-driven vasoconstriction or aldosterone signaling.

name: Delgocitinib
description: Topical pan-JAK inhibitor licensed for chronic hand eczema, delivering JAK blockade without systemic exposure.

name: Demecarium
description: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201229).

name: Demoxytocin
description: Acts at the oxytocin receptor to drive uterine contraction and milk ejection, or blocks it to suppress preterm labour; buccal analogue.

name: Denifanstat
description: Oral fatty acid synthase inhibitor investigated in MASH and acne.

name: Denosumab (Prolia)
description: Monoclonal antibody that directly blocks RANKL, preventing osteoclast formation and activity -- a different mechanism from bisphosphonates, same net effect of reduced bone resorption.

name: Dersimelagon
description: Dersimelagon is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is melanocortin receptor 1 agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Desflurane
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200733).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Desiccated Thyroid Extract (NDT)
description: Porcine thyroid powder containing both T4 and T3; a pre-1938 preparation still prescribed off guideline.

name: Desipramine
description: Inhibits norepinephrine reuptake, often alongside serotonin effects; blood pressure and discontinuation effects require attention.

name: Desirudin
description: Thrombin inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201662).

name: Desloratadine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1172).

name: Desmopressin
description: Acts on vasopressin receptors to alter free-water handling or vascular tone; sodium shifts require monitoring; V2-selective agonist.

name: Desogestrel
description: Progesterone receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1533).

name: Desonide
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201109).

name: Desoximetasone
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1766).

name: Desoxycorticosterone Acetate
description: Mineralocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200542).

name: Desoxycorticosterone Pivalate
description: Mineralocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200592).

name: Desoxymethyltestosterone (Madol)
description: Undetectable-by-design designer anabolic steroid discovered in doping investigations.

name: Desvenlafaxine
description: Inhibits norepinephrine reuptake, often alongside serotonin effects; blood pressure and discontinuation effects require attention.

name: Deucravacitinib (Sotyktu)
description: Allosteric TYK2 inhibitor for plaque psoriasis with greater kinase selectivity than broad JAK inhibitors.

name: Deuruxolitinib (Leqselvi)
description: Oral deuterated ruxolitinib analogue developed for severe alopecia areata; a systemic JAK inhibitor with boxed-warning class risks.

name: Deutetrabenazine
description: Deuterated tetrabenazine whose carbon-deuterium bonds slow CYP2D6 metabolism, smoothing the concentration profile.

name: Dexamethasone Acetate
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1530428).

name: Dexamethasone
description: Long-acting fluorinated glucocorticoid with essentially no mineralocorticoid activity.

name: Dexamethasone Phosphoric Acid
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201302).

name: Dexbrompheniramine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201287).

name: Dexchlorpheniramine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201353).

name: Dexibuprofen
description: Cyclooxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL175).

name: Dexketoprofen
description: Cyclooxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL75435).

name: Dexlansoprazole
description: Inhibits the gastric proton pump to suppress acid secretion; long-term use affects micronutrient and mineral absorption.

name: Dexmedetomidine
description: Highly selective alpha-2 agonist producing sedation that resembles natural sleep, with analgesia and no respiratory depression.

name: Dexmethylphenidate
description: Norepinephrine transporter inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL827).

name: Dexrazoxane (Zinecard)
description: An EDTA analogue given to limit anthracycline cardiotoxicity. It chelates intracellular iron and also inhibits topoisomerase II beta, and which of the two matters more is still argued.

name: Dextroamphetamine
description: Norepinephrine transporter releasing agent; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL612).

name: Dextromethorphan
description: Engages the sigma-1 chaperone at the ER-mitochondrial interface, modulating calcium handling and ER stress responses; sigma-1 agonist and NMDA antagonist.

name: Dextrothyroxine
description: Thyroid hormone receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL559).

name: Dezocine
description: Mixed agonist-antagonist opioid used widely in China, with additional monoamine reuptake inhibition.

name: Docosahexaenoic Acid (DHA)
description: Long-chain omega-3 important to neural membranes; triglyceride lowering may accompany a rise in LDL.

name: DHEA
description: Adrenal androgen precursor supplement, one step upstream of androstenedione and testosterone in the steroid synthesis pathway; sold over-the-counter unlike most of its downstream products.

name: DHT (Dihydrotestosterone)
description: The potent, non-aromatizable androgen that testosterone converts into via 5-alpha-reductase; drives androgenic effects like body hair and prostate growth, and is the direct hormone finasteride/dutasteride block the production of.

name: Diamorphine (Heroin)
description: Diacetylmorphine, a prodrug of morphine used clinically in the United Kingdom for acute severe pain and in supervised injectable treatment programmes.

name: Diazepam
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL12).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Diazoxide
description: Potassium-channel opener that suppresses insulin release and treats selected hypoglycemia disorders; causes fluid retention.

name: Dibenzepin
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1442422).

name: Dibotermin Alfa
description: Activin receptor type-2B agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2109171).

name: Dichloroacetate
description: PDK inhibitor that forces pyruvate into oxidation; studied in congenital lactic acidosis and, speculatively, oncology. Peripheral neuropathy limits chronic use.

name: Dichlorphenamide
description: Inhibits carbonic anhydrase, lowering bicarbonate-dependent fluid secretion; metabolic acidosis and paraesthesia are the usual class effects.

name: Diclofenac
description: Cyclooxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL139).

name: Dicoumarol
description: Inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase so clotting factors are undercarboxylated; effect is delayed, diet-sensitive and needs INR monitoring; the original coumarin anticoagulant.

name: Dienestrol
description: Estrogen receptor alpha agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1018).

name: Dietary nitrate (beetroot)
description: Inorganic nitrate reduced to nitrite and then NO -- a dietary route to the same vasodilation drugs target.

name: Diethylcarbamazine
description: Nematode GABA-A receptor positive modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL684).

name: Diethylpropion
description: Norepinephrine transporter inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1194666).

name: Diethylstilbestrol
description: Estrogen receptor alpha agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL411).

name: Diethylstilbestrol Diphosphate
description: Estrogen receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200598).

name: Difamilast
description: Inhibits PDE4 to raise intracellular cAMP and dampen inflammatory cytokine production; emesis and weight loss are class-limiting; topical, approved in Japan.

name: Difelikefalin
description: Peripherally restricted kappa agonist for uraemic pruritus — analgesia and antipruritus without CNS dysphoria because it does not cross the blood-brain barrier.

name: Diflorasone Diacetate
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200545).

name: Diflunisal
description: Cyclooxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL898).

name: Difluprednate
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201749).

name: Digitoxin
description: The hepatically cleared cardiac glycoside, unlike renally cleared digoxin. Same Na+/K+-ATPase mechanism but a much longer half-life and no dose adjustment in renal failure.

name: Digoxin
description: Cardiac glycoside from foxglove; a positive inotrope and rate-control agent with a famously narrow therapeutic index.

name: Dihexa
description: Angiotensin IV analogue built as an HGF potentiator; the potency claims are all preclinical.

name: Dihydroboldenone (1-Testosterone)
description: Non-aromatizable injectable anabolic steroid popular in underground labs for lean mass.

name: Dihydroergotamine
description: Ergot alkaloid for refractory and status migraine, a promiscuous agonist across serotonin, adrenergic and dopamine receptors.

name: Dihydrotachysterol
description: Vitamin D receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2356023).

name: Dilevalol
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL27193).

name: Diltiazem
description: Non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that slows the heart as well as dilating vessels.

name: Dimenhydrinate
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200406).

name: Dimethandrolone Undecanoate (DMAU)
description: Oral androgen and progestin in one molecule, developed as a male hormonal contraceptive. Not aromatised to estradiol, which is why it suppresses gonadotropins without the estrogenic offset testosterone provides. Investigational.

name: Dimethazine (DMZ)
description: Designer prohormone-era oral anabolic steroid marketed as a 'methylated superdrol' analog.

name: Dimethindene
description: Dimethindene is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is histamine H1 receptor antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: 2,4-Dinitrophenol (DNP)
description: Chemical uncoupler that dissipates the proton gradient as heat. Genuinely effective for fat loss and genuinely lethal — there is no margin between the effective and fatal dose, and deaths from supplement use are recurrent.

name: Dinoprostone
description: PGE2 used for cervical ripening and labour induction.

name: Diosmin
description: Flavonoid venotonic commonly paired with hesperidin for chronic venous disease and hemorrhoidal symptoms; it is not an arterial-performance enhancer.

name: Micronized Diosmin/Hesperidin
description: Flavonoid combination used for chronic venous disease and hemorrhoidal symptoms; benefit is symptom-focused.

name: Diphenhydramine (Benadryl)
description: First-generation antihistamine widely used as an OTC sleep aid despite rapid tolerance, next-day impairment, and anticholinergic burden.

name: Diphenylpyraline
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1492).

name: Dipyridamole
description: Antiplatelet and vasodilator used mainly with aspirin after stroke or with selected prosthetic valves.

name: Disopyramide
description: Modulates fast cardiac sodium channels to alter impulse conduction; proarrhythmia makes clinical supervision essential.

name: Distigmine
description: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1199307).

name: Disulfiram
description: Alcohol deterrent that works by making drinking acutely unpleasant rather than by reducing craving.

name: DMAE (Dimethylaminoethanol)
description: An older cholinergic-adjacent supplement whose proposed conversion to choline in the brain is poorly supported. Retained mainly because it still appears in stacks.

name: Dobutamine
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL926).

name: Dofetilide
description: Alters cardiac repolarization through potassium-channel effects; QT prolongation and torsades risk vary by agent.

name: Dolasetron
description: Antagonises 5-HT3 receptors on vagal afferents and in the area postrema; QT effects vary by agent; IV use restricted over QT effects.

name: Dolutegravir
description: Inhibits HIV integrase strand transfer as a component of combination antiretroviral therapy.

name: Domagrozumab
description: Anti-myostatin monoclonal antibody whose Duchenne program failed its primary functional endpoint.

name: Domperidone
description: Peripheral dopamine antagonist prokinetic that does not cross the blood-brain barrier, so it lacks the extrapyramidal effects of metoclopramide.

name: Donanemab (Kisunla)
description: An antibody against the pyroglutamate-modified amyloid found only in established plaque. It clears plaque faster than lecanemab and is stopped once clearance is achieved, which is a genuinely different treatment paradigm.

name: Donepezil (Aricept)
description: Reversible, centrally selective acetylcholinesterase inhibitor; the most widely prescribed drug for Alzheimer's dementia.

name: Dopamine (IV infusion)
description: Inotrope and vasopressor whose receptor profile changes with infusion rate, now largely displaced by noradrenaline in shock.

name: Doravirine
description: Inhibits HIV reverse transcriptase and is used only as part of a resistance-aware antiretroviral regimen.

name: Dorzolamide
description: Inhibits carbonic anhydrase, lowering bicarbonate-dependent fluid secretion; metabolic acidosis and paraesthesia are the usual class effects; topical ophthalmic.

name: Dostarlimab
description: Anti-PD-1 antibody that produced complete clinical responses in every patient in a small mismatch-repair-deficient rectal cancer trial.

name: Dothiepin
description: Serotonin transporter inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1492500).

name: Dotinurad
description: Blocks proximal-tubule urate reabsorption to raise fractional urate excretion; urine volume and stone risk need attention; approved in Japan.

name: Dovitinib
description: Multi-kinase inhibitor hitting FGFR1-3 alongside VEGFR and PDGFR. Oncology-developed and never pursued for skeletal dysplasia; the off-target breadth is why.

name: Doxazosin (Cardura)
description: Alpha-1 blocker that treats blood pressure and prostatic obstruction at once.

name: Doxepin
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1628227).

name: Doxepin, low dose (Silenor)
description: Tricyclic antidepressant repurposed at 3 mg and 6 mg, doses at which it acts as a nearly pure histamine H1 antagonist.

name: Doxercalciferol
description: Vitamin D receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200810).

name: Doxofylline
description: Xanthine bronchodilator with markedly less adenosine-receptor antagonism than theophylline, giving a wider therapeutic window and fewer cardiac and CNS effects.

name: Doxorubicin (Adriamycin)
description: An anthracycline that intercalates DNA, poisons topoisomerase II and generates iron-dependent free radicals. The last of those is why its cardiotoxicity is cumulative and dose-limited rather than reversible.

name: Doxycycline
description: Tetracycline used for acne and sub-antimicrobial anti-inflammatory dosing in rosacea; photosensitivity and antimicrobial stewardship matter.

name: Doxycycline 40 mg modified release (Oracea)
description: Sub-antimicrobial dose tetracycline for rosacea; deliberately dosed below the level that treats infection.

name: Doxylamine
description: Sedating first-generation antihistamine used OTC for short-term insomnia and in pregnancy nausea combinations; tolerance and anticholinergic effects limit repeated use.

name: Droloxifene
description: Droloxifene is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is estrogen receptor modulator; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Dromostanolone Propionate
description: Androgen Receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201048).

name: Dronabinol
description: Synthetic delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol licensed for chemotherapy nausea and for AIDS-related anorexia.

name: Dronedarone
description: Alters cardiac repolarization through potassium-channel effects; QT prolongation and torsades risk vary by agent.

name: Droperidol
description: D2-like dopamine receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1108).

name: Drospirenone
description: Progesterone receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1509).

name: Masteron (Drostanolone)
description: DHT-derived steroid with anti-estrogenic properties, used mainly for a harder, drier physique.

name: DSIP (Delta sleep-inducing peptide)
description: Historic sleep-research peptide with unresolved receptor pharmacology, studied for effects on sleep and stress-hormone secretion.

name: Dulaglutide (Trulicity)
description: Once-weekly GLP-1 receptor agonist for type 2 diabetes, similar class effect to semaglutide on glycemic control and weight.

name: Duloxetine (Cymbalta)
description: SNRI used for depression, anxiety, and neuropathic pain; withdrawal, liver, blood-pressure, and sexual effects matter.

name: Dupilumab (Dupixent, subcutaneous)
description: Monoclonal antibody against the IL-4 receptor alpha subunit; the first biologic approved for atopic dermatitis.

name: Durvalumab
description: Anti-PD-L1 antibody established as consolidation after chemoradiotherapy in stage III lung cancer.

name: Dusigitumab
description: Dusigitumab is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is insulin-like growth factor I inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Dutasteride (Avodart)
description: Dual type-1/type-2 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor, more complete DHT suppression than finasteride (which mainly hits type 2), sometimes used off-label for hair loss.

name: Dutogliptin
description: Inhibits DPP-4 to prolong endogenous incretin signaling and glucose-dependent insulin release.

name: Dydrogesterone
description: Progesterone receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200853).

name: Ebastine
description: Histamine H1 receptor inverse agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL305660).

name: Ecdysterone (20-Hydroxyecdysone)
description: Phytoecdysteroid marketed for muscle gain; limited human training data exist, while receptor pharmacology differs from anabolic-androgenic steroids.

name: Echothiophate
description: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201341).

name: Ecnoglutide (XW003)
description: Weekly GLP-1 analogue in late-stage development, developed primarily in China.

name: Econazole
description: Topical imidazole for dermatophyte and candidal skin infection, one of the oldest members of the class still in routine use.

name: Eculizumab
description: Inhibits a step of the complement cascade; blocking terminal complement raises encapsulated-organism risk and requires meningococcal vaccination; C5 inhibitor.

name: Calcium Disodium EDTA
description: Parenteral chelator for symptomatic lead poisoning, formulated as the calcium salt so it does not strip calcium itself.

name: Edoxaban (Savaysa/Lixiana)
description: Once-daily factor Xa inhibitor whose dosing depends on renal function and indication.

name: Edrophonium
description: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1104).

name: Efavirenz
description: Inhibits HIV reverse transcriptase and is used only as part of a resistance-aware antiretroviral regimen.

name: Efgartigimod
description: Engineered Fc fragment that lowers circulating IgG by outcompeting it for the neonatal Fc receptor, used in myasthenia gravis.

name: Efinopegdutide
description: Long-acting GLP-1/glucagon co-agonist studied for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.

name: Efocipegtrutide
description: Investigational long-acting GLP-1/glucagon receptor co-agonist studied for obesity and metabolic liver disease.

name: Efpeglenatide
description: Exendin-based weekly GLP-1 with a completed cardiovascular and kidney outcomes trial.

name: Efruxifermin
description: An Fc-FGF21 fusion protein in trials for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis, improving liver fat, fibrosis and lipids through FGF21 receptor complexes.

name: EGCG (Green Tea Extract)
description: Green tea catechin studied for modestly increasing fat oxidation and energy expenditure.

name: Topical EGF
description: Epidermal growth factor applied cosmetically to accelerate skin repair and support a more youthful appearance.

name: Elacestrant
description: Estrogen receptor alpha degrader; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL4297509).

name: Elafibranor
description: Dual PPAR-alpha/delta agonist developed for cholestatic and metabolic liver disease.

name: Elagolix
description: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1208155).

name: Elamipretide (SS-31)
description: Mitochondria-targeted tetrapeptide studied in clinical trials for improving mitochondrial function, exercise tolerance, and skeletal muscle bioenergetics in aging and mitochondrial disease.

name: Elbasvir
description: Blocks an HCV replication target and is combined with complementary direct-acting antivirals to prevent resistance.

name: Eldecalcitol (Edirol)
description: Japanese active vitamin D analogue with a 2-beta hydroxypropyloxy group and a long half-life.

name: Eletriptan
description: Triptan with the highest oral efficacy in comparative meta-analyses, and a P-glycoprotein substrate.

name: Elexacaftor
description: A next-generation CFTR corrector binding a site distinct from tezacaftor's, so the two are additive. The triple combination it anchors reaches roughly 90% of people with cystic fibrosis.

name: Eliglustat
description: Oral substrate reduction therapy for Gaucher disease, lowering glucosylceramide production rather than replacing the enzyme.

name: Elinogrel
description: Inhibits platelet P2Y12 ADP signalling to reduce aggregation, at the cost of bleeding risk; investigational, development discontinued.

name: Elotuzumab
description: Anti-SLAMF7 antibody for myeloma that works partly by activating natural killer cells rather than only by tagging the tumour.

name: Elranatamab
description: Tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 17 binding agent; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL4297809).
mechanism: Tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 17 binding agent

name: Eluxadoline
description: Mixed mu agonist / delta antagonist acting locally in the gut for IBS with diarrhoea; contraindicated without a gallbladder over pancreatitis risk.

name: Elvitegravir
description: Inhibits HIV integrase strand transfer as a component of combination antiretroviral therapy.

name: Emedastine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL594).

name: Empagliflozin (Jardiance)
description: SGLT2 inhibitor that blocks renal glucose reabsorption; the landmark EMPA-REG trial found real cardiovascular mortality benefit in type 2 diabetes, not just glucose lowering.

name: Emricasan
description: Pan-caspase inhibitor trialled in liver disease; lowered transaminases without improving fibrosis.

name: Emtricitabine
description: Inhibits HIV reverse transcriptase and is used only as part of a resistance-aware antiretroviral regimen.

name: Enalapril
description: ACE inhibitor with the best-documented haematocrit-lowering effect of any drug in this graph.

name: Enalaprilat Anhydrous
description: Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL577).

name: Encaleret
description: Acts on the PTH axis: intermittent PTH1R agonism is anabolic for bone, while calcimimetics suppress PTH secretion through the calcium-sensing receptor; investigational calcilytic.

name: Enclomiphene
description: One of the two isomers that make up clomiphene citrate; stimulates the body's own testosterone and sperm production by blocking estrogen feedback at the hypothalamus, unlike exogenous testosterone which shuts that down.

name: Enflurane
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1257).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive modulator

name: Enfuvirtide
description: Inhibits HIV integrase strand transfer as a component of combination antiretroviral therapy.

name: Enoxaparin
description: Low-molecular-weight heparin anticoagulant; renal dosing and bleeding surveillance are essential.

name: Enoximone
description: PDE3 inhibitor inodilator, used mainly in Europe. Same class effects as milrinone with an oral formulation history.

name: Ensifentrine (Ohtuvayre)
description: Inhaled dual PDE3/PDE4 inhibitor approved for COPD in 2024 — the first genuinely new inhaled mechanism in that indication for decades. Bronchodilates and suppresses inflammation from one molecule.

name: Ensitrelvir
description: Non-covalent oral SARS-CoV-2 main protease inhibitor developed in Japan, notable for not requiring ritonavir boosting.

name: Entacapone
description: A peripheral COMT inhibitor given with levodopa-carbidopa. It blocks the remaining route of peripheral levodopa loss once decarboxylase is already inhibited, extending each dose's on-time rather than raising its peak.

name: Entecavir
description: Guanosine analogue for hepatitis B with a very high genetic barrier to resistance in treatment-naive patients.

name: Entinostat
description: Class I selective HDAC inhibitor investigated in combination oncology.

name: Entolimod
description: Entolimod is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is toll-like receptor 5 agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Enzalutamide
description: Nonsteroidal androgen receptor antagonist approved for prostate cancer; blocks androgen binding, nuclear translocation, and DNA binding at the receptor.

name: Eicosapentaenoic Acid (EPA)
description: Long-chain omega-3 that lowers triglycerides; purified prescription evidence should not be generalized to every fish-oil blend.

name: Epalrestat
description: Inhibits aldose reductase to limit polyol-pathway flux and the osmotic and oxidative stress it imposes during hyperglycaemia; approved in Japan, India and China.

name: Epelsiban
description: Acts at the oxytocin receptor to drive uterine contraction and milk ejection, or blocks it to suppress preterm labour; investigational antagonist.

name: Ephedrine
description: Sympathomimetic stimulant that raises energy expenditure substantially through beta-adrenoceptor activation; historically paired with caffeine as a fat-loss stack ('ECA'), now restricted in many countries.

name: Epiandrosterone
description: Naturally occurring DHEA metabolite that converts onward to DHT; sold as a legal prohormone.

name: Epinastine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1106).

name: Adrenaline (Epinephrine)
description: The first-line drug in anaphylaxis and cardiac arrest, acting on every adrenergic receptor class at once with dose-dependent balance.

name: Epistane (Methylepitiostanol)
description: 17-alpha-alkylated designer steroid sold as a supplement until scheduling; a documented cause of cholestatic liver injury.

name: Epitalon
description: A synthetic tetrapeptide claimed to activate telomerase, derived from Soviet-era pineal extract work. Human data amount to a handful of small unblinded studies from one group; the telomerase claim is unreplicated.

name: Epithalon
description: Synthetic tetrapeptide studied for telomerase activation and longevity/anti-aging effects.

name: Eplerenone
description: More selective mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist than spironolactone, developed specifically to avoid spironolactone's antiandrogenic side effects (gynecomastia, menstrual disturbance) while retaining its blood-pressure/potassium-sparing benefits.

name: Epoetin Alfa
description: Erythropoietin receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201565).

name: Epoetin Beta
description: Erythropoietin receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2109092).

name: Epoetin Delta
description: Erythropoietin receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2109093).

name: Epoetin Theta
description: Erythropoietin receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2108290).

name: Epoetin Zeta
description: Erythropoietin receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2108593).

name: Epoprostenol
description: Synthetic prostacyclin requiring continuous central infusion because its half-life is a few minutes; the first PAH therapy shown to improve survival.

name: Eprosartan
description: Angiotensin II receptor blocker for hypertension with class risks of hyperkalemia and fetal toxicity.

name: Eprotirome
description: Eprotirome is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is thyroid hormone receptor beta-1 agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Eptifibatide
description: Cyclic heptapeptide GPIIb/IIIa antagonist, reversible with a short half-life so platelet function recovers within hours of stopping.

name: Eptinezumab
description: Blocks CGRP ligand or receptor signalling in the trigeminovascular system for migraine prevention or acute treatment; intravenous monoclonal antibody.

name: Eptotermin Alfa
description: Activin receptor type-1 agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2108594).

name: Eravacycline
description: Inhibits bacterial protein synthesis at the ribosome; spectrum, resistance, and toxicity are agent-specific.

name: Balversa (Erdafitinib)
description: Oral pan-FGFR1-4 inhibitor approved for urothelial carcinoma; hyperphosphatemia from off-isoform blockade is dose-limiting.

name: Erenumab
description: Blocks CGRP ligand or receptor signalling in the trigeminovascular system for migraine prevention or acute treatment; receptor monoclonal antibody.

name: Ergocalciferol
description: Vitamin D receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1536).

name: Ergoloid
description: Dopamine receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2364968).

name: Ergothioneine
description: Amino acid the body cannot make but built a dedicated transporter for -- which is the argument for it.

name: Erlotinib
description: Inhibits oncogenic EGFR-family signaling; activity depends on tumor genotype and acquired resistance.

name: Ertapenem
description: Once-daily carbapenem lacking antipseudomonal and enterococcal activity, which is exactly why it is used for community ESBL infection without driving Pseudomonas resistance.

name: Ertugliflozin
description: Sodium/glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1770248).

name: Erythromycin
description: Inhibits bacterial protein synthesis at the ribosome; spectrum, resistance, and toxicity are agent-specific.

name: Esaxerenone
description: Blocks mineralocorticoid-receptor signalling to reduce sodium retention and fibrotic remodelling; hyperkalaemia is the defining class risk; non-steroidal, approved in Japan.

name: Escitalopram (Lexapro)
description: Selective SSRI for depression and generalized anxiety; QT, sexual, withdrawal, and serotonin-syndrome considerations remain.

name: Esflurbiprofen
description: Cyclooxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL435298).

name: Esketamine (Spravato)
description: Intranasal S-enantiomer of ketamine, the first genuinely new antidepressant mechanism in decades, administered under observation.

name: Eslicarbazepine Acetate
description: Reduces high-frequency neuronal firing through voltage-gated sodium-channel modulation.

name: Esmolol
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL768).

name: Esomeprazole
description: Inhibits the gastric proton pump to suppress acid secretion; long-term use affects micronutrient and mineral absorption.

name: Estazolam
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL285674).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Estetrol Anhydrous
description: Estrogen receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1230314).

name: Estradiol Acetate
description: Estrogen receptor alpha agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200430).

name: Estradiol
description: The primary and most potent naturally occurring estrogen; used clinically in HRT, and the downstream hormone that aromatase produces from testosterone -- the target that AIs like anastrozole work to suppress.

name: Estradiol Cypionate
description: Estrogen receptor alpha agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200973).

name: Estradiol Valerate
description: Estrogen receptor alpha agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1511).

name: L-NMMA (Tilarginine)
description: Non-selective NOS inhibitor — the pharmacological opposite of the supplements above. Used experimentally to prove an effect is NO-mediated; a cardiogenic shock trial was stopped for harm.

name: L-Tyrosine
description: Precursor amino acid for dopamine and noradrenaline. Only helps where synthesis has been depleted by acute stress, cold or sleep loss -- it does nothing measurable in rested, unstressed people.

name: Labetalol (Trandate)
description: Combined alpha-1 and non-selective beta blocker; the standard oral and intravenous antihypertensive in pregnancy.

name: Lacosamide
description: Reduces high-frequency neuronal firing through voltage-gated sodium-channel modulation.

name: Lactitol
description: Nonabsorbed disaccharide laxative also used for hepatic encephalopathy through colonic ammonia trapping.

name: Lactulose
description: Nonabsorbed sugar used to trap ammonia in the colon and treat hepatic encephalopathy; diarrhea limits dosing.

name: Lafutidine
description: Blocks parietal-cell H2 receptors to reduce stimulated gastric acid secretion; approved in Japan.

name: Lamivudine
description: Inhibits HIV reverse transcriptase and is used only as part of a resistance-aware antiretroviral regimen.

name: Lamotrigine
description: Reduces high-frequency neuronal firing through voltage-gated sodium-channel modulation.

name: Landogrozumab (LY2495655)
description: Anti-myostatin antibody studied for sarcopenia and hip-fracture recovery with limited functional benefit.

name: Lanifibranor
description: Pan-PPAR agonist in late-stage study for steatohepatitis; weight gain and edema are relevant class effects.

name: Lanreotide
description: Long-acting somatostatin analog used to suppress excess growth hormone secretion.

name: Lansoprazole
description: Inhibits the gastric proton pump to suppress acid secretion; long-term use affects micronutrient and mineral absorption.

name: Lanthanum Carbonate
description: Phosphate binder using a rare earth metal, effective at low pill burden and minimally absorbed.

name: Larazotide Acetate (AT1001)
description: Octapeptide zonulin antagonist that tightens intestinal junctions rather than acting systemically. Taken furthest in celiac disease; investigational everywhere.

name: Largazole
description: Largazole is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC3. ChEMBL records IC50 9.09 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: Largazole Thiol
description: Largazole Thiol is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC3. ChEMBL records IC50 0.7 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: Lasmiditan
description: Ditan acting at 5-HT1F, which produces no vasoconstriction at all and so is usable in patients with cardiovascular contraindications to triptans.

name: Lasofoxifene
description: High-potency SERM approved in Europe but never in the US; now being revisited for resistant breast cancer.

name: Latanoprost
description: Glaucoma prostaglandin analogue whose eyelash side effect became the point.

name: Latanoprostene Bunod
description: Prostanoid FP receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2364612).

name: Latanoprostene Bunod
description: Nitric oxide donating prostaglandin analogue for glaucoma, lowering pressure through two outflow routes at once.

name: 5α-Hydroxy Laxogenin
description: Plant-derived brassinosteroid analogue marketed as a non-hormonal anabolic despite a lack of credible human trials.

name: LBY-135
description: LBY-135 is a phase 1 research agent catalogued by ChEMBL as an agonist of death receptor 5 (TNFRSF10B). The pathway link describes that curated mechanism, not established safety or clinical benefit.

name: Lebrikizumab (Ebglyss)
description: IL-13–blocking monoclonal antibody for moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, with conjunctivitis and injection reactions among key risks.

name: Lecanemab (Leqembi)
description: A monoclonal antibody selective for soluble amyloid-beta protofibrils. It slowed decline by roughly 27% on CDR-SB over 18 months, a statistically clear but clinically contested effect, at the cost of ARIA in about one in five treated patients.

name: Ledipasvir
description: Blocks an HCV replication target and is combined with complementary direct-acting antivirals to prevent resistance.

name: Lefamulin
description: First systemic pleuromutilin, approved for community-acquired pneumonia and acting at a ribosomal site no other human antibiotic class uses.

name: Leflunomide
description: Pyrimidine synthesis inhibitor for rheumatoid arthritis with an active metabolite that recirculates enterohepatically for months.

name: Lemborexant (Dayvigo)
description: Dual orexin-receptor antagonist for sleep-onset and maintenance insomnia, with next-day impairment and CNS-depressant interaction concerns.

name: Lenacapavir
description: Inhibits HIV integrase strand transfer as a component of combination antiretroviral therapy.

name: Lenalidomide
description: Second-generation IMiD central to myeloma therapy and uniquely effective in del(5q) myelodysplastic syndrome.

name: Lenvatinib
description: Multi-kinase inhibitor with FGFR1-4 activity used in thyroid, hepatocellular and renal cancer. Included for FGFR completeness, not as a growth agent.

name: Lepirudin
description: Thrombin inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201666).

name: Lercanidipine
description: Third-generation lipophilic dihydropyridine marketed on a lower rate of ankle oedema than amlodipine.

name: Lerodalcibep
description: Investigational long-acting PCSK9-binding fusion protein designed for monthly LDL lowering.

name: Lesinurad
description: Blocks proximal-tubule urate reabsorption to raise fractional urate excretion; urine volume and stone risk need attention; withdrawn from marketing.

name: Lestaurtinib
description: Lestaurtinib is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is tyrosine-protein kinase JAK2 inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Letermovir
description: CMV prophylactic with a target unique to that virus, avoiding the marrow toxicity that limited valganciclovir prophylaxis.

name: Femara (Letrozole)
description: Highly potent non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor, more aggressive than anastrozole at suppressing estrogen.

name: Leucine
description: Branched-chain amino acid that directly activates mTORC1 signaling, the single strongest known dietary trigger of muscle protein synthesis among individual amino acids.

name: Leuprolide (Lupron)
description: The most widely used GnRH agonist; depot formulations suppress the axis for months at a time.

name: Levetiracetam
description: Broad-spectrum anticonvulsant with no significant drug interactions and a target no other class shares, offset by behavioural adverse effects.

name: Levobunolol
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201237).

name: Levocabastine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1615438).

name: Levocetirizine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201191).

name: Levodopa / Carbidopa (Sinemet)
description: Dopamine precursor combined with a peripheral decarboxylase inhibitor; still the reference treatment for Parkinson's disease.

name: Levodopa
description: The dopamine precursor that crosses the blood-brain barrier where dopamine itself cannot. Still the most effective symptomatic treatment for Parkinson disease more than fifty years on, and always co-formulated with a peripheral decarboxylase inhibitor.

name: Levofloxacin
description: Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase or topoisomerase IV; tendon, neurologic, cardiac, and resistance risks limit indiscriminate use.

name: Levoketoconazole
description: Steroidogenesis inhibitor approved for endogenous Cushing syndrome; liver and QT monitoring are required.

name: Levomepromazine
description: D2-like dopamine receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1764).

name: Levomilnacipran
description: Inhibits norepinephrine reuptake, often alongside serotonin effects; blood pressure and discontinuation effects require attention.

name: Levonorgestrel
description: Progesterone receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1389).

name: Levorphanol
description: Long-acting morphinan opioid with NMDA antagonism and monoamine reuptake inhibition, sometimes described as an oral methadone alternative.

name: Levosalbutamol
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1002).

name: Levosimendan
description: Calcium-sensitizing inodilator used for acute heart failure in some countries; hypotension and arrhythmia risk require monitored infusion.

name: Levothyroxine (Synthroid)
description: Synthetic T4 thyroid hormone, the standard hypothyroidism replacement therapy and a component of some fat-loss protocols.

name: Lexatumumab
description: Lexatumumab is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 10B agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.
mechanism: tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 10B agonist

name: LGD-2226
description: Preclinical SARM investigated for muscle and bone effects; never established as a human performance drug.

name: LGD-3303
description: Ligandrol's less-known sibling, characterised in animal bone and muscle models and never taken further.

name: Lh (Menotropins)
description: Luteinizing hormone/Choriogonadotropin receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201697).

name: Licogliflozin
description: Licogliflozin is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is sodium/glucose cotransporter 1 inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Lidocaine
description: The most widely used local anaesthetic and also a class Ib antiarrhythmic, the same channel block serving two entirely different purposes.

name: Systemic Lidocaine
description: Modulates fast cardiac sodium channels to alter impulse conduction; proarrhythmia makes clinical supervision essential.

name: Lidorestat
description: Inhibits aldose reductase to limit polyol-pathway flux and the osmotic and oxidative stress it imposes during hyperglycaemia; research compound.

name: Ligandrol (LGD-4033)
description: Potent SARM studied for lean mass and strength gains via selective androgen receptor activation.

name: Linaclotide
description: Guanylate cyclase C agonist peptide for constipation-predominant irritable bowel syndrome, not absorbed at all.

name: Linagliptin (Tradjenta)
description: DPP-4 inhibitor for type 2 diabetes, unusual in requiring no renal dose adjustment; weight-neutral rather than a weight-loss drug.

name: Lindane
description: GABA-A receptor negative allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL15891).

name: Linezolid
description: Inhibits bacterial protein synthesis at the ribosome; spectrum, resistance, and toxicity are agent-specific.

name: Linsidomine (SIN-1)
description: Active metabolite of molsidomine and a direct NO donor. Also generates superoxide as it releases NO, so it produces peroxynitrite — a genuine caveat for a molecule marketed as an NO source.

name: Linsitinib
description: Linsitinib is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is insulin-like growth factor I receptor inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.
mechanism: insulin-like growth factor I receptor inhibitor

name: Linzagolix
description: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL3668014).

name: Lion's Mane (Hericium erinaceus)
description: Mushroom whose hericenones and erinacines stimulate nerve growth factor in vitro. The human trials are small, short and mixed, and none has measured NGF in people.

name: Liothyronine (Cytomel)
description: Synthetic T3, the biologically active thyroid hormone; faster-acting than levothyroxine and sometimes misused for aggressive fat loss due to its direct metabolic effect.

name: Liproxstatin-1
description: Ferroptosis inhibitor active in GPX4-null models. Research compound.

name: Saxenda/Victoza (Liraglutide)
description: Earlier daily GLP-1 receptor agonist, predecessor to semaglutide, used for both diabetes and weight loss.

name: Lisdexamfetamine (Vyvanse)
description: Dextroamphetamine prodrug for ADHD and binge-eating disorder; controlled stimulant risks still apply.

name: Lisinopril Anhydrous
description: Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1237).

name: Lisinopril
description: ACE inhibitor and ALLHAT first-line arm; cheap and effective, dry cough being the usual reason to switch to an ARB.

name: Lithium Carbonate
description: The oldest and still most effective mood stabiliser, the only psychotropic with replicated anti-suicide evidence, and dangerously narrow in therapeutic index.

name: Lithium Orotate
description: Low-dose lithium salt sold as a supplement, at a fraction of the psychiatric dose and without monitoring.

name: Livagen
description: Khavinson tetrapeptide (Lys-Glu-Asp-Ala) reported to act on chromatin condensation in lymphocytes. Interesting mechanism, very thin evidence.

name: Lixisenatide (Adlyxin)
description: Once-daily GLP-1 receptor agonist, shorter-acting than dulaglutide/semaglutide, used for glycemic control in type 2 diabetes.

name: Lixivaptan
description: Acts on vasopressin receptors to alter free-water handling or vascular tone; sodium shifts require monitoring; investigational.

name: LL-37
description: Human cathelicidin antimicrobial peptide studied for its role in innate immune defense and wound healing.

name: Lobeglitazone
description: PPAR-gamma agonist approved in South Korea, with a claimed lower dose than pioglitazone.

name: Lodenafil Carbonate
description: Inhibits PDE5 so nitric-oxide/cGMP vasodilation persists in corporal and pulmonary vascular smooth muscle; approved in Brazil.

name: Lomefloxacin
description: Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase or topoisomerase IV; tendon, neurologic, cardiac, and resistance risks limit indiscriminate use.

name: Lomitapide (Juxtapid)
description: Oral microsomal triglyceride transfer protein inhibitor for homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, with a hepatic steatosis warning.

name: Lonafarnib (Zokinvy)
