description: A farnesyltransferase inhibitor and the only approved treatment for Hutchinson-Gilford progeria, preventing the farnesyl anchor that traps toxic progerin at the nuclear membrane.

name: Lonapegsomatropin
description: PEGylated long-acting prodrug of human growth hormone.

name: Loperamide
description: Over-the-counter antidiarrhoeal that is a potent mu agonist kept out of the brain by P-glycoprotein, and cardiotoxic when that is defeated.

name: Lopinavir
description: HIV protease inhibitor available only co-formulated with ritonavir, which is why the combination product is dosed as one drug.

name: Loratadine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL998).

name: Lorazepam
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL580).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Lorediplon
description: Lorediplon is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is gABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Lornoxicam
description: Short-half-life oxicam with potency comparable to ketorolac.

name: Losartan
description: The reference ARB, with the largest hypertension outcome dataset in the class (LIFE).

name: Loteprednol Etabonate
description: Ophthalmic ester corticosteroid designed to be inactivated rapidly in the eye, lowering the intraocular pressure risk.

name: Loteprednol Etabonate
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200865).

name: Lotiglipron
description: Oral small-molecule GLP-1 agonist discontinued after liver-enzyme concerns in development.

name: Lovastatin (Mevacor)
description: The first statin approved anywhere, a fungal natural product later found in red yeast rice.

name: Loxapine
description: D2-like dopamine receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL831).

name: LOXO-435
description: Investigational FGFR3-selective inhibitor for FGFR3-altered urothelial cancer; no skeletal programme reported.

name: Loxoprofen
description: Cyclooxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL19299).

name: Lubiprostone
description: Prostone chloride channel activator for chronic constipation, working through a channel rather than a receptor.

name: Lumacaftor
description: The first CFTR corrector. Its clinical usefulness was limited by modest efficacy and by strong CYP3A4 induction that undermined its own partner drug ivacaftor.

name: Lumateperone
description: Serotonin transporter inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL3306803).

name: Lumbrokinase
description: Earthworm-derived fibrinolytic enzyme supplement with uncertain product standardization and additive bleeding risk.

name: Lumefantrine
description: Long-acting partner drug to artemether, clearing residual parasites after the artemisinin has cleared the bulk.

name: Lumiracoxib
description: Cyclooxygenase-2 inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL404108).

name: Lurasidone
description: Antagonizes or partially agonizes dopamine D2 receptors; movement, metabolic, and prolactin effects depend on receptor profile.

name: Luspatercept
description: Transforming growth factor beta inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL3039545).

name: Lutein
description: Dietary xanthophyll concentrated in the macula, studied with zeaxanthin for progression of age-related macular degeneration rather than general anti-aging.

name: Luteolin
description: Dietary flavone with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activity in laboratory models; oral bioavailability is limited and clinical evidence is indication-specific.

name: Lutetium Oxodotreotide
description: Somatostatin receptor binding agent; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL4302409).

name: Lutropin Alfa
description: Luteinizing hormone/Choriogonadotropin receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201419).

name: Ly2452473
description: Ly2452473 is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is androgen Receptor modulator; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Lycopene
description: Tomato-derived carotenoid antioxidant studied for photoprotection and prostate/cardiometabolic outcomes; supplementation results are mixed.

name: Macimorelin (Macrilen)
description: Oral ghrelin receptor agonist approved as a diagnostic test, not a treatment.

name: Macitentan
description: Endothelin receptor, ET-A/ET-B antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2103873).

name: Madol (Desoxymethyltestosterone)
description: Designer steroid identified in doping control in 2005 rather than developed for clinical use. Orally active, never approved anywhere, and no human safety data exists.

name: Magnesium
description: Essential mineral studied for raising free and total testosterone, plausibly via competing with testosterone for SHBG binding, on top of its many other roles in enzymatic function.

name: Magnesium L-Threonate
description: A magnesium form selected for raising brain magnesium specifically, where common salts largely do not. Magnesium blocks the NMDA channel pore, which is the proposed synaptic-density mechanism.

name: Malathion
description: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200468).

name: Mapracorat
description: Mapracorat is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is glucocorticoid receptor agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Maprotiline
description: Inhibits norepinephrine reuptake, often alongside serotonin effects; blood pressure and discontinuation effects require attention.

name: Maralixibat
description: Ileal bile acid transporter inhibitor licensed for cholestatic pruritus in Alagille syndrome.

name: Maraviroc
description: Inhibits HIV integrase strand transfer as a component of combination antiretroviral therapy.

name: Maribavir
description: Oral CMV antiviral for refractory or resistant infection, inhibiting the same UL97 kinase that activates ganciclovir, which makes the two antagonistic.

name: Masoprocol
description: Insulin-like growth factor I receptor inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL313972).
mechanism: Insulin-like growth factor I receptor inhibitor

name: Matrixyl (Palmitoyl Pentapeptide-4)
description: Topical peptide (palmitoyl pentapeptide-4/-3) studied for stimulating dermal collagen and elastin synthesis to reduce wrinkle depth.

name: Mavacamten
description: Cardiac myosin inhibitor, the first disease-specific drug for obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and a genuine reversal of the pathophysiology.

name: Mavacoxib
description: Mavacoxib is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is cyclooxygenase-1 inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Mavrilimumab
description: GM-CSF receptor antibody investigated in rheumatoid arthritis and giant cell arteritis.

name: Mazdutide
description: Dual GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonist studied for obesity, developed primarily in China.

name: Mazindol
description: A tricyclic monoamine reuptake inhibitor formerly licensed as an anorectic and now in trials for narcolepsy and ADHD, with weaker reinforcing properties than the amphetamines.

name: MCC950
description: Selective NLRP3 inhibitor and the field's standard research tool; clinical development stopped over hepatotoxicity.

name: MDMA
description: A substituted amphetamine that reverses the serotonin transporter, releasing serotonin rather than merely blocking reuptake. Trialled as an adjunct in PTSD; the FDA declined approval in 2024 over trial conduct and functional unblinding.

name: Mebendazole
description: Benzimidazole for intestinal nematodes, poorly absorbed by design so it acts luminally with almost no systemic exposure.

name: Mecasermin (Increlex)
description: Recombinant IGF-1, used when growth failure doesn't respond to GH itself (e.g. GH receptor insensitivity); acts one step downstream of GH in the same axis.

name: Mecasermin Rinfabate
description: Insulin-like growth factor I receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201717).
mechanism: Insulin-like growth factor I receptor agonist

name: Meclizine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1623).

name: Meclofenamic Acid
description: Arachidonate 5-lipoxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL509).

name: Medi-6469
description: Medi-6469 is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 4 agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.
mechanism: tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 4 agonist

name: Medroxyprogesterone Acetate
description: Progesterone receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL717).

name: Medrysone
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201173).

name: Mefenamic Acid
description: Cyclooxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL686).

name: Mefloquine
description: Quinoline methanol for malaria prophylaxis in chloroquine-resistant areas, restricted by neuropsychiatric adverse effects.

name: Megestrol Acetate
description: Progesterone receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201139).

name: Melanotan II
description: Melanocortin receptor agonist peptide studied for UV-independent skin tanning via melanogenesis.

name: Melanotan II
description: A non-selective melanocortin agonist used unlicensed for tanning. Because it hits MC1R, MC3R and MC4R together, the pigmentation comes with nausea, spontaneous erections and appetite suppression; bremelanotide is the licensed MC4R-selective descendant.

name: Melarsoprol
description: Arsenical for late-stage African trypanosomiasis, formulated in propylene glycol and lethal to roughly one treated patient in twenty.

name: Topical melatonin solution
description: Topical scalp solution studied for extending hair follicle anagen phase in androgenetic and diffuse alopecia.

name: Melatonin (oral)
description: Pineal hormone sold as a supplement in the US and regulated as a prescription drug in much of Europe.

name: Meldonium
description: Carnitine-pathway metabolic modulator used in parts of Eastern Europe; prohibited by anti-doping authorities.

name: Meloxicam
description: Cyclooxygenase-2 inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL599).

name: Memantine (Namenda)
description: Low to moderate affinity, uncompetitive, voltage-dependent open-channel blocker of the NMDA glutamate receptor.

name: Menotropins (hMG, Menopur)
description: Human menopausal gonadotrophin: urinary FSH plus hCG-driven LH activity in roughly equal measure.

name: Pethidine (Meperidine)
description: Old synthetic opioid largely abandoned because its normeperidine metabolite is a proconvulsant that accumulates.

name: Mepivacaine
description: Amide local anaesthetic with intrinsic vasoconstrictor properties, so it works without added adrenaline.

name: Mepolizumab
description: Anti-IL-5 antibody for severe eosinophilic asthma, eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis and hypereosinophilic syndrome.

name: Meprednisone
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201148).

name: Meprobamate
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL979).

name: Mequinol
description: Tyrosinase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL544).

name: Mequitazine
description: Mequitazine is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is histamine H1 receptor antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Meropenem
description: Carbapenem with the broadest reliable gram-negative spectrum and good tolerability, and less epileptogenic than imipenem.

name: Mesalamine
description: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL704).

name: Mesalazine (5-ASA)
description: Topically acting anti-inflammatory for ulcerative colitis, delivered by formulation rather than by systemic absorption.

name: Proviron (Mesterolone)
description: Oral DHT derivative used to raise free testosterone via SHBG binding rather than for direct mass gain.

name: Mestranol
description: Estrogen receptor alpha agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201151).

name: Metamizole
description: Cyclooxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL461522).

name: Metaproterenol
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL776).

name: Metformin
description: First-line type 2 diabetes drug that activates AMPK and reduces hepatic glucose output; widely studied off-label for longevity given its AMPK/mTOR-opposing metabolic profile.

name: Methadone
description: Long-acting opioid used for maintenance therapy and for complex pain, with a half-life that varies tenfold between individuals.

name: Dianabol (Methandienone)
description: Fast-acting oral steroid, one of the original mass-building compounds, known for rapid strength/water-weight gain.

name: Methandrostenolone
description: Androgen Receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1418176).

name: Methapyrilene
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1411979).

name: Methaqualone
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL282052).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Metharbital
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL450).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Methazolamide
description: Inhibits carbonic anhydrase, lowering bicarbonate-dependent fluid secretion; metabolic acidosis and paraesthesia are the usual class effects.

name: Methdilazine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200959).

name: Primobolan (Methenolone)
description: Mild anabolic steroid with low androgenic activity, often used in cutting phases or by women.

name: Methimazole (Tapazole)
description: First-line thionamide antithyroid drug; blocks thyroid peroxidase and so blocks hormone synthesis.

name: Methohexital
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL7413).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Methotrexate
description: Antifolate used at cytotoxic doses in oncology and at a fraction of that weekly in rheumatology, where the mechanism is different.

name: Methoxsalen (8-MOP)
description: Psoralen given with ultraviolet A for psoriasis and vitiligo, forming DNA crosslinks only where light reaches.

name: Methoxy Polyethylene Glycol-Epoetin Beta
description: Erythropoietin receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL3707314).

name: Methoxyflurane
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1341).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive modulator

name: Methyl-1-Testosterone (M1T)
description: 17-alpha-alkylated designer steroid sold as a prohormone before scheduling. The alkylation that makes it orally active is also what makes it hepatotoxic.

name: Methyldopa (Aldomet)
description: Centrally acting alpha-2 agonist prodrug from the 1960s, kept in use almost entirely for its pregnancy safety record.

name: Methylene Blue
description: At low doses acts as an alternative mitochondrial electron carrier, bypassing damaged complexes. Genuinely interesting mechanism, essentially no controlled cognitive evidence, and a serotonin-syndrome risk with serotonergic drugs.

name: Methylene Blue
description: Redox dye acting as an alternative electron carrier at low dose; also a MAO-A inhibitor, so serotonin syndrome with serotonergic drugs is a real risk.

name: Methylnaltrexone
description: Quaternary opioid antagonist that cannot cross the blood-brain barrier, so it reverses constipation without reversing analgesia.

name: Methylphenidate (Ritalin / Concerta)
description: Blocks the dopamine and noradrenaline transporters. The best-evidenced cognitive effects in healthy adults are on recall, sustained attention and inhibitory control -- all small, and smaller than users believe.

name: Methylprednisolone Acetate
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1364144).

name: Methylprednisolone
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL650).

name: Methylprednisolone Hemisuccinate
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201265).

name: Methylpromazine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL829).

name: Methylstenbolone
description: Potent designer oral anabolic steroid sold during the prohormone era.

name: Methyltestosterone
description: 17-alpha-alkylated oral form of testosterone, largely obsolete today due to significant hepatotoxicity relative to newer compounds.

name: Methyltrienolone (R1881)
description: Synthetic androgen with no real clinical or performance use today -- exists purely as the standard reference ligand pharmacology labs use to measure androgen receptor binding, due to its resistance to metabolic breakdown.

name: Methyprylon
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200790).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Metipranolol
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1291).

name: Metoclopramide
description: Dopamine-antagonist antinausea/prokinetic drug; a well-documented side effect is raising prolactin, the opposite of what dopamine agonists like cabergoline do -- a real illustration of the same pathway working in both directions.

name: Metolazone
description: Thiazide-like diuretic used for resistant edema; electrolyte depletion and kidney injury are key monitoring concerns.

name: Metoprolol
description: The most commonly prescribed beta-1 selective blocker; effective on blood pressure, without nebivolol's endothelial effect.

name: Metreleptin
description: Recombinant leptin approved for generalized lipodystrophy, not routine obesity treatment.

name: Metronidazole
description: Nitroimidazole active only against organisms with an anaerobic reducing environment, covering anaerobic bacteria and several protozoa.

name: Topical Metronidazole
description: Topical antimicrobial/anti-inflammatory treatment for rosacea; not interchangeable with systemic metronidazole exposure.

name: Metyrapone (Metopirone)
description: Steroidogenesis inhibitor that blocks 11-beta-hydroxylase, the last step of cortisol synthesis.

name: Mexiletine
description: Modulates fast cardiac sodium channels to alter impulse conduction; proarrhythmia makes clinical supervision essential.

name: Mf101
description: Mf101 is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is estrogen receptor beta agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: MGF (Mechano Growth Factor)
description: A splice variant of IGF-1 expressed after mechanical loading; studied in cells and rodents only.

name: Mibavademab
description: Mibavademab is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is leptin receptor agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Mibolerone
description: Extremely potent veterinary anabolic steroid occasionally diverted for human doping use.

name: Micafungin
description: Echinocandin with no meaningful renal clearance and few drug interactions, widely used in critical care and in neonates.

name: Midazolam
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL655).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Mifepristone (Korlym/Mifeprex)
description: Glucocorticoid and progesterone receptor antagonist; blocks cortisol action rather than cortisol synthesis.

name: Migalastat
description: Oral pharmacological chaperone for Fabry disease, stabilising a patient's own mutant enzyme rather than replacing it.

name: Miglitol
description: An alpha-glucosidase inhibitor that, unlike acarbose, is systemically absorbed but excreted unchanged by the kidney. Same intestinal mechanism, different disposition and a slightly different tolerability profile.

name: Miglustat
description: Iminosugar substrate reduction therapy for Gaucher and Niemann-Pick type C, small enough to cross into the brain.

name: Milk Thistle (Silymarin)
description: Flavonoid complex from the milk thistle plant studied for liver protection, most robustly for preventing drug-induced liver injury.

name: Milnacipran
description: Inhibits norepinephrine reuptake, often alongside serotonin effects; blood pressure and discontinuation effects require attention.

name: Milrinone
description: Selective PDE3 inhibitor used intravenously as an inodilator in acute decompensated heart failure. Raises cardiac cAMP; the same mechanism drives its arrhythmia risk.

name: Miltefosine
description: The first oral treatment for visceral leishmaniasis, an alkylphosphocholine originally developed as an anticancer agent and strongly teratogenic.

name: Minaprine
description: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL278819).

name: Minocycline
description: Tetracycline antibiotic used for inflammatory acne; vestibular effects, pigmentation, autoimmune reactions, and antimicrobial stewardship limit long-term casual use.

name: Minoxidil
description: Topical potassium-channel opener applied twice daily to the scalp for androgenetic alopecia.

name: Minoxidil (oral, low dose)
description: The original systemic antihypertensive vasodilator, now used off-label at 0.25 to 5 mg for hair loss; NOT the topical scalp solution.

name: Mipomersen (Kynamro)
description: Antisense oligonucleotide against apolipoprotein B-100; approved in 2013 and later withdrawn from the market.

name: Mirikizumab
description: Neutralizes IL-23 signaling to suppress pathogenic Th17 maintenance in immune-mediated disease.

name: Mirodenafil
description: Inhibits PDE5 so nitric-oxide/cGMP vasodilation persists in corporal and pulmonary vascular smooth muscle; approved in South Korea.

name: Mirtazapine
description: Noradrenergic and specific serotonergic antidepressant that works by blocking autoreceptors rather than by inhibiting reuptake.

name: Misoprostol
description: PGE1 analogue used for NSAID ulcer prophylaxis and in obstetrics; uterotonic effect is the reason for its pregnancy contraindication.

name: Mitapivat (Pyrukynd)
description: An allosteric activator of erythrocyte pyruvate kinase that restores glycolytic ATP production. The first therapy for pyruvate kinase deficiency aimed at the enzyme defect itself.

name: MitoQ
description: Ubiquinone conjugated to triphenylphosphonium so it accumulates in mitochondria driven by membrane potential.

name: Mitotane
description: Adrenolytic drug for adrenocortical carcinoma that causes profound, persistent adrenal suppression.

name: Mizolastine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL94454).

name: Mizoribine
description: Imidazole nucleoside immunosuppressant used mainly in Japan, inhibiting the same purine route as mycophenolate with a better safety profile.

name: Mk-0767
description: Mk-0767 is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: MK-0773
description: SARM tested clinically for sarcopenia; lean-mass signals did not translate cleanly into functional benefit.

name: Mk-3577
description: Mk-3577 is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is glucagon receptor antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Mocetinostat
description: Class I/IV selective HDAC inhibitor, investigational.

name: Moclobemide
description: Inhibits monoamine oxidase to raise synaptic monoamines; selectivity and reversibility determine tyramine and serotonin-syndrome risk; reversible MAO-A inhibitor.

name: Modafinil (Provigil)
description: Wake-promoting agent structurally unrelated to the amphetamines. A weak dopamine transporter inhibitor that occupies roughly half of striatal DAT at normal doses -- the finding that complicates its reputation as having no abuse liability.

name: Moexipril
description: Blocks the renin–angiotensin system to reduce angiotensin-driven vasoconstriction or aldosterone signaling.

name: Mofarotene
description: Mofarotene is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is retinoid receptor modulator; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Mofezolac
description: Cyclooxygenase-1 inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL259972).

name: Molidustat
description: HIF-PHI approved in Japan for renal anaemia.

name: Molindone
description: Dihydroindolone antipsychotic notable for being weight-neutral or weight-reducing, unlike almost every other agent in the class.

name: Molnupiravir
description: Oral ribonucleoside prodrug that works by error catastrophe rather than chain termination, which is both its mechanism and its main safety concern.

name: Molsidomine
description: NO-donor prodrug converted to linsidomine (SIN-1). Unlike organic nitrates it does not require enzymatic bioactivation, so classical nitrate tolerance is less of an issue.

name: Momelotinib
description: Activin receptor type-1 inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1078178).

name: Mometasone Furoate
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1161).

name: Monobenzone
description: Tyrosinase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1388).

name: Montelukast (Singulair)
description: Leukotriene-receptor antagonist for asthma and allergic rhinitis carrying a boxed warning for serious neuropsychiatric effects.

name: Morphine
description: The reference opioid against which every other is measured, with an active glucuronide metabolite that accumulates in renal failure.

name: MOTS-c
description: Mitochondrial-derived peptide that activates AMPK, studied as an exercise-mimetic for metabolic health.

name: Moxidectin
description: Unknown; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2104415).

name: Moxifloxacin
description: Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase or topoisomerase IV; tendon, neurologic, cardiac, and resistance risks limit indiscriminate use.

name: Mozavaptan
description: Acts on vasopressin receptors to alter free-water handling or vascular tone; sodium shifts require monitoring; approved in Japan.

name: MSM (Methylsulfonylmethane)
description: Sulfur-containing compound studied for joint pain and as an anti-inflammatory/antioxidant, often stacked with glucosamine and chondroitin.

name: Mupirocin
description: Topical agent for staphylococcal impetigo and nasal MRSA decolonisation, with a target no systemic antibiotic shares.

name: Muraglitazar
description: Muraglitazar is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Mycophenolate Mofetil
description: Antiproliferative immunosuppressant that displaced azathioprine in transplantation, selective for lymphocytes because they cannot salvage purines.

name: N-Acetyl Semax Amidate
description: Modified Semax with terminal groups added to resist peptidases; sold as a nasal spray.

name: Nabilone
description: Synthetic cannabinoid analogue for refractory chemotherapy-induced nausea, more potent and longer acting than dronabinol.

name: Nabumetone
description: Cyclooxygenase-2 inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1070).

name: NAC (N-Acetylcysteine)
description: Glutathione precursor and antioxidant, the clinical antidote for acetaminophen overdose; studied for broader hepatoprotection against drug-induced liver injury.

name: Nadolol
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL521606).

name: Nadroparin
description: Low molecular weight heparin used widely in continental Europe for thromboprophylaxis and treatment.

name: Nafarelin
description: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201309).

name: Nafcillin
description: Antistaphylococcal penicillin resistant to staphylococcal penicillinase, hepatically cleared so usable in renal failure.

name: Naftidrofuryl (Naftidrofuryl Oxalate)
description: 5-HT2 antagonist and vasoactive drug used for intermittent claudication in some countries; improves walking distance but does not remove underlying vascular risk.

name: Naftifine
description: Disrupts fungal ergosterol synthesis or membrane function; interaction and organ-toxicity profiles differ substantially.

name: Nalbuphine
description: Mixed kappa agonist / mu antagonist with a ceiling on respiratory depression.

name: Nalfurafine
description: Kappa agonist approved in Japan for pruritus, engineered to minimise dysphoria.

name: Nalmefene
description: Longer-acting opioid antagonist used for overdose and for alcohol use disorder.

name: Naloxegol
description: PEGylated naloxone derivative for opioid-induced constipation, kept out of the brain by both its size and P-glycoprotein.

name: Naloxone
description: Short-acting opioid antagonist for overdose reversal; its half-life is shorter than most opioids, so re-narcotisation is a real risk.

name: Naltrexone
description: Opioid-receptor antagonist used for alcohol and opioid-use disorders and paired with bupropion for weight management; blocks opioid analgesia.

name: Namilumab
description: Neutralizes IL-23 signaling to suppress pathogenic Th17 maintenance in immune-mediated disease.

name: Nanaomycin A
description: A quinone antibiotic identified as the first DNMT3B-selective inhibitor, used to separate maintenance methylation by DNMT1 from de novo methylation experimentally.

name: Nanatinostat
description: Nanatinostat is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC2. ChEMBL records IC50 4.0 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: Deca (Nandrolone)
description: 19-nor injectable steroid valued for joint comfort and lean mass gain; long ester, long detection window.

name: Nandrolone Decanoate
description: Androgen Receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200946).

name: Nandrolone Phenpropionate
description: Androgen Receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200412).

name: NPP (Nandrolone Phenylpropionate)
description: Shorter-acting phenylpropionate ester of nandrolone; the same 19-nor hormone as Deca with a faster rise and clearance.

name: Naproxcinod
description: Naproxcinod is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is cyclooxygenase inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Naproxen
description: Cyclooxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL154).

name: Naratriptan
description: Slow-onset, long-half-life triptan with the lowest adverse effect burden, useful for slowly evolving or recurring attacks.

name: Narsoplimab
description: Inhibits a step of the complement cascade; blocking terminal complement raises encapsulated-organism risk and requires meningococcal vaccination; MASP-2 inhibitor, investigational.

name: Natalizumab
description: Anti-alpha-4-integrin antibody, highly effective in multiple sclerosis and defined by the risk of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy.

name: Nattokinase
description: Fermented-soy enzyme supplement marketed for fibrinolysis and blood pressure; clinical outcome evidence is limited and bleeding interactions are a concern.

name: Navafenterol
description: Navafenterol is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Navepegritide (TransCon CNP)
description: Once-weekly prodrug of C-type natriuretic peptide for achondroplasia. Sustained-release design addresses CNP's very short native half-life, and it is being trialled alongside lonapegsomatropin.

name: Navitoclax (ABT-263)
description: BCL-2 family inhibitor and a potent senolytic; dose-limiting thrombocytopenia stopped it as a cancer drug.

name: Nebivolol
description: Beta-1 selective blocker that also raises nitric oxide bioavailability, improving endothelial function rather than only lowering the number.

name: Necrostatin-1
description: RIPK1 inhibitor that defines necroptosis experimentally.

name: Nefazodone
description: Serotonin transporter inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL623).

name: Nefiracetam
description: Investigational racetam studied for cognitive impairment, with proposed cholinergic and glutamatergic effects. It has no established healthy-user benefit or approved nootropic use.

name: Nelivaptan
description: Acts on vasopressin receptors to alter free-water handling or vascular tone; sodium shifts require monitoring; investigational, discontinued.

name: Nemolizumab
description: Anti-IL-31-receptor antibody targeting itch specifically, used in prurigo nodularis and atopic dermatitis.

name: Neostigmine
description: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL278020).

name: Nepafenac
description: Cyclooxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1021).

name: Nesiritide
description: Recombinant human BNP given intravenously in acute decompensated heart failure. Large outcome trials were disappointing, and use has fallen away.

name: Netakimab
description: Blocks IL-17 ligand or receptor signaling to reduce neutrophil-dominant inflammation.

name: Netarsudil
description: Rho kinase inhibitor eye drop that lowers intraocular pressure by acting on the trabecular meshwork itself.

name: Netupitant
description: NK-1 antagonist co-formulated with palonosetron as a single oral capsule covering both emetic phases.

name: Nevirapine
description: First non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor, now restricted by hypersensitivity and hepatotoxicity that track CD4 count at initiation.

name: Nexturastat A
description: Nexturastat A is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC8. ChEMBL records IC50 954.0 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: Nezulcitinib
description: Nezulcitinib is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is janus Kinase (JAK) inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Niacin (Nicotinic Acid)
description: Vitamin B3 at pharmacologic doses alters lipids but commonly causes flushing, glucose disruption, and liver toxicity.

name: Niacin (extended-release)
description: Raises HDL more than anything else available -- and is the clearest evidence that raising HDL is not the same as reducing risk.

name: Niacinamide
description: Topical vitamin B3 derivative studied for strengthening the skin barrier and reducing hyperpigmentation.

name: Nicardipine
description: Dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker used orally and intravenously for blood-pressure control.

name: Niclosamide
description: Anticestodal salicylanilide that uncouples mitochondrial phosphorylation in the worm, now widely repurposed in oncology and metabolic research.

name: Nicorandil
description: Potassium-channel opener and nitrate-like antianginal; hypotension and serious mucosal ulceration are recognized risks.

name: Nicotinamide
description: The amide form of vitamin B3 and an NAD precursor that is also a direct product-inhibitor of the sirtuins and PARPs. That dual role is why very high doses can oppose the sirtuin activation that NAD-boosting is supposed to produce.

name: Nicotinamide (oral 500 mg, vitamin B3)
description: Oral vitamin B3 amide used for skin cancer chemoprevention; distinct from topical niacinamide and from niacin.

name: Nicotinamide Riboside (NR)
description: Another NAD+ precursor supplement, alternative to NMN, with human RCT data showing it safely raises NAD+ levels.

name: Nicotine
description: Nicotinic acetylcholine receptor agonist with genuine, replicated attentional effects, and the strongest dependence liability of anything in this section. The cognitive benefit is real and so is the addiction.

name: Nifedipine
description: The prototype dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker; the modern extended-release form is a different drug in practice from the old capsules.

name: Nifekalant
description: Alters cardiac repolarization through potassium-channel effects; QT prolongation and torsades risk vary by agent.

name: Nifurtimox
description: Nitrofuran for Chagas disease and, combined with eflornithine, for late-stage African trypanosomiasis.

name: Nilotinib
description: Inhibits BCR–ABL-family kinase signaling; mutation coverage and off-target cardiovascular risks differ by agent.

name: Niltubacin
description: Niltubacin is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC8. ChEMBL records Ki 750.0 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: Nilutamide (Nilandron)
description: First-generation androgen receptor antagonist with two side effects unique in its class.

name: Nimesulide
description: COX-2-preferential NSAID withdrawn in several countries over hepatotoxicity.

name: Nimodipine
description: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1428).

name: Niperotidine
description: Blocks parietal-cell H2 receptors to reduce stimulated gastric acid secretion; withdrawn over hepatotoxicity.

name: Nirmatrelvir
description: SARS-CoV-2 main protease inhibitor, given with ritonavir purely to keep its concentrations high enough to work.

name: Nitazoxanide
description: Thiazolide antiparasitic for cryptosporidiosis and giardiasis, with broad in vitro antiviral activity that has not translated cleanly.

name: Nitisinone
description: Enzyme inhibitor for hereditary tyrosinaemia type 1 that works by deliberately blocking a step upstream of the toxic metabolite.

name: Nitric Oxide
description: Soluble guanylate cyclase activator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200689).

name: Nitrofurantoin
description: Urinary-specific agent concentrated in urine but with negligible tissue levels, so it treats cystitis and never pyelonephritis.

name: Nitroglycerin
description: Rapid nitrate vasodilator for acute angina; severe hypotension can occur with PDE5 inhibitors or other vasodilators.

name: Nitroprusside
description: Soluble guanylate cyclase activator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2097081).

name: Nitrous Oxide
description: Inhaled anaesthetic and analgesic gas used since the nineteenth century, and the only common anaesthetic that irreversibly inactivates a vitamin.

name: Nivolumab
description: Anti-PD-1 antibody used alone and combined with ipilimumab, where the combination buys response rate at a substantial toxicity cost.

name: Nizatidine
description: Blocks parietal-cell H2 receptors to reduce stimulated gastric acid secretion.

name: NK-308
description: NK-308 is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC6. ChEMBL records Ki 28.0 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: NMN (Nicotinamide Mononucleotide)
description: NAD+ precursor supplement studied for raising cellular NAD+ levels, the cofactor sirtuins require to function; one of the most hyped current longevity supplements.

name: Nomegestrol Acetate
description: Progesterone receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1476022).

name: Nonivamide
description: Activates TRPV1 on nociceptive afferents, where sustained exposure defunctionalises the nerve terminal and produces lasting analgesia; synthetic capsaicin analogue.

name: Noopept
description: A dipeptide developed in Russia and often grouped with the racetams despite a different structure. Human data is almost entirely Russian-language and unreplicated elsewhere.

name: 19-Norandrostenedione
description: Direct nandrolone precursor; the usual explanation offered for a nandrolone doping positive.

name: Norbolethone
description: Designer anabolic steroid first identified through doping-detection research.

name: Norelgestromin
description: Progesterone receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200807).

name: Noradrenaline (Norepinephrine, IV)
description: The first-line vasopressor in septic shock, chosen over dopamine after trials showed fewer arrhythmias.

name: Norethandrolone (Nilevar)
description: The first widely marketed oral 19-nor anabolic; withdrawn after its hepatic and virilising profile became clear.

name: Norethindrone Acetate
description: Progesterone receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201146).

name: Norethindrone
description: Progesterone receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1162).

name: Norethynodrel
description: Progesterone receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1387).

name: Norfloxacin
description: Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase or topoisomerase IV; tendon, neurologic, cardiac, and resistance risks limit indiscriminate use.

name: Norgestimate
description: Progesterone receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200934).

name: Norgestrel
description: Progesterone receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2107797).

name: Nortriptyline
description: Serotonin transporter inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL445).

name: Norursodeoxycholic Acid
description: Investigational side-chain-shortened bile acid studied for cholestatic and metabolic liver disease.

name: NSI-189
description: Investigational neurogenic small molecule studied in depression trials; not approved and its precise molecular target remains unsettled.

name: Nusinersen (Spinraza)
description: An intrathecal antisense oligonucleotide that blocks an intronic splice silencer, forcing SMN2 exon 7 inclusion. The first disease-modifying treatment for spinal muscular atrophy.

name: Nystatin
description: Disrupts fungal ergosterol synthesis or membrane function; interaction and organ-toxicity profiles differ substantially.

name: Obatoclax
description: Pan-BCL-2 family inhibitor; development stopped over neurotoxicity and unclear on-target activity.

name: Obeticholic Acid (Ocaliva)
description: FXR agonist for cholestatic liver disease; carries a boxed warning for fatal dosing errors.

name: Obicetrapib
description: Late-stage oral CETP inhibitor, the fourth serious attempt at the target after torcetrapib, dalcetrapib and anacetrapib.

name: Obinutuzumab
description: Glycoengineered type II anti-CD20 with enhanced direct cell death and antibody-dependent killing, used in follicular lymphoma and lupus nephritis.

name: Ocrelizumab
description: Humanised anti-CD20 antibody and the first therapy to show benefit in primary progressive multiple sclerosis, which reframed the disease as B-cell driven.

name: Octocrylene
description: Organic UVB filter used mainly as a photostabiliser for avobenzone rather than for its own absorbance.

name: Octreotide
description: Somatostatin analog that suppresses growth hormone (and other hormone) secretion, used to treat acromegaly and GH-secreting tumors -- the pharmacological opposite of a GH secretagogue.

name: Odevixibat
description: Ileal bile acid transporter inhibitor for progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis, treating pruritus by interrupting enterohepatic recycling.

name: Ofatumumab
description: Fully human anti-CD20 given as a monthly subcutaneous injection in multiple sclerosis, binding a membrane-proximal epitope.

name: Ofloxacin
description: Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase or topoisomerase IV; tendon, neurologic, cardiac, and resistance risks limit indiscriminate use.

name: Oglemilast
description: Inhibits PDE4 to raise intracellular cAMP and dampen inflammatory cytokine production; emesis and weight loss are class-limiting; investigational.

name: Olanzapine
description: Antagonizes or partially agonizes dopamine D2 receptors; movement, metabolic, and prolactin effects depend on receptor profile.

name: Oleuropein
description: Major olive-leaf secoiridoid studied for vascular and metabolic signaling, mostly in preclinical work.

name: Olezarsen (Tryngolza)
description: GalNAc-conjugated antisense oligonucleotide against APOC3, approved for familial chylomicronaemia syndrome.

name: Oliceridine
description: G-protein-biased mu agonist intended to spare beta-arrestin signalling and reduce respiratory depression; the bias hypothesis remains contested.

name: Olinciguat
description: Oral sGC stimulator investigated in sickle cell disease, where the vasculopathy is partly NO-depletion driven.

name: Olive Leaf Extract
description: Oleuropein-rich botanical studied for modest blood-pressure and metabolic effects; standardization matters.

name: Olmesartan (Benicar)
description: Potent ARB carrying a distinctive warning about a sprue-like enteropathy.

name: Olmesartan Medoxomil
description: Type-1 angiotensin II receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200692).

name: Olodanrigan
description: Olodanrigan is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is angiotensin II type 2 (AT-2) receptor antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Olodaterol
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL605846).

name: Olokizumab
description: Blocks IL-17 ligand or receptor signaling to reduce neutrophil-dominant inflammation.

name: Olopatadine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1189432).

name: Olprinone
description: PDE3 inhibitor approved in Japan, with inotropic, vasodilator and bronchodilator effects.

name: Olsalazine
description: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL425).

name: Olvanil
description: Activates TRPV1 on nociceptive afferents, where sustained exposure defunctionalises the nerve terminal and produces lasting analgesia; research compound.

name: Olverembatinib
description: Inhibits BCR–ABL-family kinase signaling; mutation coverage and off-target cardiovascular risks differ by agent.

name: Omadacycline
description: Inhibits bacterial protein synthesis at the ribosome; spectrum, resistance, and toxicity are agent-specific.

name: Omalizumab (Xolair)
description: Anti-IgE monoclonal antibody for allergic asthma, chronic urticaria, and food-allergy risk reduction; injectable biologic with anaphylaxis precautions.

name: Omarigliptin
description: Inhibits DPP-4 to prolong endogenous incretin signaling and glucose-dependent insulin release.

name: Ombitasvir
description: Blocks an HCV replication target and is combined with complementary direct-acting antivirals to prevent resistance.

name: Omecamtiv Mecarbil
description: Cardiac myosin activator that raises stroke volume without raising intracellular calcium, tested in systolic heart failure.

name: Omega-3-Acid Ethyl Esters
description: Unknown; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200711).

name: Omega-3 Fatty Acids (Fish Oil)
description: Long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid supplement shown in an RCT to augment the muscle protein synthesis response to feeding, on top of its established anti-inflammatory and cardiovascular benefits.

name: Omeprazole
description: Inhibits the gastric proton pump to suppress acid secretion; long-term use affects micronutrient and mineral absorption.

name: Ondansetron
description: Antagonises 5-HT3 receptors on vagal afferents and in the area postrema; QT effects vary by agent.

name: Onercept
description: Neutralizes TNF or its receptor signaling to suppress systemic inflammation, increasing susceptibility to selected infections.

name: Ongericimab
description: Blocks PCSK9 so hepatic LDL receptors recycle instead of being degraded, lowering LDL-C and ApoB; approved in China.

name: Opigolix
description: Opigolix is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Oral Minoxidil
description: Systemic arteriolar vasodilator increasingly used off-label at low dose for hair loss; edema, tachycardia, and rare pericardial effects require caution.

name: Oral Tretinoin (ATRA)
aliases: All-trans retinoic acid; ATRA; Oral Tretinoin
description: Systemic retinoid used primarily for acute promyelocytic leukemia; fundamentally different risk and indication from topical tretinoin.

name: Orelabrutinib
description: Inhibits BTK to interrupt B-cell receptor signalling; covalent and reversible agents differ in kinase selectivity, bleeding and atrial-fibrillation risk; approved in China.

name: Orforglipron
description: Oral non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist, notable for not requiring injection.

name: Oritavancin
description: Lipoglycopeptide with three mechanisms rather than one, given as a single infusion for skin and soft tissue infection.

name: Orlistat (Xenical/Alli)
description: Gastrointestinal lipase inhibitor that reduces dietary-fat absorption; produces modest weight loss and can impair fat-soluble vitamin absorption.

name: Orn-0829 Hydrate
description: Orn-0829 Hydrate is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is orexin receptor antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: L-Ornithine L-Aspartate
description: Ammonia-lowering combination used in hepatic encephalopathy by supporting urea-cycle and glutamine handling.

name: L-Ornithine
description: Urea-cycle amino acid marketed for ammonia handling and recovery; standalone clinical evidence is limited.

name: Orphenadrine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL900).

name: Oseltamivir
description: Oral neuraminidase inhibitor for influenza, effective only if started within roughly 48 hours because it caps ongoing replication rather than clearing infected cells.

name: Osilodrostat (Isturisa)
description: Potent oral 11-beta-hydroxylase inhibitor approved for Cushing's disease and Cushing's syndrome.

name: Osimertinib
description: Inhibits oncogenic EGFR-family signaling; activity depends on tumor genotype and acquired resistance.

name: Ospemifene (Osphena)
description: Approved SERM with an unusual profile -- oestrogen agonist where most SERMs antagonise.

name: Ostabolin-C
description: Ostabolin-C is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is parathyroid hormone receptor agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Ostarine (MK-2866)
description: Selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) studied for muscle wasting, with milder side effects than steroids.

name: Otamixaban
description: Directly inhibits factor Xa to reduce thrombin generation; renal clearance and reversal-agent availability differ by agent; investigational, discontinued.

name: Oteseconazole
description: Tetrazole designed to avoid human CYP binding, approved for recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis with an exceptionally long half-life.

name: Ouabain (g-strophanthin)
description: The prototypical Na+/K+-ATPase inhibitor and the standard pharmacological tool for the pump. Also detectable as an endogenous steroid-like compound, which remains a contested area of physiology.

name: Oxabolone (Cipionate)
description: 4-hydroxylated nandrolone metabolite, sold in a handful of European markets as an injectable.

name: Oxaloacetate
description: TCA intermediate sold as a supplement for NAD+/NADH ratio and longevity claims that rest largely on invertebrate lifespan data.

name: Oxamflatin
description: Oxamflatin is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC3. ChEMBL records Ki 2.7 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: Anavar (Oxandrolone)
description: Mild oral anabolic steroid with a favorable anabolic-to-androgenic ratio, commonly used by both sexes.

name: Oxaprozin
description: Cyclooxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1071).

name: Oxazepam
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL568).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Oxcarbazepine
description: Reduces high-frequency neuronal firing through voltage-gated sodium-channel modulation.

name: Oxelumab
description: Oxelumab is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 4 inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.
mechanism: tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 4 inhibitor

name: Oxiracetam
description: A racetam marketed for memory, with the same weak evidence base and unconfirmed mechanism as the rest of the family.

name: Oxprenolol
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL546).

name: Oxybenzone
description: Broad organic UV filter whose systemic absorption and environmental persistence have made it the most controversial sunscreen ingredient.

name: Oxybutynin
description: Antagonises muscarinic receptors; peripheral selectivity determines how much dry mouth, constipation and central anticholinergic burden an agent carries; high central anticholinergic burden.

name: Oxycodone
description: Semi-synthetic opioid with high oral bioavailability, and the drug at the centre of the North American opioid epidemic.

name: Anadrol (Oxymetholone)
description: Strong oral steroid producing rapid mass and strength gains, with high hepatotoxicity and water retention.

name: Oxyphenbutazone Anhydrous
description: Cyclooxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1228).

name: Oxypurinol
description: Inhibits xanthine oxidoreductase to reduce urate production at its terminal synthetic step; active metabolite of allopurinol.

name: Oxytocin
description: Neuropeptide hormone increasingly studied for a direct role in muscle stem cell regeneration alongside its social/reproductive functions.

name: Ozanimod
description: Selective S1P1 and S1P5 modulator for multiple sclerosis and ulcerative colitis, designed to avoid the S1P3-mediated cardiac effects of fingolimod.

name: Ozarelix
description: Ozarelix is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Ozoralizumab
description: Neutralizes TNF or its receptor signaling to suppress systemic inflammation, increasing susceptibility to selected infections.

name: Pacritinib
description: Activin receptor type-1 inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2035187).

name: Paliperidone
description: Antagonizes or partially agonizes dopamine D2 receptors; movement, metabolic, and prolactin effects depend on receptor profile.

name: Palmitoyl Tripeptide-1 (Biopeptide CL)
description: Palmitoylated collagen-fragment tripeptide used topically to signal fibroblasts and stimulate collagen/elastin production, often paired with palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 in anti-aging formulations.

name: Palonosetron
description: Antagonises 5-HT3 receptors on vagal afferents and in the area postrema; QT effects vary by agent.

name: Palopegteriparatide
description: Parathyroid hormone receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL5095475).

name: Palovarotene
description: Retinoic acid receptor gamma agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2105648).

name: Paltusotine
description: Oral nonpeptide somatostatin receptor type 2 agonist developed for acromegaly.

name: Pamidronate (Aredia)
description: Second-generation intravenous nitrogen-containing bisphosphonate; a mainstay in paediatric OI.

name: Pancuronium
description: Long-acting steroidal relaxant with vagolytic and sympathomimetic effects, now used mainly where cost matters most.

name: Panobinostat
description: Potent pan-HDAC inhibitor used in myeloma with substantial toxicity.

name: Panthenol
description: Provitamin B5 used topically as a humectant to support skin barrier hydration.

name: Pantoprazole
description: Inhibits the gastric proton pump to suppress acid secretion; long-term use affects micronutrient and mineral absorption.

name: Papaverine
description: Inhibits PDE5 so nitric-oxide/cGMP vasodilation persists in corporal and pulmonary vascular smooth muscle; non-selective PDE inhibitor, intracavernosal use.

name: Paramethasone Acetate
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200342).

name: Parathyroid Hormone
description: Parathyroid hormone receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2108078).

name: Pardoprunox
description: Pardoprunox is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is dopamine receptors; D2 & D3 partial agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Parecoxib
description: Cyclooxygenase-2 inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1206690).

name: Pargyline
description: Inhibits monoamine oxidase to raise synaptic monoamines; selectivity and reversibility determine tyramine and serotonin-syndrome risk; withdrawn from clinical use.

name: Paricalcitol (Zemplar)
description: Selective vitamin D receptor activator designed to suppress PTH with less calcium and phosphate rise.

name: Paromomycin
description: Aminoglycoside given orally for luminal amoebiasis and by injection for visceral leishmaniasis, exploiting its near-zero absorption.

name: Paroxetine
description: Inhibits serotonin reuptake through SERT; benefits, activation, sexual effects, and withdrawal profiles differ by agent.

name: Pasireotide
description: Multi-receptor somatostatin analog used to control growth hormone and ACTH hypersecretion.

name: Patiromer
description: Potassium binding polymer that allows renin-angiotensin blockade to continue in patients who would otherwise become hyperkalaemic.

name: Patisiran (Onpattro)
description: A lipid-nanoparticle siRNA against transthyretin mRNA, the first RNAi therapeutic ever approved. It lowers circulating TTR by around 80%.

name: Pazopanib
description: Inhibits VEGF-receptor angiogenic signaling; hypertension, bleeding, thrombosis, and wound-healing effects require monitoring.

name: Pefcalcitol
description: Pefcalcitol is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is vitamin D receptor agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Peficitinib
description: Janus Kinase (JAK) inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL3137308).

name: PEG-MGF
description: MGF with a polyethylene glycol chain attached to slow clearance; no published human data either.

name: Pegcetacoplan
description: Inhibits a step of the complement cascade; blocking terminal complement raises encapsulated-organism risk and requires meningococcal vaccination; C3 inhibitor.

name: Peginesatide
description: Erythropoietin receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2107866).

name: Pegnivacogin
description: Pegnivacogin is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is coagulation factor IX inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Pegozafermin
description: A glycopegylated FGF21 analogue engineered for a longer half-life, in late-stage trials for steatohepatitis and severe hypertriglyceridaemia.

name: Pegvisomant (Somavert)
description: Pegylated GH receptor antagonist that blocks GH from signaling at its own receptor, used when acromegaly doesn't respond to somatostatin analogs.

name: Pelacarsen
description: Investigational antisense therapy targeting apolipoprotein(a) to lower lipoprotein(a); outcomes benefit remains under study.

name: Pemafibrate (Parmodia)
description: Selective PPAR-alpha modulator, marketed in Japan, and the drug that tested the triglyceride hypothesis directly.

name: Pembrolizumab
description: Anti-PD-1 antibody and the archetype of checkpoint blockade, effective across many tumour types and defined by immune-related toxicity.

name: Pemetrexed (Alimta)
description: A multitargeted antifolate hitting thymidylate synthase, dihydrofolate reductase and GARFT. Mandatory folate and B12 supplementation cuts its haematological toxicity without reducing efficacy.

name: Pemazyre (Pemigatinib)
description: Oral FGFR1-3 inhibitor approved for FGFR2-fusion cholangiocarcinoma; FGFR3 activity is incidental to its approved use.

name: Pemvidutide
description: Investigational GLP-1/glucagon co-agonist for obesity and steatohepatitis.

name: Penbutolol
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1290).

name: Penicillamine
description: Chelator for Wilson disease and cystinuria, also used historically in rheumatoid arthritis, with a long list of autoimmune adverse effects.

name: Pentaerythritol Tetranitrate
description: Pentaerythritol Tetranitrate is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is soluble guanylate cyclase activator; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Pentamidine
description: Aromatic diamidine for Pneumocystis and trypanosomiasis, with a striking dual effect on the pancreatic beta cell.

name: Pentazocine
description: Benzomorphan kappa agonist; its psychotomimetic effects are the classic illustration of kappa signalling.

name: Pentobarbital
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL448).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Pentosan Polysulfate (Elmiron)
description: Semisynthetic heparinoid used for interstitial cystitis and, off-label, as a joint agent. Carries a well-documented and often-missed long-term risk.

name: Pentoxifylline
description: Methylxanthine hemorheologic drug used for intermittent claudication. Benefits are modest and evidence is weaker than for structured exercise or cilostazol.

name: Perakizumab
description: Blocks IL-17 ligand or receptor signaling to reduce neutrophil-dominant inflammation.

name: Peramivir
description: Single-dose intravenous neuraminidase inhibitor for patients who cannot take oral or inhaled therapy.

name: Perampanel
description: Selective non-competitive AMPA receptor antagonist, the first of its class, carrying a boxed warning for aggression.

name: Pergolide
description: Dopamine receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL531).

name: Perhexiline
description: Carnitine O-palmitoyltransferase 1, muscle isoform inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL75880).

name: Perindopril (Aceon)
description: Long-acting ACE inhibitor, usually seen in fixed combination with indapamide or amlodipine.

name: Perphenazine
description: Mid-potency phenothiazine that performed as well as the second-generation drugs in the CATIE effectiveness trial.

name: Petrelintide
description: Long-acting amylin analogue being tested as a GLP-1 alternative rather than an add-on.

name: Pf-00489791
description: Pf-00489791 is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is phosphodiesterase 5A inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Pf-00610355
description: Pf-00610355 is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Pf-4191834
description: Pf-4191834 is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is arachidonate 5-lipoxygenase inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Pf-5190457
description: Pf-5190457 is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is ghrelin receptor inverse agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Phenacetin
description: Unknown; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL16073).

name: Phendimetrazine
description: Norepinephrine transporter inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1615439).

name: Phenelzine
description: Inhibits monoamine oxidase to raise synaptic monoamines; selectivity and reversibility determine tyramine and serotonin-syndrome risk; irreversible non-selective, requires tyramine restriction.

name: Pheneturide
description: Obsolete phenylacetylurea anticonvulsant, retained mainly as a historical comparator to phenytoin and phenobarbital.

name: Phenformin
description: Unknown; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL170988).

name: Phenindione
description: Inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase so clotting factors are undercarboxylated; effect is delayed, diet-sensitive and needs INR monitoring; largely superseded over hypersensitivity.

name: Pheniramine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1193).

name: Phenmetrazine
description: Norepinephrine transporter inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201208).

name: Phenobarbital
description: The oldest anticonvulsant still in use, a barbiturate that remains first-line for neonatal seizures and in low-resource settings.

name: Phenoxybenzamine
description: Blocks alpha-1 adrenoceptors to relax vascular or prostatic smooth muscle; first-dose hypotension and floppy-iris syndrome are class effects; irreversible, phaeochromocytoma use.

name: Phenprocoumon
description: Inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase so clotting factors are undercarboxylated; effect is delayed, diet-sensitive and needs INR monitoring; longer half-life, used in Europe.

name: Phentermine
description: FDA-approved sympathomimetic appetite suppressant, most often prescribed combined with topiramate (Qsymia); the CONQUER trial found real, substantial weight loss and metabolic risk-factor improvement in a large randomized trial.

name: Phentolamine
description: Blocks alpha-1 adrenoceptors to relax vascular or prostatic smooth muscle; first-dose hypotension and floppy-iris syndrome are class effects; non-selective, reversible.

name: Phenylbutazone
description: Cyclooxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL101).

name: Phenylbutyrylhydroxamic Acid
description: Phenylbutyrylhydroxamic Acid is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC6. ChEMBL records Ki 150.0 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: Phenylephrine
description: Pure alpha-1 agonist used as a vasopressor, a mydriatic and a decongestant, though its oral decongestant efficacy is now doubted.

name: Phenylpiracetam (Phenotropil)
description: A phenylated racetam with stimulant character and reported dopamine transporter affinity. Banned by WADA, which is a stronger signal that it does something than its trial record is.

name: Phenylpropanolamine
description: Norepinephrine transporter releasing agent; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL61006).

name: Phenytoin
description: Reduces high-frequency neuronal firing through voltage-gated sodium-channel modulation.

name: Phosphatidic Acid
description: Membrane lipid and signaling intermediate studied as an mTOR-linked resistance-training supplement; trials are small and product-specific.

name: Phosphatidylcholine
description: Membrane phospholipid and choline source used in nutrition and liver research; injectable cosmetic use has separate risks.

name: Phosphatidylserine
description: Phospholipid supplement studied for blunting the cortisol spike from intense exercise, marketed as a recovery aid for people training hard enough to be chronically overstressed.

name: Physostigmine
description: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL94).

name: Pibrentasvir
description: Blocks an HCV replication target and is combined with complementary direct-acting antivirals to prevent resistance.

name: Piclamilast
description: Inhibits PDE4 to raise intracellular cAMP and dampen inflammatory cytokine production; emesis and weight loss are class-limiting; research tool compound.

name: Pilocarpine
description: Muscarinic agonist used as a miotic in glaucoma, as an oral treatment for xerostomia, and now topically for presbyopia.

name: Pilsicainide
description: Modulates fast cardiac sodium channels to alter impulse conduction; proarrhythmia makes clinical supervision essential.

name: Pimavanserin
description: Selective 5-HT2A inverse agonist for Parkinson disease psychosis, treating psychosis without any dopamine receptor blockade.

name: Pimecrolimus
description: Topical calcineurin inhibitor for atopic dermatitis, used on face and flexures where steroid atrophy is a concern.

name: Pimobendan
description: PDE3 inhibitor that is also a calcium sensitiser, so it raises contractility at lower cAMP cost than pure PDE3 agents. Mostly veterinary cardiology now.

name: Pimozide
description: Dopamine receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1423).

name: Pindolol
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor partial agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL500).

name: Pinealon
description: Three-amino-acid 'bioregulator' from the Russian peptide programme; effectively no Western literature.

name: Pioglitazone (Actos)
description: PPAR-gamma agonist ('insulin sensitizer') that improves glycemic control and lipid profiles in type 2 diabetes; a distinct mechanism from metformin or SGLT2 inhibitors.

name: Piperacillin
description: Ureidopenicillin with antipseudomonal activity, used almost exclusively combined with tazobactam. A mainstay of empirical therapy for hospital-acquired sepsis and neutropenic fever.

name: Piperaquine
description: Bisquinoline partner drug used with dihydroartemisinin, effective but with a dose-dependent QT signal.

name: Piperazine Citrate Anhydrous
description: Nematode GABA-A receptor positive modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL3990694).

name: Piperine (Black Pepper Extract)
description: Bioavailability enhancer that inhibits metabolic enzymes and transporters, making interactions—not fat loss—its most important stack property.

name: Piperlongumine
description: Long pepper alkaloid with senolytic and pro-oxidant activity in vitro; no clinical data.

name: Piracetam
description: The original racetam and the compound the category is named after. A cyclic GABA derivative with no confirmed receptor target after fifty years; not approved in the United States.

name: Pirbuterol
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1094966).

name: Piroctone Olamine
description: Antifungal shampoo agent used where ketoconazole is unavailable or poorly tolerated.

name: Piromelatine
description: Agonises MT1/MT2 receptors to shift circadian phase and shorten sleep latency; investigational.

name: Piroxicam
description: Cyclooxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL527).

name: Pirprofen
description: Cyclooxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL188952).

name: Pirtobrutinib
description: Inhibits BTK to interrupt B-cell receptor signalling; covalent and reversible agents differ in kinase selectivity, bleeding and atrial-fibrillation risk; non-covalent, active against C481S.

name: Pitavastatin (Livalo)
description: Statin with minimal cytochrome P450 metabolism, dosed at 1 to 4 mg.

name: Pitolisant (Wakix)
description: Histamine H3 inverse agonist for narcolepsy. Promotes wakefulness by raising central histamine rather than through dopamine, so it is non-scheduled.

name: Plant sterols / stanols
description: Cholesterol look-alikes that compete for absorption; stanols outperform sterols by roughly two to one.

name: Plazomicin
description: Next-generation aminoglycoside engineered against modifying enzymes, approved for complicated urinary infection caused by resistant Enterobacterales.

name: Plecanatide
description: Uroguanylin analogue with pH-dependent activity, so it acts preferentially in the proximal small bowel.

name: Policosanol
description: Sugarcane-wax alcohol supplement marketed for cholesterol; independent trials have produced inconsistent results.

name: Polyestradiol Phosphate
description: Estrogen receptor alpha agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201477).

name: Polymyxin B
description: The other clinical polymyxin, differing from colistin mainly in being given as active drug rather than as a prodrug, which makes its pharmacokinetics more predictable.

name: Polypodium Leucotomos
description: Fern-derived oral supplement studied as an adjunct photoprotectant against UV skin damage.

name: Pomalidomide
description: Third-generation IMiD active in myeloma refractory to lenalidomide and bortezomib, and used in Kaposi sarcoma.

name: Ponalrestat
description: Inhibits aldose reductase to limit polyol-pathway flux and the osmotic and oxidative stress it imposes during hyperglycaemia; development discontinued.

name: Ponatinib
description: Inhibits BCR–ABL-family kinase signaling; mutation coverage and off-target cardiovascular risks differ by agent.

name: Posaconazole
description: Disrupts fungal ergosterol synthesis or membrane function; interaction and organ-toxicity profiles differ substantially.

name: Potassium
description: Dietary mineral with a modest, well-replicated blood pressure effect -- and a genuine ceiling above which more does nothing.

name: Potassium Iodide (SSKI/KI)
description: Pharmacologic iodide; transiently shuts down thyroid hormone release through the Wolff-Chaikoff effect.

name: Potassium Perchlorate
description: Competitive NIS inhibitor used for amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis and in the perchlorate discharge test.

name: Pracinostat
description: An oral hydroxamate pan-HDAC inhibitor trialled with azacitidine in acute myeloid leukaemia on the rationale that HDAC and DNMT inhibition are complementary; the phase 3 combination did not confirm the phase 2 signal.

name: Praliciguat
description: Oral sGC stimulator studied in diabetic nephropathy, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and peripheral artery disease. Stimulators need functional haem — they amplify NO rather than replacing it.

name: Pralidoxime
description: Acetylcholinesterase activator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1420).

name: Pramipexole (Mirapex)
description: Non-ergoline dopamine agonist with D3 receptor preference; used in Parkinson's disease and restless legs syndrome.

name: Pramiracetam
description: The most lipophilic and, by weight, most potent racetam, reported to enhance high-affinity choline uptake. Human evidence is limited to small trials in brain injury and dementia.

name: Pramlintide (Symlin)
description: Synthetic amylin analog used alongside insulin in diabetes, slows gastric emptying and increases satiety through amylin receptor signaling.

name: Pranlukast
description: Cysteinyl leukotriene receptor 1 antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL21333).

name: Prasugrel (Effient)
description: Potent irreversible P2Y12 inhibitor used around coronary intervention, with greater bleeding risk in specific populations.

name: Pravastatin (Pravachol)
description: Hydrophilic statin, given in the active acid form and largely spared from CYP3A4 interactions.

name: Prazepam
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL969).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Praziquantel
