description: The single drug behind schistosomiasis control worldwide, acting on a calcium channel subunit unique to flatworms.

name: Prazosin (Minipress)
description: The original selective alpha-1 blocker; now used more for PTSD nightmares and phaeochromocytoma than for hypertension.

name: Prednicarbate
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200386).

name: Prednisolone Acetate
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1152).

name: Prednisolone
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL131).

name: Prednisolone Phosphoric Acid
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201231).

name: Prednisolone Tebutate
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200909).

name: Prednisone
description: Oral glucocorticoid prodrug converted to prednisolone in the liver; the workhorse anti-inflammatory steroid.

name: Pregabalin
description: Alpha-2-delta ligand with linear pharmacokinetics, licensed for neuropathic pain, generalised anxiety and fibromyalgia, and now a controlled drug in several countries.

name: Pregnenolone
description: Upstream neurosteroid and precursor to progesterone, cortisol, and androgens; supplement effects are unpredictable because metabolism branches across several hormone pathways.

name: Pretomanid
description: Nitroimidazooxazine used in the six-month all-oral BPaL regimen for extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis.

name: Pridopidine
description: Engages the sigma-1 chaperone at the ER-mitochondrial interface, modulating calcium handling and ER stress responses; investigational.

name: Prilocaine
description: Amide local anaesthetic with the lowest systemic toxicity of the class, but a metabolite that causes methaemoglobinaemia.

name: Primaquine
description: The only widely available drug that clears the hepatic hypnozoites of vivax and ovale malaria, and the classic G6PD hazard.

name: Primidone
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL856).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: PRL-8-53
description: Experimental benzoic-acid derivative associated with one small 1970s human memory study; its mechanism, safety, and reproducibility remain uncertain.

name: Probenecid
description: Blocks proximal-tubule urate reabsorption to raise fractional urate excretion; urine volume and stone risk need attention.

name: Probucol
description: Legacy lipid-lowering antioxidant that lowers LDL and HDL and can prolong QT; withdrawn in several markets.

name: Procainamide
description: Modulates fast cardiac sodium channels to alter impulse conduction; proarrhythmia makes clinical supervision essential.

name: Procaine
description: An ester local anaesthetic that also binds CpG-rich DNA and inhibits DNA methyltransferase, producing demethylation in cancer cell lines. The concentrations required are far above anaesthetic ones, so it is a mechanistic curiosity rather than a therapy.

name: Procaterol
description: Procaterol is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Progesterone (micronised)
description: The native C21 progestogen; endometrial secretory transformation and luteal phase support.

name: Proguanil
description: Biguanide prodrug whose active metabolite is an antifolate, paired with atovaquone for prophylaxis and treatment.

name: Promazine
description: D2-like dopamine receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL564).

name: Promethazine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL643).

name: Pronetalol
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL16476).

name: Propafenone
description: Modulates fast cardiac sodium channels to alter impulse conduction; proarrhythmia makes clinical supervision essential.

name: Propanidid
description: Butyrylcholinesterase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2105345).

name: Propentofylline
description: Xanthine derivative studied for vascular dementia, acting through adenosine reuptake inhibition and PDE inhibition on glial cells. Never approved for that indication.

name: Propiomazine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201210).

name: Propiverine
description: Antagonises muscarinic receptors; peripheral selectivity determines how much dry mouth, constipation and central anticholinergic burden an agent carries.

name: Propofol
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL526).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Propranolol
description: Classic non-selective beta-blocker; blocks rather than activates beta-adrenergic receptors, the exact opposite mechanism from beta-agonists like clenbuterol -- used clinically to reduce physical tremor and performance anxiety.

name: Propylthiouracil (PTU)
description: Older thionamide that also blocks peripheral T4 to T3 conversion; now reserved because of hepatotoxicity.

name: Prostanozol
description: Stanozolol-related designer steroid; the subject of a landmark US enforcement case over supplement mislabelling.

name: Protamine Sulfate
description: Heparin antidote, a strongly cationic peptide that neutralises heparin by direct charge interaction, and itself an anticoagulant if overdosed.

name: Protokylol
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201273).

name: Protriptyline
description: Inhibits norepinephrine reuptake, often alongside serotonin effects; blood pressure and discontinuation effects require attention.

name: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP)
description: Autologous platelet concentrate injected into the scalp as an androgenetic alopecia treatment.

name: Prucalopride
description: Selective 5-HT4 agonist for chronic constipation; selectivity avoids the cardiac risk that withdrew earlier agents.

name: Prulifloxacin
description: Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase or topoisomerase IV; tendon, neurologic, cardiac, and resistance risks limit indiscriminate use.

name: Pruxelutamide
description: Pruxelutamide is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is androgen Receptor antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Pseudoephedrine
description: Norepinephrine transporter releasing agent; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1590).

name: Psilocybin
description: A prodrug dephosphorylated to psilocin, a 5-HT2A agonist. Trials in treatment-resistant depression show large short-term effects, though blinding is essentially impossible, which is the central methodological problem in this field.

name: Psyllium husk
description: Viscous soluble fibre with a real, meta-analysed LDL and apoB reduction at about 10g a day.

name: PT-141 (Bremelanotide)
description: Melanocortin receptor agonist peptide, FDA-approved for low sexual desire, acting centrally rather than vascularly.

name: Pterostilbene
description: Dimethylated resveratrol analogue; better absorbed, and it raises LDL in the human trial.

name: Pumpkin Seed Oil
description: Botanical extract with mild antiandrogen activity, studied as an adjunct hair-loss treatment.

name: Pycnogenol
description: Standardized maritime pine-bark extract studied for endothelial and venous outcomes; effects are generally modest.

name: Pyrantel Pamoate
description: Depolarising neuromuscular blocker for the worm, causing spastic paralysis, which is why it must not be combined with piperazine.

name: Pyrazinamide
description: The sterilising drug of short-course tuberculosis therapy, active only at acid pH inside the phagosome, which is why it shortened treatment from nine months to six.

name: Pyridostigmine (Mestinon)
description: Quaternary ammonium cholinesterase inhibitor that stays outside the brain by design; first-line symptomatic treatment for myasthenia gravis.

name: Pyrilamine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL511).

name: Pyrilutamide (KX-826)
description: Topical antiandrogen in clinical trials for hair loss; results so far have been mixed.

name: Pyrimethamine
description: Antifolate for toxoplasmosis and, historically, malaria, always given with folinic acid rescue to protect the host marrow.

name: Pyroxamide
description: Pyroxamide is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC6. ChEMBL records Ki 4.8 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: Quazepam
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200472).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Quercetin
description: Flavonoid studied as a senolytic (typically paired with dasatinib) that selectively clears senescent cells; also has general antioxidant properties.

name: Quetiapine
description: Antagonizes or partially agonizes dopamine D2 receptors; movement, metabolic, and prolactin effects depend on receptor profile.

name: Quinagolide (Norprolac)
description: Non-ergot dopamine D2 agonist for hyperprolactinaemia; never marketed in the United States.

name: Quinapril
description: ACE inhibitor formerly used for hypertension and heart failure; monitor potassium and renal function.

name: Quinbolone (Anabolicum)
description: Orally active boldenone enol ether from the 1960s, marketed in Italy and long discontinued. Notable for being non-17-alkylated, so it lacks the hepatotoxicity of oral steroids that are.

name: Quinestrol
description: Estrogen receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201165).

name: Quinidine
description: Modulates fast cardiac sodium channels to alter impulse conduction; proarrhythmia makes clinical supervision essential.

name: Quinine
description: The original antimalarial, still used for severe falciparum malaria and misused for leg cramps, with a well-characterised toxidrome.

name: Quinupristin / Dalfopristin
description: Streptogramin combination reserved for vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium, notable for infusion-site phlebitis and severe arthralgia.

name: Quisinostat
description: A second-generation hydroxamate with unusually high potency against HDAC1, allowing weekly rather than daily dosing.

name: Quisovalimab
description: Quisovalimab is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 14 inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.
mechanism: tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 14 inhibitor

name: R-306465
description: R-306465 is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC11. ChEMBL records IC50 2.1 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: Rabeprazole
description: Inhibits the gastric proton pump to suppress acid secretion; long-term use affects micronutrient and mineral absorption.

name: Ractopamine
description: Beta-adrenergic growth promoter used in livestock feed and banned for that use in the EU, China and elsewhere. Not a human medicine; human exposure is dietary or deliberate misuse.

name: RAD-140 (Testolone)
description: Investigational SARM with high androgen receptor affinity in muscle and bone tissue.

name: RAD-150 (TLB-150)
description: An ester of RAD-140 sold as a distinct product; the pharmacology is its parent's, with no data of its own.

name: Radiprodil
description: Radiprodil is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is glutamate NMDA receptor; GRIN1/GRIN2B antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Radotinib
description: Inhibits BCR–ABL-family kinase signaling; mutation coverage and off-target cardiovascular risks differ by agent.

name: Ragifilimab
description: Ragifilimab is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 18 agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.
mechanism: tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 18 agonist

name: Ralfinamide
description: Reduces high-frequency neuronal firing through voltage-gated sodium-channel modulation.

name: Raloxifene (Evista)
description: Selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) that mimics estrogen's bone-protective effect without stimulating breast or uterine tissue, used for osteoporosis.

name: Raltegravir
description: Inhibits HIV integrase strand transfer as a component of combination antiretroviral therapy.

name: Ramatroban
description: Dual thromboxane TP and CRTH2 antagonist marketed in Japan for allergic rhinitis.

name: Ramelteon (Rozerem)
description: MT1/MT2 melatonin-receptor agonist approved for sleep-onset insomnia, non-controlled and generally less impairing than GABAergic hypnotics.

name: Ramipril (Altace)
description: ACE inhibitor whose cardiovascular prevention trial changed how the class is prescribed.

name: Ramosetron
description: Antagonises 5-HT3 receptors on vagal afferents and in the area postrema; QT effects vary by agent; approved in Japan.

name: Ranirestat
description: Inhibits aldose reductase to limit polyol-pathway flux and the osmotic and oxidative stress it imposes during hyperglycaemia; investigational.

name: Ranitidine
description: Blocks parietal-cell H2 receptors to reduce stimulated gastric acid secretion; withdrawn in many markets over NDMA contamination.

name: Ranolazine (Ranexa)
description: Antianginal that inhibits the late sodium current, working without lowering heart rate or blood pressure.

name: Rapamycin (Sirolimus)
description: The namesake mTOR inhibitor, originally an immunosuppressant, studied extensively in longevity research for its ability to slow age-related decline via mTOR suppression.

name: Rasagiline (Azilect)
description: Selective irreversible MAO-B inhibitor of the propargylamine class, given once daily for Parkinson's disease.

name: Rasburicase
description: Recombinant urate oxidase that converts uric acid to soluble allantoin, used for tumour lysis syndrome.

name: Ravulizumab
description: Inhibits a step of the complement cascade; blocking terminal complement raises encapsulated-organism risk and requires meningococcal vaccination; long-acting C5 inhibitor.

name: Rebastinib
description: Inhibits BCR–ABL-family kinase signaling; mutation coverage and off-target cardiovascular risks differ by agent.

name: Reboxetine
description: Inhibits norepinephrine reuptake, often alongside serotonin effects; blood pressure and discontinuation effects require attention.

name: Recaticimab
description: Blocks PCSK9 so hepatic LDL receptors recycle instead of being degraded, lowering LDL-C and ApoB; investigational.

name: Recifercept (PF-07256472)
description: Soluble FGFR3 decoy that sequesters FGF ligands before they reach the receptor; a ligand trap rather than a kinase inhibitor.

name: Red Yeast Rice
description: Fermented rice supplement containing natural monacolin K (chemically identical to lovastatin); the most consistently evidenced OTC option for meaningfully lowering LDL cholesterol.

name: Relacorilant
description: Selective glucocorticoid-receptor modulator developed for hypercortisolism without progesterone antagonism.

name: Relamorelin
description: Investigational ghrelin-receptor agonist studied for diabetic gastroparesis and gastrointestinal motility.

name: Relatlimab
description: Anti-LAG-3 antibody, the third checkpoint class to reach approval, used with nivolumab in melanoma.

name: Relcovaptan
description: Acts on vasopressin receptors to alter free-water handling or vascular tone; sodium shifts require monitoring; investigational.

name: Relebactam
description: Diazabicyclooctane inhibitor paired with imipenem-cilastatin for carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales and difficult Pseudomonas.

name: Relugolix (Orgovyx)
description: Oral GnRH receptor antagonist approved for advanced prostate cancer; rapidly and profoundly suppresses LH and testosterone and is not post-cycle therapy.

name: Remdesivir
description: Adenosine analogue prodrug given intravenously for COVID-19, the first antiviral shown to shorten recovery time in that disease.

name: Remibrutinib
description: Inhibits BTK to interrupt B-cell receptor signalling; covalent and reversible agents differ in kinase selectivity, bleeding and atrial-fibrillation risk; investigational.

name: Remifentanil
description: Ultra-short-acting opioid cleared by non-specific plasma esterases, so its context-sensitive half-time stays constant however long it is infused.

name: Remimazolam
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL4297526).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Remoxipride
description: Dopamine D2 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL22242).

name: Resequinil
description: Resequinil is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is gABA-A receptor; anion channel inverse agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Reserpine
description: Rauwolfia alkaloid, the first effective antihypertensive and the drug whose depressive effect founded the monoamine hypothesis of depression.

name: Resiniferatoxin
description: Activates TRPV1 on nociceptive afferents, where sustained exposure defunctionalises the nerve terminal and produces lasting analgesia; ultrapotent agonist, investigational.

name: Reslizumab
description: Intravenous anti-IL-5 antibody dosed by weight, used in severe eosinophilic asthma where the subcutaneous agents are insufficient.

name: Resmetirom (Rezdiffra)
description: Liver-targeted thyroid hormone receptor-beta agonist; the first drug approved for NASH.

name: Resminostat
description: An oral hydroxamate pan-HDAC inhibitor investigated in hepatocellular carcinoma and cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

name: Resocortol Butyrate
description: Resocortol Butyrate is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is glucocorticoid receptor agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Resveratrol
description: Plant polyphenol studied as a sirtuin (SIRT1) activator and mitochondrial function booster, the compound that popularized the sirtuin-longevity research area.

name: Retatrutide
description: Triple GIP/GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonist in obesity trials, the most potent incretin-class weight loss agent reported to date.

name: Reteplase
description: Deletion mutant of tPA given as a double bolus.

name: Retigabine (Ezogabine)
description: Withdrawn Kv7 channel opener, the first anticonvulsant with that mechanism, retired for blue skin and retinal pigment deposits.

name: Retinaldehyde
description: Retinoid intermediate between retinol and tretinoin, offering more potency than retinol with less irritation than tretinoin.

name: Retinol
description: Over-the-counter vitamin A derivative and gentler alternative to prescription tretinoin for skin aging.

name: Retosiban
description: Acts at the oxytocin receptor to drive uterine contraction and milk ejection, or blocks it to suppress preterm labour; investigational antagonist.

name: Revaprazan
description: Inhibits the gastric proton pump to suppress acid secretion; long-term use affects micronutrient and mineral absorption; potassium-competitive, South Korea.

name: Rezafungin
description: Long-acting echinocandin dosed once weekly, engineered for stability by replacing the metabolically labile part of the anidulafungin scaffold.

name: Rezvilutamide
description: Rezvilutamide is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is androgen Receptor antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: RG108
description: A non-nucleoside DNMT inhibitor that blocks the enzyme's active site directly rather than being incorporated into DNA, so it demethylates without the covalent DNA adducts and cytotoxicity of the azanucleosides.

name: Rhodiola Rosea
description: Adaptogen with genuine randomised evidence for fatigue rather than for cognition -- the endpoint it moves is how tired the work feels, not how well it is done.

name: Ribavirin
description: Old broad-spectrum nucleoside with several proposed mechanisms, now mainly a hepatitis C adjunct and a treatment for viral haemorrhagic fever.

name: Ricolinostat (ACY-1215)
description: The first selective HDAC6 inhibitor to reach the clinic. Sparing the class I enzymes avoids the myelosuppression of the pan-inhibitors, which is what made combination with proteasome inhibitors in myeloma feasible.

name: Ridaforolimus
description: Ridaforolimus is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is serine/threonine-protein kinase mTOR inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Rifabutin
description: Rifamycin preferred over rifampicin in HIV coinfection because it induces CYP3A4 far less, at the cost of uveitis at higher doses.

name: Rifampicin
description: Antimycobacterial and the archetypal enzyme inducer — the reference case for PXR-mediated CYP3A4 induction.

name: Rifaximin
description: Minimally absorbed antibiotic used to prevent recurrent hepatic encephalopathy; antimicrobial stewardship still matters.

name: Rilonacept
description: IL-1 trap fusion protein used in periodic fever syndromes and recurrent pericarditis.

name: Rilpivirine
description: Inhibits HIV reverse transcriptase and is used only as part of a resistance-aware antiretroviral regimen.

name: Riluzole (Rilutek)
description: Benzothiazole antiglutamatergic agent; the first drug approved anywhere for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.

name: Rilzabrutinib
description: Inhibits BTK to interrupt B-cell receptor signalling; covalent and reversible agents differ in kinase selectivity, bleeding and atrial-fibrillation risk; reversible covalent.

name: Rimegepant (Nurtec ODT)
description: Small-molecule CGRP receptor antagonist (a gepant) approved for both acute treatment and prevention of migraine.

name: Rimexolone
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200617).

name: Rimiterol
description: Rimiterol is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Rimonabant
description: CB1 inverse agonist withdrawn worldwide after psychiatric adverse effects; the definitive cautionary case for central CB1 blockade in obesity.

name: Riociguat
description: Soluble guanylate cyclase positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2107834).
mechanism: Soluble guanylate cyclase positive allosteric modulator

name: Risankizumab
description: Neutralizes IL-23 signaling to suppress pathogenic Th17 maintenance in immune-mediated disease.

name: Risdiplam (Evrysdi)
description: An orally bioavailable small molecule that shifts SMN2 exon 7 inclusion. Being systemically distributed, it reaches peripheral tissues that intrathecal antisense therapy does not.

name: Risedronate
description: Bisphosphonate used to slow bone resorption and increase bone density.

name: Risperidone
description: Antagonizes or partially agonizes dopamine D2 receptors; movement, metabolic, and prolactin effects depend on receptor profile.

name: Ritlecitinib (oral, Litfulo)
description: Oral irreversible JAK3 and TEC-family kinase inhibitor approved for severe alopecia areata from age 12.

name: Ritodrine
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL83063).

name: Ritonavir
description: HIV protease inhibitor used almost entirely as a pharmacokinetic booster, exploiting its potent CYP3A4 inhibition.

name: Rituximab
description: The first therapeutic monoclonal antibody approved for cancer, now used far more widely in autoimmune disease. Depletes B cells for six to twelve months per cycle.

name: Rivaroxaban (Xarelto)
description: Oral factor Xa inhibitor with once-daily regimens for several indications; renal function, food requirements, and bleeding interactions matter.

name: Rivastigmine (Exelon)
description: Pseudo-irreversible dual inhibitor of acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase, available as a capsule and a transdermal patch.

name: Rivoglitazone
description: Rivoglitazone is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Rizatriptan
description: Fast-onset oral triptan available as an orally disintegrating wafer, with the shortest time to peak of the oral agents.

name: Robatumumab
description: Robatumumab is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is insulin-like growth factor I receptor antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.
mechanism: insulin-like growth factor I receptor antagonist

name: Robenacoxib
description: Robenacoxib is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is cyclooxygenase-2 inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Rocatinlimab
description: Rocatinlimab is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 4 antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.
mechanism: tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 4 antagonist

name: Rocuronium
description: Non-depolarising relaxant with an onset fast enough to replace suxamethonium for rapid sequence induction, especially now that sugammadex exists.

name: Rofecoxib
description: Cyclooxygenase-2 inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL122).

name: Roflumilast
description: Inhibits PDE4 to raise intracellular cAMP and dampen inflammatory cytokine production; emesis and weight loss are class-limiting.

name: Roflumilast Foam (Zoryve)
description: Topical PDE4 inhibitor for seborrheic dermatitis and plaque psoriasis, designed to reduce steroid-related skin toxicity.

name: Roflumilast (topical)
description: Topical PDE4 inhibitor for plaque psoriasis including intertriginous sites, where steroids are problematic.

name: Rolapitant
description: Long-acting NK-1 antagonist with a half-life of about seven days, covering the whole delayed emesis window from one dose.

name: Rolipram
description: Inhibits PDE4 to raise intracellular cAMP and dampen inflammatory cytokine production; emesis and weight loss are class-limiting; research tool compound, never marketed.

name: Romidepsin
description: Cyclic peptide HDAC inhibitor with class I selectivity; carries QT prolongation risk.

name: Romosozumab
description: Antibody that blocks sclerostin, both increasing bone formation and decreasing resorption.

name: Ropeginterferon Alfa-2B
description: Interferon alpha/beta receptor positive modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL4297819).

name: Ropinirole
description: D2-like dopamine receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL589).

name: Ropivacaine
description: Single-enantiomer long-acting local anaesthetic developed to reduce bupivacaine's cardiotoxicity while preserving duration.

name: Rosemary Oil
description: Botanical extract studied head-to-head against minoxidil for androgenetic hair loss.

name: Rosiglitazone
description: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL121).

name: Rosuvastatin (Crestor)
description: High-potency statin, effective at lowering LDL cholesterol and cardiovascular event risk even at low starting LDL levels.

name: Rotigotine
description: D2-like dopamine receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1303).

name: Roxadustat
description: HIF prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor raising endogenous erythropoietin for renal anaemia.

name: Roxatidine
description: Blocks parietal-cell H2 receptors to reduce stimulated gastric acid secretion.

name: RU58841
description: Topical antiandrogen abandoned in development and sold as a research chemical ever since.

name: Rufinamide
description: Reduces high-frequency neuronal firing through voltage-gated sodium-channel modulation.

name: Runcaciguat
description: sGC activator developed for chronic kidney disease and diabetic retinopathy rather than for blood pressure.

name: Rupatadine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL91397).

name: Ruxolitinib
description: Tyrosine-protein kinase JAK1 inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1789941).

name: Ruxolitinib cream 1.5% (Opzelura)
description: Topical JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor for atopic dermatitis and non-segmental vitiligo; the cream, not the oral myelofibrosis drug.

name: Ruxolitinib (topical)
description: Topical JAK1/2 inhibitor for atopic dermatitis and non-segmental vitiligo, the first drug to achieve repigmentation in vitiligo.

name: S-40503
description: SARM characterised specifically for bone rather than muscle; preclinical only.

name: S-23
description: Non-aromatizable SARM with high androgen receptor affinity, studied for both anabolic and male contraceptive effects.

name: Sacubitril
description: Neprilysin inhibitor, given with valsartan as ARNI therapy. Raises natriuretic peptides by blocking their degradation rather than supplying more — which is why it is combined with an ARB to offset the angiotensin II that also accumulates.

name: Sacubitril/Valsartan (Entresto)
description: Neprilysin inhibitor plus ARB; cannot be combined with an ACE inhibitor without risking angioedema.

name: Safinamide
description: Inhibits monoamine oxidase to raise synaptic monoamines; selectivity and reversibility determine tyramine and serotonin-syndrome risk.

name: Salbutamol (Albuterol)
description: Short-acting beta-2 agonist bronchodilator. High systemic doses can affect lean mass but carry tachycardia, tremor, hypokalaemia and cardiac-remodelling risk.

name: Salicylic Acid
description: Beta-hydroxy acid exfoliant used topically for acne and skin texture.

name: Salmeterol
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1263).

name: Salsalate
description: Non-acetylated salicylate that spares platelets and has been studied for insulin resistance via NF-kB inhibition.

name: Salvinorin A
description: Non-nitrogenous kappa agonist from Salvia divinorum — the most potent naturally occurring hallucinogen and pharmacologically unusual for lacking a basic nitrogen.

name: SAMe (S-adenosylmethionine)
description: The universal methyl donor for DNA and histone methyltransferases, sold as a supplement for depression and osteoarthritis. Supplying more donor is the opposite pharmacological lever from inhibiting the transferase that consumes it.

name: Samidorphan
description: Mu antagonist combined with olanzapine to blunt its weight gain.

name: Sapanisertib
description: Sapanisertib is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is serine/threonine-protein kinase mTOR inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Saquinavir
description: The first HIV protease inhibitor licensed, in 1995, and the drug that made combination antiretroviral therapy work. Poor bioavailability and QT effects retired it.

name: Saralasin
description: Type-1 angiotensin II receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL938).

name: Sarcosine (N-methylglycine)
description: An endogenous GlyT1 inhibitor sold as a supplement, raising synaptic glycine and enhancing NMDA co-agonist site occupancy. Small trials in schizophrenia negative symptoms are suggestive but underpowered.

name: Sarecycline (oral, Seysara)
description: Narrow-spectrum oral tetracycline designed specifically for acne, with reduced activity against enteric Gram-negatives.

name: Sarilumab
description: IL-6 receptor antibody for rheumatoid arthritis.

name: Saroglitazar
description: Dual PPAR-alpha and PPAR-gamma agonist licensed in India for diabetic dyslipidaemia and metabolic liver disease.

name: Satavaptan
description: Acts on vasopressin receptors to alter free-water handling or vascular tone; sodium shifts require monitoring; investigational, discontinued.

name: Satralizumab
description: Anti-IL-6-receptor antibody engineered for recycling, used in aquaporin-4-positive neuromyelitis optica.

name: Saw Palmetto
description: Popular herbal 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor for hair loss/BPH; a tissue biopsy study confirmed real DHT reduction in the prostate, though real-world clinical results have been more mixed and weaker than pharmaceutical options like finasteride.

name: Saxagliptin Anhydrous
description: Dipeptidyl peptidase IV inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL385517).

name: Saxagliptin
description: Inhibits DPP-4 to prolong endogenous incretin signaling and glucose-dependent insulin release.

name: Hyoscine (Scopolamine)
description: Tertiary antimuscarinic that crosses into the brain, used transdermally for motion sickness and historically as the standard amnesic model drug.

name: Scriptaid
description: Scriptaid is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC6. ChEMBL records Ki 0.25 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: Seclidemstat
description: A reversible, non-covalent LSD1 inhibitor that also disrupts LSD1's scaffolding interactions, studied in Ewing sarcoma where the fusion oncoprotein depends on LSD1 recruitment.

name: Secobarbital
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL447).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Secukinumab

description: The drug whose teratogenicity created modern drug regulation, later rehabilitated for erythema nodosum leprosum and myeloma.

name: Theacrine
description: A purine alkaloid structurally close to caffeine with similar adenosine antagonism, marketed on the claim that it does not produce the same tolerance. That claim is not well tested.

name: L-Theanine
description: An amino acid from tea, structurally close to glutamate. Used mainly to blunt the jitter and blood-pressure edge of caffeine while keeping the alertness; the pairing has better evidence than theanine alone.

name: Thenalidine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2105458).

name: Theobromine
description: The dominant methylxanthine in cocoa. Weaker adenosine antagonist than caffeine with a longer half-life and gentler subjective profile.

name: Theophylline
description: Methylxanthine acting as a non-selective PDE inhibitor and adenosine-receptor antagonist. Narrow therapeutic window — the reason it lost ground to inhaled therapy.

name: Thiamidol
description: Isobutylamido thiazolyl resorcinol, currently the most potent human tyrosinase inhibitor identified.

name: Thiamylal
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL440).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Thiopental
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL441).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Thioridazine
description: D2-like dopamine receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL479).

name: Thiothixene
description: High-potency thioxanthene antipsychotic, pharmacologically close to the high-potency phenothiazines.

name: Thymalin
description: Thymic peptide bioregulator studied (mainly in Russian/Eastern European literature) for immune restoration and slowing biomarkers of aging.

name: Thymogen (Glutamyl-Tryptophan)
description: Synthetic dipeptide immunomodulator registered in Russia; no Western approval.

name: Thymosin alpha-1
description: Thymic peptide immune modulator used clinically to boost T-cell response, most established in chronic hepatitis B.

name: Thyrotropin Alfa
description: Thyroid stimulating hormone receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201533).

name: Thyrotropin
description: Thyroid stimulating hormone receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201532).

name: Tiagabine
description: GABA reuptake inhibitor for focal epilepsy, notable for provoking non-convulsive status in patients without epilepsy.

name: Tianeptine
description: Prescribed as an atypical antidepressant in parts of Europe, and a full mu-opioid receptor agonist. Sold unregulated in the US as a supplement, where it produces opioid dependence and withdrawal.

name: Ticagrelor (Brilinta)
description: Reversible P2Y12 antiplatelet used after acute coronary syndromes; dyspnea, bradyarrhythmia, and bleeding are notable.

name: Ticlopidine
description: Inhibits platelet P2Y12 ADP signalling to reduce aggregation, at the cost of bleeding risk; largely superseded over neutropenia.

name: Tigatuzumab
description: Tigatuzumab is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 10B agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.
mechanism: tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 10B agonist

name: Tigecycline
description: Inhibits bacterial protein synthesis at the ribosome; spectrum, resistance, and toxicity are agent-specific.

name: Tildacerfont
description: Investigational CRF1 antagonist studied for ACTH and adrenal-androgen reduction in congenital adrenal hyperplasia.

name: Tildrakizumab
description: Neutralizes IL-23 signaling to suppress pathogenic Th17 maintenance in immune-mediated disease.

name: Tiludronate
description: Suppresses osteoclast-mediated bone resorption; jaw osteonecrosis and atypical femoral fracture are rare long-term class risks.

name: Timolol
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL499).

name: Tinzaparin
description: Low molecular weight heparin with a higher mean molecular weight than the others, so it retains more anti-thrombin activity.

name: Tioclomarol
description: Inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase so clotting factors are undercarboxylated; effect is delayed, diet-sensitive and needs INR monitoring.

name: Tioconazole
description: Topical imidazole formulated for single-dose vaginal candidiasis and for onychomycosis as a nail solution.

name: Tipranavir
description: Non-peptidic HIV protease inhibitor reserved for multidrug-resistant virus, carrying a hepatotoxicity and intracranial haemorrhage warning.

name: Tirabrutinib
description: Inhibits BTK to interrupt B-cell receptor signalling; covalent and reversible agents differ in kinase selectivity, bleeding and atrial-fibrillation risk; approved in Japan.

name: Tiratricol (TRIAC)
description: T3 metabolite with THR-beta preference, used in MCT8 deficiency and misused as an unapproved weight-loss agent.

name: Tirbanibulin
description: Topical microtubule inhibitor for actinic keratosis, applied for five days rather than the weeks that older field treatments need.

name: Tirofiban
description: Small-molecule GPIIb/IIIa antagonist given intravenously during percutaneous coronary intervention.

name: Mounjaro/Zepbound (Tirzepatide)
description: Dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist with stronger weight-loss effect than GLP-1-only drugs.

name: Tisopurine
description: Inhibits xanthine oxidoreductase to reduce urate production at its terminal synthetic step; also called thiopurinol.

name: Tobramycin
description: Aminoglycoside with better antipseudomonal potency than gentamicin, widely used inhaled in cystic fibrosis where systemic exposure stays low.

name: Tocilizumab
description: IL-6 receptor antibody used in rheumatoid arthritis, giant cell arteritis and cytokine release syndrome.

name: Tofacitinib
description: Janus Kinase (JAK) inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL221959).

name: Tofogliflozin Anhydrous
description: Sodium/glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2110731).

name: Tolazamide
description: Closes pancreatic beta-cell KATP channels to stimulate insulin release, with hypoglycemia as the central class risk.

name: Tolazoline
description: Histamine H1 receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL770).

name: Tolbutamide
description: Closes pancreatic beta-cell KATP channels to stimulate insulin release, with hypoglycemia as the central class risk.

name: Tolcapone
description: Brain-penetrant COMT inhibitor, and the cleanest tool for raising prefrontal dopamine specifically. Carries a black-box warning for fatal hepatotoxicity, which is why it is a research tool and not a nootropic.

name: Tolmetin
description: Cyclooxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1020).

name: Toloxatone
description: Inhibits monoamine oxidase to raise synaptic monoamines; selectivity and reversibility determine tyramine and serotonin-syndrome risk; reversible MAO-A inhibitor, France.

name: Tolrestat
description: Inhibits aldose reductase to limit polyol-pathway flux and the osmotic and oxidative stress it imposes during hyperglycaemia; withdrawn over hepatotoxicity.

name: Tolterodine
description: Antagonises muscarinic receptors; peripheral selectivity determines how much dry mouth, constipation and central anticholinergic burden an agent carries.

name: Tolvaptan
description: Acts on vasopressin receptors to alter free-water handling or vascular tone; sodium shifts require monitoring; V2 antagonist.

name: Topical Finasteride
description: Scalp finasteride formulation aiming to lower local DHT with less systemic exposure; serum DHT still falls to some degree.

name: Topical Spironolactone
description: Topical antiandrogen formulation investigated for acne and androgenetic hair loss, aiming to reduce systemic exposure; evidence and product quality vary.

name: Topiramate (Topamax)
description: Antiseizure drug that reduces appetite and weight, used alone off-label or with phentermine; cognitive slowing, kidney stones, and teratogenicity are key risks.

name: Topiroxostat
description: Inhibits xanthine oxidoreductase to reduce urate production at its terminal synthetic step; approved in Japan.

name: Torcetrapib
description: Abandoned CETP inhibitor that raised HDL but increased mortality through off-target blood-pressure and aldosterone effects.

name: Toremifene (Fareston)
description: Triphenylethylene SERM closely related to tamoxifen, used for estrogen-receptor-positive breast cancer and sometimes for on-cycle estrogen management.

name: Torsemide
description: Loop diuretic with more predictable oral absorption and a longer half-life than furosemide.

name: Tralokinumab (Adbry)
description: Anti-IL-13 monoclonal antibody for moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis; conjunctivitis is a notable adverse effect.

name: Tramadol
description: Weak opioid with substantial monoaminergic activity, marketed as low-risk and responsible for a great deal of serotonin syndrome and seizure.

name: Trandolapril
description: Blocks the renin–angiotensin system to reduce angiotensin-driven vasoconstriction or aldosterone signaling.

name: Tranexamic Acid
description: Originally an anti-bleeding medication, found to also treat melasma (oral or topical) through a distinct mechanism -- blocking plasmin-mediated melanocyte stimulation upstream of tyrosinase itself.

name: Tranylcypromine
description: Inhibits monoamine oxidase to raise synaptic monoamines; selectivity and reversibility determine tyramine and serotonin-syndrome risk; irreversible non-selective, requires tyramine restriction.

name: Trapoxin A
description: Trapoxin A is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC1. ChEMBL records EC50 820.0 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: Travoprost
description: Prostaglandin F2alpha analogue for glaucoma; the class also lengthens and darkens eyelashes.

name: Trazodone (Desyrel)
description: Serotonin antagonist and reuptake inhibitor, licensed as an antidepressant but overwhelmingly prescribed off-label at low doses for sleep.

name: Trelagliptin
description: Inhibits DPP-4 to prolong endogenous incretin signaling and glucose-dependent insulin release.

name: Tremelimumab
description: Anti-CTLA-4 antibody used in combination regimens in hepatocellular and lung cancer.

name: Tren (Trenbolone)
description: Potent 19-nor steroid with no aromatization; strong recomposition effect but notable cardiovascular/neuropsychiatric risk.

name: Treprostinil
description: Prostacyclin analogue stable enough for subcutaneous, inhaled and oral delivery, unlike epoprostenol.

name: Trestolone (MENT)
description: Experimental potent synthetic androgen resistant to 5-alpha-reduction, studied for male contraception/TRT; not FDA-approved, used mainly in research and by some biohackers/enhancement communities.

name: Tretinoin
description: Topical retinoic acid prescribed for photoaging and acne, the active metabolite of vitamin A.

name: Trevogrumab
description: Anti-myostatin antibody studied for muscle preservation, including combination senolytic strategies.

name: Triamcinolone Acetonide
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1504).

name: Triamcinolone
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1451).

name: Triamcinolone Diacetate
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200449).

name: Triamcinolone Hexacetonide
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1200878).

name: Triamterene
description: Potassium-sparing ENaC blocker used with thiazides; hyperkalemia is the central interaction risk.

name: Triazolam
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL646).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator

name: Tribulus Terrestris
description: Popular test-boosting herbal supplement; human trial evidence for a real hormonal effect is weak and mixed compared to better-supported options like boron or zinc.

name: Tributyrin
description: A triglyceride prodrug of butyrate that survives gastric passage and releases butyrate on lipase hydrolysis, solving the minutes-long half-life and unpleasant odour that make sodium butyrate itself impractical.

name: Trichostatin A
description: The original natural-product hydroxamate pan-HDAC inhibitor from Streptomyces and the reference compound almost the entire field was built on. Too toxic for clinical use; vorinostat is its synthetic descendant.

name: Triciferol
description: Triciferol is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC6. ChEMBL records IC50 580.0 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: Triclofos
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1201317).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive modulator

name: Trientine
description: Second-line copper chelator for Wilson disease, better tolerated than penicillamine with fewer autoimmune effects.

name: Trifarotene (topical, Aklief)
description: Fourth-generation topical retinoid selective for RAR-gamma, approved for facial and truncal acne.

name: Trifluoperazine
description: D2-like dopamine receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL422).

name: Trimebutine
description: Peripheral opioid receptor modulator used for irritable bowel syndrome, normalising motility in either direction.

name: Trimetazidine
description: Metabolic antianginal that shifts myocardial fuel use; prohibited in sport and associated with movement disorders.

name: Trimethoprim
description: Bacterial dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor used alone for urinary infection and with sulfamethoxazole for broader cover.

name: Trimipramine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL644).

name: Tripelennamine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1241).

name: Triprolidine
description: Histamine H1 receptor antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL855).

name: Triptorelin Acetate
description: Triptorelin Acetate is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Triptorelin (Trelstar)
description: GnRH agonist; a flare then profound suppression, which is why it is used both ways.

name: Troglitazone
description: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL408).

name: Tropicamide
description: The shortest-acting antimuscarinic mydriatic, standard for fundus examination.

name: Tropifexor
description: Potent non-steroidal FXR agonist investigated in MASH.

name: Tropisetron
description: Prescription 5-HT3 receptor antagonist used for nausea and vomiting. Cognitive interest centers on alpha-7 nicotinic receptor activity, but it is not an established nootropic.

name: Trospium
description: Antagonises muscarinic receptors; peripheral selectivity determines how much dry mouth, constipation and central anticholinergic burden an agent carries; quaternary, poor CNS penetration.

name: Troxerutin
description: Hydroxyethylrutoside venotonic used in some countries for chronic venous insufficiency.

name: Trv-120027
description: Trv-120027 is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is type-1 angiotensin II receptor antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Tubacin
description: Tubacin is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC6. ChEMBL records IC50 13.0 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: Tubastatin A
description: The standard research tool for selective HDAC6 inhibition, with roughly a thousand-fold selectivity over HDAC1. Widely used to show that a given effect is cytoplasmic and tubulin-dependent rather than transcriptional.

name: Tucidinostat (chidamide)
description: An orally available benzamide HDAC inhibitor selective for class I plus HDAC10, approved in China for peripheral T-cell lymphoma and, unusually for this class, for hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer alongside endocrine therapy.

name: TUDCA (Tauroursodeoxycholic Acid)
description: Bile acid supplement studied for liver protection and reducing endoplasmic reticulum stress; commonly used to offset hepatotoxicity from oral 17-alpha-alkylated steroids.

name: Tulobuterol
description: Tulobuterol is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Turinabol (Chlorodehydromethyltestosterone)
description: Oral steroid derived from Dianabol with reduced aromatization, historically used in state-sponsored doping programs.

name: Turkesterone
description: Phytoecdysteroid supplement promoted as anabolic; direct human efficacy, pharmacokinetics, and product-content evidence are notably sparse.

name: TYRA-300 (Dabogratinib)
description: Investigational FGFR3-selective inhibitor designed to avoid the hyperphosphatemia that dose-limits pan-FGFR drugs; animal growth data only.

name: Tzp-102
description: Tzp-102 is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is ghrelin receptor agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Ubrogepant
description: Blocks CGRP ligand or receptor signalling in the trigeminovascular system for migraine prevention or acute treatment; oral small-molecule gepant.

name: UBX0101
description: MDM2/p53 interaction inhibitor developed as a senolytic for osteoarthritis; failed its phase 2 knee trial.

name: Udenafil
description: Inhibits PDE5 so nitric-oxide/cGMP vasodilation persists in corporal and pulmonary vascular smooth muscle; approved in South Korea.

name: Ularitide (Urodilatin)
description: Synthetic urodilatin, the kidney-derived ANP variant. Failed to improve long-term outcomes in the TRUE-AHF trial despite favourable haemodynamics.

name: Ulimorelin
description: Intravenous ghrelin-receptor agonist studied for postoperative ileus; not an approved performance compound.

name: Ulipristal Acetate
description: Progesterone receptor modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL260538).

name: Ulipristal
description: Progesterone receptor modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2103846).

name: Ulotaront
description: TAAR1 agonist investigated as a non-D2 antipsychotic; phase 3 results were disappointing.

name: Undecylenic Acid
description: Fatty acid antifungal available over the counter for tinea pedis, one of the oldest topical antifungals still marketed.

name: Upadacitinib (Rinvoq)
description: Oral JAK1 inhibitor for multiple inflammatory diseases with boxed warnings for infection, malignancy, thrombosis, and cardiovascular events.

name: Urapidil
description: Blocks alpha-1 adrenoceptors to relax vascular or prostatic smooth muscle; first-dose hypotension and floppy-iris syndrome are class effects; also a 5-HT1A agonist, Europe.

name: Urea (topical, 5% to 40%)
description: Humectant and keratolytic depending on concentration; a natural moisturising factor component, not an inert base.

name: Urelumab
description: Urelumab is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 9 agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.
mechanism: tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 9 agonist

name: Uridine Monophosphate
description: Substrate for the Kennedy pathway of membrane phosphatide synthesis. Studied as one leg of a three-nutrient combination in Alzheimer's rather than on its own.

name: Urofollitropin (Bravelle/Fostimon)
description: Highly purified FSH extracted from postmenopausal urine, with the LH activity stripped out.

name: Urokinase
description: Direct plasminogen activator, not fibrin-selective.

name: Urolithin A
description: Gut-metabolite compound studied for improving mitochondrial quality control (mitophagy) in aging muscle.

name: Ursodeoxycholic Acid (UDCA)
description: The prescription bile acid TUDCA is conjugated from; first-line for primary biliary cholangitis.

name: Ursolic Acid
description: Pentacyclic triterpenoid investigated for muscle, adiposity, and metabolic effects; most anabolic claims remain preclinical.

name: Ustekinumab
description: Neutralizes IL-23 signaling to suppress pathogenic Th17 maintenance in immune-mediated disease.

name: Vaborbactam
description: Cyclic boronate beta-lactamase inhibitor paired with meropenem, targeted specifically at KPC carbapenemases.

name: Vadadustat
description: HIF-PHI whose approval history differs sharply between regions over cardiovascular safety.

name: Valaciclovir
description: L-valyl ester prodrug of aciclovir with three to five times the oral bioavailability, achieved by hijacking an intestinal peptide transporter.

name: Valbenazine
description: Selective VMAT2 inhibitor developed specifically for tardive dyskinesia, dosed once daily with less off-target activity.

name: Valdecoxib
description: Cyclooxygenase-2 inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL865).

name: Valganciclovir
description: Valyl ester prodrug of ganciclovir that made oral CMV prophylaxis after transplantation practical.

name: Sodium Valproate
description: Broad-spectrum anticonvulsant and mood stabiliser with multiple mechanisms and the most serious teratogenic profile of the class.

name: Valsartan (Diovan)
description: Widely used ARB with heart failure and post-infarction indications alongside hypertension.

name: Vamorolone
description: Glucocorticoid receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL2348780).

name: Vancomycin
description: Glycopeptide binding the cell wall substrate rather than the enzyme, and the historical standard for MRSA. Requires level monitoring because efficacy and nephrotoxicity both track exposure.

name: Vapreotide
description: Vapreotide is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is somatostatin receptor 2 agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Vardenafil (Levitra)
description: PDE5 inhibitor structurally close to sildenafil, with more QT prolongation attached.

name: Vasopressin (IV)
description: Second-line vasopressor in septic shock, acting on a receptor system entirely separate from the adrenergic one.

name: Vecuronium
description: Intermediate-acting steroidal relaxant with minimal cardiovascular effect, whose active metabolite accumulates in renal failure.

name: Vedaprofen
description: Vedaprofen is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is cyclooxygenase-1 inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Vedolizumab
description: Gut-selective anti-alpha-4-beta-7 antibody for inflammatory bowel disease, whose selectivity is the reason it carries no PML signal.

name: Veliflapon
description: Veliflapon is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is 5-lipoxygenase activating protein inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Veligrotug
description: Veligrotug is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is insulin-like growth factor I receptor antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.
mechanism: insulin-like growth factor I receptor antagonist

name: Velpatasvir
description: Blocks an HCV replication target and is combined with complementary direct-acting antivirals to prevent resistance.

name: Velsecorat
description: Velsecorat is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is glucocorticoid receptor modulator; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Venetoclax
description: Selective BCL-2 inhibitor; the first clinically successful BH3 mimetic. Tumour lysis risk requires ramp-up dosing.

name: Venlafaxine (Effexor)
description: SNRI with dose-related blood-pressure effects and a prominent discontinuation syndrome.

name: Verapamil
description: The most cardiac-selective calcium channel blocker; constipation is the near-universal complaint.

name: Vericiguat (Verquvo)
description: Oral soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator for heart failure after a worsening event.

name: Verinurad
description: Blocks proximal-tubule urate reabsorption to raise fractional urate excretion; urine volume and stone risk need attention; investigational.

name: Vernakalant
description: Alters cardiac repolarization through potassium-channel effects; QT prolongation and torsades risk vary by agent.

name: Vesugen (Lys-Glu-Asp)
description: Synthetic Lys-Glu-Asp tripeptide marketed as a vascular bioregulator. The literature is small and regionally concentrated, with limited controlled human evidence.

name: Vigabatrin
description: Irreversible GABA transaminase inhibitor, uniquely effective in infantile spasms and causing permanent visual field loss in a third of patients.

name: Vilanterol
description: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL1198857).

name: Vilazodone
description: Inhibits serotonin reuptake through SERT; benefits, activation, sexual effects, and withdrawal profiles differ by agent.

name: Vildagliptin
description: Inhibits DPP-4 to prolong endogenous incretin signaling and glucose-dependent insulin release.

name: Vilon (Lys-Glu)
description: Synthetic Lys-Glu dipeptide studied mainly in thymocyte and cell-culture experiments. Human clinical efficacy and long-term safety are not established.

name: Viloxazine
description: Inhibits norepinephrine reuptake, often alongside serotonin effects; blood pressure and discontinuation effects require attention.

name: Vinpocetine
description: Semi-synthetic vincamine derivative acting as a cerebral vasodilator and PDE1 inhibitor. Banned from supplements in several jurisdictions over developmental toxicity concerns.

name: VIP (Vasoactive Intestinal Peptide)
description: Endogenous 28-amino-acid neuropeptide with vasodilatory and immunomodulatory activity.

name: Vistusertib
description: Vistusertib is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is serine/threonine-protein kinase mTOR inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid)
description: Essential cofactor for the enzymes that hydroxylate collagen during synthesis; a classic mechanistic study found it directly induces procollagen gene expression in skin fibroblasts.

name: Vitamin D
description: Fat-soluble prohormone supplemented for bone mineralization and broader musculoskeletal health.

name: Vitamin E
description: Lipid-soluble antioxidant used topically, often paired with vitamin C, to protect skin from oxidative photoaging.

name: Vitamin K2
description: Fat-soluble vitamin that activates osteocalcin via carboxylation, the step required for osteocalcin to bind bone mineral; studied for bone density support.

name: VK2809
description: Liver-targeted THR-beta agonist prodrug investigated for MASH and dyslipidaemia.

name: Voclosporin
description: Structurally modified cyclosporine with more predictable pharmacokinetics, approved for lupus nephritis.

name: Vodobatinib
description: Inhibits BCR–ABL-family kinase signaling; mutation coverage and off-target cardiovascular risks differ by agent.

name: Voglibose
description: A potent alpha-glucosidase inhibitor used mainly in Japan, with greater selectivity for disaccharidases than acarbose and correspondingly less colonic fermentation.

name: Volanesorsen (Waylivra)
description: First-generation APOC3 antisense drug, approved in Europe only and constrained by thrombocytopenia.

name: Vonoprazan
description: Inhibits the gastric proton pump to suppress acid secretion; long-term use affects micronutrient and mineral absorption; potassium-competitive acid blocker.

name: Vorapaxar
description: PAR-1 antiplatelet drug with a very long effect; contraindicated after stroke because of intracranial bleeding risk.

name: Voriconazole
description: Disrupts fungal ergosterol synthesis or membrane function; interaction and organ-toxicity profiles differ substantially.

name: Vorinostat
description: First approved HDAC inhibitor, for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

name: Vortioxetine
description: Inhibits serotonin reuptake through SERT; benefits, activation, sexual effects, and withdrawal profiles differ by agent.

name: Vosilasarm (RAD140)
description: Clinical development name for RAD140 in breast cancer; included separately to prevent users mistaking oncology trials for performance-use evidence.

name: Voxzogo (Vosoritide)
description: Daily injectable CNP analogue, the first approved drug to increase height in achondroplasia; antagonises MAPK downstream of FGFR3 rather than the receptor itself.

name: Voxelotor (Oxbryta)
description: A haemoglobin oxygen-affinity modulator that stabilises the R state so less HbS is available to polymerise. Withdrawn in 2024 after post-marketing data suggested harm, a cautionary case for haemoglobin surrogate endpoints.

name: Voxilaprevir
description: Blocks an HCV replication target and is combined with complementary direct-acting antivirals to prevent resistance.

name: Vunakizumab
description: Blocks IL-17 ligand or receptor signaling to reduce neutrophil-dominant inflammation.

name: Vupanorsen
description: Vupanorsen is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is angiopoietin like 3 (ANGPTL3) mRNA antisense inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Vutrisiran (Amvuttra)
description: A GalNAc-conjugated siRNA against transthyretin given subcutaneously every three months, replacing patisiran's infusions and premedication with a far simpler regimen.

name: Warfarin (Coumadin)
description: Vitamin K antagonist anticoagulant with a narrow therapeutic window, extensive food/drug interactions, and INR monitoring requirements.

name: WR301839
description: WR301839 is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC6. ChEMBL records IC50 3.0 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: WR301849
description: WR301849 is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC6. ChEMBL records IC50 2.54 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: WR301858
description: WR301858 is a named HDAC research compound with a curated biochemical result against HDAC3. ChEMBL records IC50 25.0 nM in the selected assay; that describes target potency, not a proven clinical benefit.

name: Xanomeline
description: An M1/M4-preferring muscarinic agonist that produces antipsychotic effects without touching dopamine D2, the first genuinely new antipsychotic mechanism in decades. Paired with trospium to block its peripheral cholinergic effects.

name: Xentuzumab
description: Xentuzumab is a phase 2 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is insulin-like growth factor I inhibitor; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Ximelagatran
description: Thrombin inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL522038).

name: Xipamide
description: Thiazide-like diuretic retaining efficacy at lower glomerular filtration rates than most thiazides.

name: YK-11
description: Myostatin-inhibiting steroidal SARM studied for muscle growth beyond typical androgen receptor activation.

name: Yohimbine
description: Alpha-2 adrenergic receptor antagonist that removes a natural brake on fat-cell lipolysis, indirectly potentiating adrenaline's fat-mobilizing effect rather than acting as a stimulant itself.

name: Zafirlukast
description: Cysteinyl leukotriene receptor 1 antagonist; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL603).

name: Zaleplon (Sonata)
description: Very short-acting GABA-A hypnotic for sleep-onset insomnia; dependence and complex sleep behaviors remain possible.

name: Zanamivir
description: Inhaled neuraminidase inhibitor with negligible oral bioavailability, delivered straight to the airway epithelium instead.

name: Zanubrutinib
description: Inhibits BTK to interrupt B-cell receptor signalling; covalent and reversible agents differ in kinase selectivity, bleeding and atrial-fibrillation risk; second-generation covalent.

name: Zaprinast
description: Inhibits PDE5 so nitric-oxide/cGMP vasodilation persists in corporal and pulmonary vascular smooth muscle; research tool compound, never marketed.

name: Zatolmilast (BPN14770)
description: PDE4D-selective inhibitor investigated for Fragile X syndrome. Subtype selectivity is the attempt to keep the cognitive benefit without the emesis that comes with pan-PDE4 blockade.

name: Zavegepant
description: Blocks CGRP ligand or receptor signalling in the trigeminovascular system for migraine prevention or acute treatment; intranasal gepant.

name: Zebularine
description: A chemically stable cytidine analogue DNMT inhibitor with oral activity and much lower toxicity than azacitidine, used mainly as a research tool because the doses needed for demethylation in vivo are very high.

name: Zenarestat
description: Inhibits aldose reductase to limit polyol-pathway flux and the osmotic and oxidative stress it imposes during hyperglycaemia; development discontinued.

name: Zibotentan
description: Zibotentan is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is endothelin receptor ET-A antagonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Zidovudine
description: Inhibits HIV reverse transcriptase and is used only as part of a resistance-aware antiretroviral regimen.

name: Zileuton
description: Arachidonate 5-lipoxygenase inhibitor; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL93).

name: Zilpaterol
description: Beta-2 agonist feed additive for cattle. Appears in human and equine anti-doping casework through feed contamination rather than intentional use.

name: Ziltivekimab
description: Monoclonal antibody against the interleukin-6 ligand, developed specifically for residual inflammatory cardiovascular risk.

name: Zilucoplan
description: Inhibits a step of the complement cascade; blocking terminal complement raises encapsulated-organism risk and requires meningococcal vaccination; macrocyclic peptide C5 inhibitor.

name: Zimelidine
description: Inhibits serotonin reuptake through SERT; benefits, activation, sexual effects, and withdrawal profiles differ by agent.

name: Zinc
description: Essential trace mineral required for normal androgen synthesis; deficiency lowers testosterone, though supplementing beyond adequate status has weaker evidence.

name: Zinc Oxide
description: Inorganic broad-spectrum UV filter that works by absorption and scattering, and the reference agent for sensitive and paediatric skin.

name: Ziprasidone
description: Antagonizes or partially agonizes dopamine D2 receptors; movement, metabolic, and prolactin effects depend on receptor profile.

name: Zodasiran
description: Investigational RNA interference therapy targeting ANGPTL3 for atherogenic lipid reduction.

name: Zofenopril
description: Blocks the renin–angiotensin system to reduce angiotensin-driven vasoconstriction or aldosterone signaling.

name: Zoledronic Acid
description: Suppresses osteoclast-mediated bone resorption; jaw osteonecrosis and atypical femoral fracture are rare long-term class risks.

name: Zoledronic Acid (Reclast)
description: Potent IV nitrogen-containing bisphosphonate given as an annual infusion, used for osteoporosis and cancer-related bone disease.

name: Zolmitriptan
description: Triptan available orally and as a nasal spray, with an active metabolite that prolongs its effect.

name: Zolpidem (Ambien)
description: Nonbenzodiazepine GABA-A hypnotic with next-day impairment, dependence, and boxed-warning complex sleep behaviors.

name: Zonisamide
description: Inhibits carbonic anhydrase, lowering bicarbonate-dependent fluid secretion; metabolic acidosis and paraesthesia are the usual class effects; weak carbonic anhydrase activity alongside sodium-channel block.

name: Zopiclone
description: GABA-A receptor; agonist GABA site positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL135400).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; agonist GABA site positive allosteric modulator

name: Zopolrestat
description: Inhibits aldose reductase to limit polyol-pathway flux and the osmotic and oxidative stress it imposes during hyperglycaemia; development discontinued.

name: Zoptarelin Doxorubicin
description: Zoptarelin Doxorubicin is a phase 3 compound catalogued by ChEMBL. Its curated mechanism is gonadotropin-releasing hormone receptor agonist; the pathway link is mechanistic and does not by itself establish benefit, safety, or an appropriate use.

name: Zuclopenthixol
description: Thioxanthene available as an acetate for rapid tranquillisation and as a decanoate for maintenance, widely used in acute psychiatry.

name: Zuranolone
description: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator; approved/marketed compound catalogued by ChEMBL (CHEMBL4105630).
mechanism: GABA-A receptor; anion channel positive allosteric modulator
